quotes.race: Lexus Melbourne Cup (Group 1 Handicap) (3yo+) (Turf)
quotes.quote: I've had an amazing year, having got married and had some brilliant days on the track, but nothing ever compares to this feeling right now. I wanted to ride Half Yours as quiet as I could but at the two-furlong pole I couldn't go any quieter. I had to let him go. This horse was so fit and strong, he went through a tight gap and then an extremely tight gap, but I had no say - he just took me through. You grow up thinking you want to ride in the Melbourne Cup, but you never actually think you might win it. You don't think it will happen . . . but it's just happened. Tony and Calvin [joint-trainers] have been incredible supporters of mine and have been there for me since I was a 15-year-old kid. They have done an amazing job and deserve this so much - Jamie Melham, jockey.

quotes.race: Sportsbet Caulfield Cup (Group 1 Handicap) (3yo+) (Turf)
quotes.quote: This is why we do it, to have a runner in this, but they're very hard to win. That was incredible. Half Yours has come along way in six months and travelling really grows horses up. He was a big, raw horse and we took him to Queensland, and it's been the making of him. It's very important and what a proud moment it's been for me to do it with Calvin, it's really enjoyable - Tony McEvoy, joint-trainer.

runners.spotlight: Got back when beat tired horses home this track. Better draw here. A distance specialist. Worth a look.

quotes.race: Juddmonte Royal Lodge Stakes (Group 2) (Colts & Geldings)
quotes.quote: Jason (Hart) said Royal Patronage was a bit free early on and he was trying to settle him and no sooner was he getting him under control than the race was on again. He said when he hit the rising ground he found another gear. He has got a lot of speed. We almost supplemented him for the Champagne Stakes. He is out of a Dalakhani mare so there is lots of stamina on the dam's side. It is great that you have a horse you think will stay a mile and a half that has so much speed early on - Mark Johnston, trainer.

quotes.race: Tattersalls Acomb Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.quote: Royal Patronage was the most exposed horse in the race but we brought him here to the Dante meeting, which shows we thought very, very highly of him at that stage. He was beaten over six furlongs first time out, ran well second time at Sandown and then showed us what we always thought of him at Epsom. We'll go home and think about targets. On pedigree the horse will clearly stay further. I was asked whether he's a Guineas horse, it may be he's more a Dante horse but time will tell - Mark Johnston, trainer.

runners.comment: Pulled up mid-race in the Topham but this is a lower grade than he's used to contesting
runners.spotlight: Something to prove regarding current form although he didn't take to the National fences when pulled up mid-race in the Topham at Aintree last week; this is a lower grade than he's used to contesting and he's capable of playing a big role if back on song now returned to conventional fences.

quotes.race: Betfair Exchange Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Matata is a very talented horse and was crying out for this trip - Willy Twiston-Davies, joint-trainer.

quotes.race: William Hill Best Odds Guaranteed Game Spirit Chase (Grade 2) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Matata will go for the Champion Chase. He ran his heart out at Windsor and this probably came a little too soon. We've got just over four weeks till the next one and it's onwards and upwards - Nigel Twiston-Davies, trainer.

quotes.race: Fitzdares Great Park Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Matata is very keen but he jumps well. I think there were a lot of excuses for the ones behind, I'm not saying that for the handicapper, but he doesn't suddenly become twenty pounds better than he's been before. We'll discuss options [regarding the Champion Chase] with the owners but the other idea is that he could go for the two and a half mile race [Melling Chase] at Aintree - Nigel Twiston-Davies, trainer.

quotes.race: Three Counties Christmas Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Matat is a very talented horse on his day and he's calming down with age. I think two and a half miles on good ground could be key. He has to go left-handed so that limits our options but we'll let the dust settle - Nigel Twiston-Davies, trainer.

quotes.race: Download The BetVictor App Novices' Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Matata is a long way from the finished article and he's just a baby. He needs to learn to do things properly and has to go left-handed. Daryl Jacob, jockey

runners.comment: Two wins last autumn and mid-division in the Grand Annual last time; this isn't as hot
runners.spotlight: Soundly beaten in the Grand Annual at Cheltenham (2m, good) last month but didn't run badly in 11th and this race isn't as hot; this 10yo showed career-best form earlier in the season with two high-profile wins (2m/2m1f, good to soft) and it will be no surprise if he's in the shake-up.

quotes.race: squareintheair.com Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: At nine years old Calico probably shouldn't be putting up a career best, but he just has. He is a great horse to train for this race, and we made sure we had him right for this. The ground was perfect for him today and it's a big race in his season because he finds it harder to win once the ground softens. Today was important - I think only think only the Grand Annual is worth more - Dan Skelton, trainer.

quotes.race: squareintheair.com Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Calico just got chinned at The November Meeting last year when Triple Trade beat him and I said to John [Reilly] his owner that we might not win for the rest of the year now because I knew how much he'd put in. It has literally taken him a season to get over that run, not just because of that run but also because the handicapper put him up and the opposition got stronger. It was important today that he was fresh and it was nice ground on a track he is good at. Harry gave him a beautiful ride and it all came together. I think we will have to be sparing with him as he is very good fresh and on decent ground. I think we will probably look at the Desert Orchid Chase at Kempton over Christmas for him now, as that is now a limited handicap - Dan Skelton, trainer.

quotes.race: Virgin Bet Cheltenham Festival Money Back Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We came very close up the run-in and I was unable to use my stick as I wanted to and Calico responded really well just for hands and heels. I was surprised he battled back like he did and I felt like he was crying out for a lead turning away from the stands. He sees this trip out really well, but has that speed early to get him to the front. Bridget Andrews, jockey

quotes.race: MansionBet Faller Insurance Novices' Hurdle (Novices' Championship Hdl Qual') (GBB Race) (Div II)
quotes.quote: Calico was a nice horse in Germany and was entitled to win like he did. He was just denied in a strong race at Kempton and has a nice turn of foot - Harry Skelton, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: He won two good handicaps in the autumn and ran well enough in the Game Spirit on ground that he wouldn't have liked, but the Champion Chase looks too big an ask and we may well claim off him in the Grand Annual instead. 17-02-26

runners.comment: Runner-up in this race two years ago and in good heart this term; could have part to play
runners.spotlight: Running well in the main this season, winning at Wetherby (1m7f, soft) in December and good third at Musselburgh (2m4f, good to soft) in January last time; this two-time course winner was runner-up in this race two years ago and could again have a part to play.

quotes.race: William Hill Castleford Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Traprain Law has well  deserved that, he went to all the big days last season and the ground never went soft enough. He really likes it when it goes soft. This year he came out a lot stronger, a lot better and a lot more experienced. He's run some nice races and we really did think he'd run well today. He's done a lot for a seven-year-old and he's just starting to get to grips with things. He jumps a lot better now than he used to and hopefully we can keep going forward with him now - Patrick Wadge, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: He loves it soft, so we were pleased with his Cheltenham run. He'll be going for two-mile handicap chases and we'll be praying for rain, he could be well handicapped. 29-10-25

Two miles on soft to heavy ground is his ideal and this season he has won twice at Kelso on very deep ground, including last time from a nice newcomer [Galunggung]. There'll be more opportunities over hurdles but I can't wait to get him chasing. Keep an eye out for him while the ground is riding soft or heavy. 25-01-23

runners.comment: Ran well in his favourite Aintree race recently and he can make another bold bid
runners.spotlight: Front-runner who was 11l third of 15 at Aintree (2m, good to soft) nine days ago when bidding to win that race for the third consecutive year (wins on soft/good); his last five wins have come in the month of April and there can be optimism that he will make another bold bid; third in this in 2024.

quotes.race: Close Brothers Red Rum Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Sans Bruit is a tough, genuine little horse and I'm proud of him. He's run really well but he didn't get a soft lead this time because they know how to beat him. He loves this time of year and he'll probably go to Ayr next Saturday for the valuable 2m handicap - Paul Nicholls, trainer.

quotes.race: BetGoodwin Sussex Champion Chase Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I need to thank Harry [Cobden, jockey] because he's a big part of the team and he stood with Matterhorn because I knew we wanted to claim off Sans Bruit after he went up 9lb for Aintree. I was a bit worried it came too soon after Aintree but his owner Andy Peake was the one who keen to run today, and Jay took that handy 5lb off and rode him very well considering it's his first time on board. He was given a beautiful lead by Westport Cove today and he's only little, but he's a smashing jumper - Paul Nicholls, trainer.

quotes.race: Close Brothers Red Rum Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Sans Bruit ran very well on good ground earlier in the season, but in the winter he hated that heavy ground. When he ran at Windsor, Cobby [Harry Cobden, jockey] said, 'we'll just get him right in the spring and he'll take all the beating in this race', and that's what we've done. He managed to run off with Freddie [Gingell] the other day at Chepstow, but the biggest thing is that he looks amazing now, this is his time of year, he's come in his coat in his sunshine, he's relaxed and we had him really, really right - Paul Nicholls, trainer.

quotes.race: Close Brothers Red Rum Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Last time was a sign of Sans Bruit coming to himself and he had been too keen in the first couple of races here. He took a long time to acclimatise to racing in this country. He's just coming right now and could even go to Ayr and Sandown. I wouldn't be afraid to put him in the Celebration Chase - Paul Nicholls, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: Our 2024 Red Rum Chase winner completely lost his form in the early part of last season, with the result his handicap mark fell quickly, so by the time he went back to Aintree in the spring to try and repeat his Red Rum success he was on the same mark as 12 months earlier. And he became the first horse in 40 years to land back-to-back victories in the valuable two-miler. We took a bit of a gamble bringing him out again a fortnight later when, off a 9lb higher mark minus the excellent Jay Tidball's 5lb claim, he followed up in Plumpton's most valuable-ever chase. His run at Ascot on Saturday told us things aren't going to be easy from now on off a career-high mark. He was fit enough, as he'd absolutely flown when we took him off for an away-day gallop several days ago, but he might have to wait a bit now before he sees the winner's enclosure again as normally he takes a few runs to hit peak form; for some reason he doesn't like the cold and the wet in mid-winter and is always a better horse in the spring, when everything will be geared towards attempting a Red Rum hat-trick. 04-11-25

prev_owners.owner: Simon Munir, Haras De Saint-Voir & Isaac Souede

runners.comment: 2-4 over fences in France; acquired for 320,000euros; Irish stable won this race last year
runners.spotlight: 2-4 over fences in France, the wins coming last autumn (2m1f, very soft/heavy); changed hands for 320,000euros in November; her top Irish trainer won this race last year and this lightly raced 5yo is one to be interested in on her stable debut, especially if strong in the betting.

runners.breeder: E A R L Haras De La Croix Sonnet Et Al
runners.comment: He's had his ups and downs but made it 2-5 over fences when winning at Newbury latest
runners.spotlight: He's had his ups and downs in a short chasing career and his jumping can lack fluency but he made it 2-5 in this sphere when making virtually all to win at Newbury (2m, good to soft) four weeks ago; won on soft ground over hurdles; major player if things click again today.

quotes.race: Century Racing Club Free Horse Giveaway Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race) (Div II)
quotes.quote: Palacio is a big, rangy sort and in time he'll learn to race and be even nicer. He can be a tricky horse at home and the team have done a great job with him - Dylan Johnston, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: It's probably taken a bit of time to work him out, but he has lots of ability and he'll go for the Fulke Walwyn Trophy at Newbury on Friday. If we can keep him in one piece he could be the type for a Grand Annual later in the season. He's always been a big brute of a horse, but as time's gone by he's starting to relax. 23-11-25

He's taken a lot of time to come to himself. He travelled strongly at Exeter on his debut at Exeter in November but then stopped a bit quickly. He's had a wind operation and hopefully we can get him to show us what he can do next time. He'll be out in the next few weeks. 05-01-24

runners.comment: In good form in Irish handicaps on his last two starts and he's entitled to respect
runners.spotlight: 7yo who showed improvement to win a handicap chase at Navan (2m1f, soft to heavy) last month and again ran well when 10l second of 12 at Fairyhouse (2m, soft) a fortnight ago behind a well-backed winner; 2lb wrong at the weights today but this Irish challenger could have more to offer and is respected.

quotes.race: Kilberry Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: The young man [Eoghan Finegan, jockey] did a lovely job and I'm very pleased with the ride he gave him. Moudan hit the line well and he handles that ground well. He jumped adequately and he's still going to improve in that department. He's a late developer and is doing very little wrong which is lovely - Ciaran Murphy, trainer.

quotes.race: O'Kelly Brothers Demolition Rated Novice Chase
quotes.quote: Moudan is improving the whole time. Obviously, it mightn't have gone to plan the first couple of days, but we don't mind now. He wasn't doing a whole lot the whole way. When they came to me, he started to wake up and concentrate on his job and he was good when I needed him at the last - Eoin Walsh, jockey.

prev_owners.owner: F W Healy & Ms Margaret Mullins

runners.comment: 3lb out of the handicap but some good form this season, including here, and not ruled out
runners.spotlight: Good second to progressive novice in handicap at Sandown (1m7f, soft) in January and ran well when 14l third here (2m4f, soft) last month, when weakening late on; 3lb out of the handicap today but not ruled out now back down in trip with a visor replacing cheekpieces; best form on soft/heavy.

quotes.race: Betfred 'Classic Bookmaker' Beginners' Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: On form, Classic Maestro should have done that. It's a shame only two turned up, but his jumping was foot-perfect. He's kept improving and there should be more to come. We'll freshen him up for a couple of weeks, but he loves heavy ground and we'll have to make use of that. He should get further and can step up to two and a half miles - Alan O'Keeffe, assistant trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He was pulled up in the Ascot Chase last time. Before that he was second at Sandown in January behind Lucy Wadham's Jax Junior, who then won the Grade 2 Pendil. He has an entry at Cheltenham in the Grand Annual but would run only on soft or heavy ground. We'll enter him everywhere just to find that ground. He'll also have an entry in the Topham at Aintree. His jumping is his forte and he's my trainer's pick. 04-03-26

runners.comment: Running well in defeat this year but up against it today from 7lb out of the handicap
runners.spotlight: Went close in small field at Musselburgh (2m, good to soft) in February and again ran well when 11l third of eight at Kelso (2m1f, good to soft) last time; however, he's up against it today from 7lb out of the handicap.

quotes.race: Connolly's RED MILLS Irish EBF Auction Maiden Hurdle (IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.quote: Aeros Luck deserved that. He was very keen last day but he settled much better today. He's learning still. I would say he'll go on any ground but he is just a horse that can be hard on himself - Gavin Cromwell, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He finished second in three maiden hurdles before finally getting off the mark at Listowel in September. He received a high handicap mark after that, so he's gone on a break and we'll aim him at the spring. 10-11-23

racecards.verdict: Preference is for Irish challenger MOUDAN, who has been in good form on his last two starts and could still have more to offer.
racecards.betting_forecast: 3/1 Sans Bruit, 7/2 Le Nez Creux, 4/1 Traprain Law, 5/1 Moudan, 13/2 Palacio, 7/1 Calico, 14/1 Matata

racecards.race_name: CPMS Novices' Champion Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Won at Kempton in February; ran disappointingly at Ayr (2m4f) on Friday
runners.spotlight: Soundly beaten fourth at Kempton (2m4f, good) last month but mistakes didn't help; won there (2m4f, good to soft) in February; he's probably okay on soft ground and his dam won at up to 3m; ran disappointingly at Ayr (2m4f) on Friday.

quotes.race: Sidney Banks Memorial Novices' Hurdle (Listed Race) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We knew if Califet En Vol was in the argument two out that he would come home strongly and he's basically outstayed them. We'd rather this race be two miles and five than just short of two and a half but he overcame it and was strong through the finish. I don't think Cheltenham is the right way to go with him this year as he's still just a baby and there is a three-mile novice at Aintree and beyond that a race at Ayr, although we would have to mind him if we went there as he likes to get his toe in. We won this race with Shishkin a few years ago and hopefully this horse can be in the same sentence as him down the line - Nicky Henderson, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's done really well and has grown into a fine, big chasing type. He won the Sidney Banks at Huntingdon in February, which is no mean feat. He was running a seriously good race at Aintree in the Grade 1 [Sefton Novices' Hurdle over three miles], but he made a right mess at the second-last and went backwards. He came with an injury on his off-fore and I thought we were in big trouble. He was very sore, but he's fine now and he'll go chasing. 21-10-25

runners.breeder: Kinsale Stud & Mr D V Williams
runners.comment: Good form when winning two-runner novice chase in December but hasn't kicked on since
runners.spotlight: Good form when winning a two-runner novice chase at Doncaster (3m, good to soft) in December on his second run over fences; however, he hasn't kicked on since and needs to raise his game if he's to win this.

stable_tour.quote: He should make a better chaser because he's built for fences. He ended up in front for too long at Ayr last week, but he ran very well considering and he'll improve plenty for it. We might go for a novice at Haydock next month. He needs soft ground and three miles. He has a fair amount of ability. 20-11-25

We probably ran him back too quick at Haydock last week. It looks like he had a harder race than we thought at Chepstow the time before when he was second to a good horse in Juby Ball. We'll give him a month off and look to run him again as long as the ground isn't too firm. He needs to sharpen up but if his jumping improves he could be one for better races next season. 13-03-26

runners.comment: Inconvenienced by the start at Cheltenham; retains potential, especially left-handed
runners.spotlight: Won at Cheltenham (2m4f, soft) last November on second chase start and finished third in quality handicap at Kempton (3m, good to soft) in February, despite jumping to the left at that right-handed track; massively inconvenienced by controversial start when down the field at the Cheltenham Festival; retains potential, especially going left-handed; high on the list.

quotes.race: Sky Bet For The Fans Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It was a commanding performance from Kdeux Saint Fray. He impressed in his Ascot bumper and any horse that can win a bumper there must have a certain level of ability. I was happy to let things unfold but was keen to get going from the bottom of the straight. I couldn't have been more confident in him and this experience should stand him in good stead at galloping tracks - Jonathan Burke, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

stable_tour.quote: I was thrilled with his win at Cheltenham and I've got a few ideas for him now. He'll probably run somewhere fairly straightforward mid-December, but his main aim is to go back to Cheltenham for Trials day in January for the novice handicap. If he does well there, then there could be an argument for doing the boring thing and laying him out for the festival. 23-11-25

prev_owners.owner: Exors Of The Late Trevor Hemmings

runners.comment: Won his first two chase starts; pulled up at Uttoxeter last time but remains of interest
runners.spotlight: Very lightly raced 8yo who returned from a long layoff this year and won his first two chase starts (2m4f/2m5f, soft/heavy; including here); pulled up at Uttoxeter (3m, soft) since and hard to be confident on the back of that, but he bled from the nose and remains of interest on his previous exploits.

quotes.race: Quiz Night At Golf Inn Prestwick Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Milcree has been off a while but he's been doing plenty of work. We've had a few niggles here and there which have been very frustrating. We had him ready to run about five weeks ago and we couldn't. We're happy to be here today, and he jumped fine. He can do that. We won't be in a rush with him, but we'll get him educated and hopefully he can be a nice horse next year -  Nicky Richards, trainer, speaking on Racing TV.

quotes.race: Pauline Phizacklea Memorial Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Milcree did what he had to do and won it in the way that his odds suggested. I liked the way he did that and in these colours [Hemmings Racing] you know he'll be over a fence soon - Nicky Richards, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: A nice horse who won his point-to-point bumper for Brian Harding before coming to us. He does everything pretty well. He's a proper, big Mr Hemmings chasing type who'll be educated over hurdles this season and will take us on a journey. I'm lucky he's been sent to me and he'll be racing soon. 25-10-23

runners.comment: Won at Kelso last time but beat only three rivals and further improvement is needed
runners.spotlight: Course maiden hurdle winner (2m4f, soft) who built upon previous chasing promise with 2l win at Kelso (2m5f, good to soft) in February; there can be optimism that he will be fine now back up in trip but he beat only three rivals last time and further improvement is needed in first-time cheekpieces.

runners.owner: D & D Armstrong Ltd & L Westwood
runners.comment: He's enjoyed a progressive first season over fences and did it nicely at Newcastle latest
runners.spotlight: Runner-up on three of his first four chase starts (2m7f/2m5f, soft/heavy) before winning at Newcastle (2m7f, good to soft) last month; it was a small field last time and he's in a hotter race today, but he did it nicely and could have more to offer in the cheekpieces, which he's worn just twice.

quotes.race: High Horse Design "National Hunt" Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Young Jack ran very well last time, if he hadn't made a mistake at the second last he probably would have won. We like him and he's going forward - David Armstrong, part owner, speaking on Sky Sports Racing.

runners.comment: Pulled up at Fairyhouse just 12 days ago but the return to a left-handed track could help
runners.spotlight: He can make mistakes and was pulled up at Fairyhouse just 12 days ago in first-time cheekpieces (retained); however, he jumped to the left and returns to a left-handed track for the first time since his promising second on chase debut at Haydock (2m4f, soft); won 3m maiden hurdle here; interesting.

runners.owner: Hft Limted And P J King And Son
runners.comment: 10yo who ran pretty well when back over fences in December but needs a bigger run today
runners.spotlight: Close third over hurdles at this meeting 12 months ago (3m, good to soft) and won in that sphere at Uttoxeter (2m7f, good) last July; ran pretty well in 5l third at Newbury (2m6f, good) in December when back chasing for the first time since 2023, but this 10yo needs a bigger performance today.

quotes.race: Village Hotels Handicap Hurdle (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: That was fantastic. Pounding Poet had a break to freshen up and was always being aimed here. We hoped he might win, but second is great. That might be it for him over hurdles. He's going chasing and we are very excited about that - Toni James, owner.

stable_tour.quote: Things haven't gone to plan with him over fences this term, so we're planning to go back over hurdles at Aintree on Boxing Day to try to boost his confidence. His schooling at home has been very good over fences, but he was possibly taken off his feet at Newbury last time and his jumping fell apart after a mistake at the water, where he probably gave himself a bit of a fright. Aintree will be a good place to go back to as he's tended to run well there in the past. 20-12-23

prev_owners.owner: J Carthy, Mrs P Shanahan & D Tabor

runners.comment: Third at Doncaster in January but below par on his next two starts; wears first-time visor
runners.spotlight: Good third off 4lb higher in first-time cheekpieces at Doncaster (3m, soft) in January; however, his form away from Doncaster hasn't been great in the last two seasons and the visor needs to have a positive influence.

quotes.race: Start Your RacingTV Free Trial Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Walking On Air's dam stayed and Nico says this fella will stay. He's nice, but had some hold-ups - no big problems - and he's going to be spectacular. He'll jump a fence and might be very exciting in a year or two. Nico says he'll go two and a half, but he'll need another run before the festival. He could go somewhere with a penalty, although there is the Sidney Banks, but we've others for that - Nicky Henderson, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's a horse I've always liked and he'll be very good one day when we can get him right, but he's had only one run over fences and this would be a tough ask. He's a very big horse, and with big horses trouble is easier to come across than with little horses, but we may try to get him out very soon with a view to the festival. 19-02-24

prev_owners.owner: The Boundary Stables Partnership ( C R Barber)

runners.comment: 3-5 over fences and he's clearly on the up for his top trainer; player
runners.spotlight: Won his first two chases (2m7f, good/good to soft) and, after failing to stay 4m at Kelso, he was short-headed by I Wish You at Wetherby (3m, soft) before winning back at Kelso (2m5f, good to soft) four weeks ago; clearly on the up for his top trainer, who has won two of the last six runnings.

stable_tour.quote: He's a very good work horse - an absolute aeroplane at home - but sometimes it does look too good to be true. We ran him in a bumper at Ludlow in April and hoped it would be a walk in the park but he got interfered with, got very lit up and hung quite badly, eventually running out. The ground proved to be too quick for him at Haydock on his next start and his wind caught him out at Chepstow in a good novice hurdle on his return this campaign. He's had a wind operation since and hopefully that'll sort him out. We think he's very smart and, if he gets his act together, he could be pretty formidable. 30-11-23

runners.breeder: M Collet, J Collet & M Collet
runners.comment: 3rd at Sandown despite mistakes; this trip is worth a go; could go well if finding fluency
runners.spotlight: Two chase wins towards the end of last year (2m3f, good to soft) and did well to finish third of five at Sandown (2m4f, soft) last month having made mistakes; pulled up over 3m4f last January on sole previous run beyond 2m5f but he's worth a go at this trip; could go well if finding fluency.

stable_tour.quote: He's a full-brother to Good Risk At All. It took a while for the penny to drop with him but he's running off a lovely mark now. He's had a wind op and has made a solid start in two outings this season. Fingers crossed we can have a good second half of the campaign with him. 05-01-24

runners.comment: Ran well in defeat last month in his first two chases and he's an each-way possible
runners.spotlight: Prominent racer; beaten just a neck over hurdles at Haydock (3m, good to soft) in December and ran well in defeat last month in his first two chases (2m7f/2m4f, good to soft); has won on soft; each-way possible.

stable_tour.quote: A nice bumper horse we've bought who goes very well and will run before the ground firms up. He won his only point and should be ready to run in mid-March. He's been steadily improving at home and his work has been really good. He's taken a bit of time but is very straightforward. He's improved steadily and I'll be surprised if he can't acquit himself really well in a bumper. We've had quite a few bumper winners in the last few years and his homework compares very favourably to all of those. I'd be very hopeful he's above average. 14-02-24

runners.comment: The form of his Wetherby win was franked and he's in good hands to continue to progress
runners.spotlight: Improved form to get off the mark over fences at the third attempt at Wetherby (3m, soft) in February; hit with a 7lb rise but the short-head runner-up Diamond Dealer went one better next time and this 6yo is in good hands to continue to progress; respected.

quotes.race: Whitehall Turret Club Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race) (Div II)
quotes.quote: I Wish You was beaten by three of our horses. I never felt he was ungenuine or anything, he just wants further and to mature a bit. He was recommended and wasn't expensive, and the owners have been very good to us. We bought him as a two-year-old and it's very rewarding when you've kept them that long and they come through. I feel like there's a lot of progress in him and I think he's a chaser - Peter Scudamore, trainer's assistant.

stable_tour.quote: He was quite coltish but got loads of experience in those junior races. He finished second a lot but it was because he was a little bit weak. He knows how to win, as he proved on his hurdles debut this month. I can't wait for him to go chasing. 30-10-24

runners.comment: Lightly raced 8yo who won at Hexham and the step up in trip could be a positive move
runners.spotlight: 8yo who has returned from an absence this season and has improved with each of his three chase starts, winning at Hexham (2m4f, soft) last month; this is a tougher assignment but he did it readily last time and the step up in trip could be a positive move; he's one to consider.

quotes.race: Betting.Bet Horse Racing Tips Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: What a lovely horse Big John Wayne is. What a chaser he's going to make. We wanted to buy the Blandfords a really nice horse to go chasing in the long term but would win novice hurdles and he could have done. He's one to dream for. He's slightly stiff on his left-hand side but he's fine. I don't know if he'd have won but I know he'd have stayed and kept galloping - Lucinda Russell, trainer.

runners.comment: Has won his last two; this is tougher but this 6yo may have more left in the tank
runners.spotlight: Took a sizeable step forward when winning over C&D (soft) in February and he followed up at Kelso (3m2f, good to soft) four weeks ago; he's 5lb higher than last time and is in much more competitive race today, but this progressive 6yo could still have more left in the tank.

quotes.race: Remembering Duncan Davidson Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Blakey Boy has done us proud. I've had a few horses but this is the biggest win so far. We're setting our sights high, we'd like to come back here for the Borders National at the end of the year - Alan Gilchrist, representing the winning syndicate.

racecards.verdict: There could be a big turnaround from Ayiko but KDEUX SAINT FRAY was looking good prior to his forgiveable defeat at Cheltenham.
racecards.betting_forecast: 3/1 Diamond Dealer, 6/1 Kdeux Saint Fray, 13/2 Big John Wayne, 9/1 Milcree,  Just Over Land,  I Wish You, 11/1 Blakey Boy, 14/1 Al Kalila,  Young Jack, 16/1 Caughtinyourtrance, 20/1 Gamesters Guy,  Walking On Air, 25/1 Ayiko,  Pounding Poet

racecards.race_name: Coral Scottish Champion Hurdle (A Limited Handicap) (Grade 2) (GBB Race)

runners.breeder: E A R L Elevage Figerro & Hubert Favre
runners.comment: Won 2 high-profile handicaps then down the field in the Champion Hurdle; could bounce back
runners.spotlight: Won at Newbury (2m, soft) last November on second handicap start and easily followed up there in the prestigious William Hill Hurdle in February (2m, heavy); reluctant to line up and couldn't adopt usual prominent pitch when down the field in the Champion Hurdle at Cheltenham last month; returns to a handicap today and could bounce back with a bold bid.

quotes.race: William Hill Hurdle (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Tutti Quanti is just one of those big, backward-types who is physically improving and getting better every time. I still think there's more to come and he loves that ground. I was a little bit nervous because the record books say 12st is hard to win a race like this, but he's annihilated them. He's now becoming the real horse and he's got some engine. Colm [Donlon, owner] and I both said we could supplement him for the Champion Hurdle if we wanted to. The great thing about doing that is you don't have to do it until five or six days before, and by then you'll have a great idea about what the ground will be like. If we had a wet spell and it was like this, we'd think about it. You'd have to. If it was good, we wouldn't, but he'd hold his own. It's an open race this year, and if it'd be testing you'd want to have him in there - Paul Nicholls, trainer.Tutti Quanti was very good, wasn't he? I thought he'd run well but Paul [Nicholls] has been really bullish about him to me at home and he was right. He does hang and left-handed is the key to this horse. He's obviously a good horse. I'm not quite sure he's Champion Hurdle class just yet but he's a very good horse and will be a lovely chaser next season - Harry Cobden, jockey, speaking to ITV Racing.

quotes.race: RHN Travel Airport Transfers Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Tutti Quanti is an improving young horse who has just needed time. I need to discuss with his owner but he's highly likely to go straight novice chasing in the autumn. He definitely won't run in the Scottish Champion Hurdle as Kabral Du Mathan runs there - Paul Nicholls, trainer.

quotes.race: Weatherbys & Birdie Calendars Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race) (Div I)
quotes.quote: Tutti Quanti is very green but he's quite a smart horse. He's only four and still quite weak but he's improving all the time. Harry Cobden, jockey, talking to Sky Sports.

stable_tour.quote: He could be the big surprise of the week. The great thing is we don't need to decide about supplementing until six days before when we'll have a good idea of the weather forecast and what the ground will be like. It's hardly going to be fast on the first day anyway, but if it's soft we'll have a look. He's rated 151 ? Golden Ace is 152 and The New Lion is 159, so we're not miles apart from them. His performance at Newbury tells you he's improving rapidly, and when they're on an upward curve like that you just don't know where the ceiling is. He's got lots of natural speed and has added stamina as he's got stronger. I'll probably stick him in the County Hurdle as well, but he might not find that so easy off his new mark and we'll stick to the Champion if we can and if the ground is right. 15-02-26

runners.comment: Progressive novice who won the Morebattle Hurdle at Kelso; strong contender up 6lb
runners.spotlight: Progressive novice who made it 3-5 over hurdles when winning the competitive Morebattle Hurdle on handicap debut at Kelso (2m, good to soft) in February; has also shown promise on soft ground; this 6yo may well continue on an upward curve and he's a strong contender up 6lb.

quotes.race: bet365 Morebattle Hurdle (A Handicap Hurdle) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Captain Hugo was still travelling well when he fell at Musselburgh and it's nice that he stood up and showed us what he's capable of. He's always shown a good attitude and plenty of speed. We'll get him home and probably aim towards Aintree rather than Cheltenham - Johnson White, joint-trainer.It's a tough race but Captain Hugo travelled everywhere, so I could put him in gaps that were opening, and his jumping got slicker the further we went, that really helped. It was far from certain at the last but he's tough, he's got a great attitude and really sticks his head out. You can't knock his attitude. He had a nasty fall last time and it hasn't hindered his confidence at all - Sean Houlihan, jockey.

quotes.race: Agetur UK 40th Anniversary In Business Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: On paper, it was going to take some winning, but I was very happy with Captain Hugo at home. I knew he'd come on mentally, if not physically, and I'm chuffed with how he's started his hurdling career. We'll look at slightly bigger targets now - Johnson White, joint-trainer.

stable_tour.quote: I was delighted with his win at Newbury and we can look to go over further than two miles with him if we need to. We'll let him tell us what to do in terms of trip and we'd like to go in another ordinary novice hurdle before we step him up in class. On the evidence of Newbury he could be a smart novice hurdler this season. 20-11-25

runners.comment: Big step back in right direction when seventh in the County Hurdle and not ruled out
runners.spotlight: Easily won a competitive 4yo handicap at Chepstow (2m, good) last October on his reappearance; underwhelming on his next three starts but took big step back in right direction when keeping on for seventh of 23 in the County Hurdle at Cheltenham (2m1f, soft) last month; not ruled out.

quotes.race: Victor Ludorum Juvenile Hurdle (Go North Grey Bomber Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We were quietly confident as his work had improved since Sedgefield. Gibbs Island looks a really nice prospect. He looks a better jumper than he did a Flat horse and he jumped so well. He's got a festival entry but we'll see as he's only a four-year-old with his whole life in front of him. We'll take our time and try to make the right decision - Tom Lacey, trainer.

quotes.race: Irish EBF Median Sires Series Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.quote: Gibbs Island did it well and ground it out. He had a nice run at Roscommon and we thought that the step up in trip would be in his favour. He is a good mover and is not dependent on ground - Andy Oliver, trainer

runners.comment: Caught the eye on stable debut in the County Hurdle and he's firmly in calculations
runners.spotlight: 7yo who has shown glimpses of significant promise across his light career and didn't enjoy a clear run in the straight when 12th of 23 on his stable debut in the County Hurdle at Cheltenham (2m1f, soft) last month, when beaten only about 8l on his first run since last October; wears a first-time hood and could have plenty more to offer for the Skelton yard.

quotes.race: Arkle Finance EBF "National Hunt" Novices' Hurdle (Qualifier) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We are back on track. We turned a lot of stones to try and find out what happened at Aintree. We found a few little bits and bobs, but nothing that put us out for that long as you could see. I was just keen to get his season back on track before we dwelt on it for too long. The ground there was soft enough, and it is not the good to soft that they have advertised, but Tellherthename has handled it very well. He is an unbelievably class horse. That now gives him his fourth run so he has got the option of the Betfair Hurdle, but the ground would have to be spot on for that otherwise we will go straight to the Supreme with him. I think he is a class horse with gears galore and I sometimes think they are best fresh. They go such a gallop in that race (Supreme) and if you are anything but absolutely ready for the day then you might get flat footed - Ben Pauling, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's a good horse who'll be making his debut for us, having joined us just after Christmas. He's had a bit of a chequered career but he'll go there super-fresh and his handicap mark doesn't look beyond him, although this will be a big ask. 17-02-26

runners.comment: Very close third in this last year; ran well in the County Hurdle at Cheltenham last month
runners.spotlight: Made all in Grade 2 mares' hurdle at Ascot (1m7f, soft) in January and ran well for a long way when ninth of 23 in the County Hurdle at Cheltenham (2m1f, soft) last month; she's 1lb lower than when a very close third in this last year (good to soft) and could again be involved.

quotes.race: BetMGM Warfield Mares' Hurdle (Grade 2) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: When we got beat in a Listed race yesterday I thought our time was never going to come. We've been runner-up or third in so many £100,000 handicaps and Listed races that I can't believe we've actually got our head in front in one. To me this is like winning the Gold Cup. It sounds mental but it's really surreal. I was really down yesterday after we got beat but Ooh Betty deserves this. She was beaten a neck in a Scottish Champion Hurdle, third in a Grade 2 at Newbury and second to Golden Ace in a Listed race at Cheltenham. She's been a bit out of form but we thought we'd ironed out those issues, and this is a massive day for us - Ben Clarke, trainer.

quotes.race: Bet £10 Get £10 At PlanetSportBet Mares' Handicap Hurdle (Challenger Mares' Hurdle Series Qualifier)
quotes.quote: Ooh Betty has won three of her last five races and she's a decent mare. Quick ground is imperative to her and we'll try and find another race in three or four weeks - which is optimistic - otherwise we'll give her a break. Even good to soft is too soft for her - Ben Clarke, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: She ran in the Imperial Cup, finishing in the middle of the field behind Go Dante. She's stepped out of novice company this season and has just improved and improved, winning two £20,000 handicaps. She's 15.1hh and is all speed. She'd probably just see out 2m4f on a flat track. We might look at the Scottish Champion Hurdle at Ayr and her season might finish with the Swinton. The wind operation last  summer has certainly helped, but more importantly she needs good ground to be seen to best effect. 12-03-25

runners.comment: Just two runs this season and down the field in the County Hurdle, but he's not discounted
runners.spotlight: Just two starts this season and down the field in the County Hurdle at Cheltenham last month; however, prior to that he was a creditable third of four in the Grade 2 Kingwell Hurdle at Wincanton (1m7f, heavy) and he was a progressive handicapper last term (various ground); not discounted.

quotes.race: Fitzdares Sovereign Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: What's surprising for a horse who is quite effeminate is that Nico said Secret Squirrel is really tough. As long as he's all right, the William Hill Hurdle will be the game. The day he was born he'd walk up to you and knock you over. We broke him in as a yearling because he was such a pain - Hughie Morrison, trainer.

quotes.race: EBF Stallions "National Hunt" Novices' Hurdle (Qualifier) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We're really excited about Secret Squirrel, but you don't dare to be too excited, although you've got to have something to look forward to as well. He seemed to do that quite easily and we've always thought he was very good - Mary Morrison, owner-breeder and trainer's wife.

runners.comment: Today's mark poses a question but this mare has thrived for a new stable this season
runners.spotlight: She's thrived this season and made it 3-5 for the yard (wins at 1m7f-2m1f on good to soft/heavy) when winning big-field mares' novice handicap at Kelso four weeks ago; from out of the handicap she's 12lb higher today back against males but it remains to be seen where her limitations lie.

quotes.race: BetWright Herring Queen Series Final Mares' Novices' Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Queenie St Clair did everything right, she jumped and travelled great. I had enough under me to get the gaps I wanted. She's very gutsy and she's done it very well - Freddie Keighley, jockey.

runners.comment: Made a fine start for this yard and he could leave his Newbury run miles behind
runners.spotlight: Went close on stable debut in big field at Ascot (1m7f, soft) in December then won at Sandown (2m, good) in January, turning the tables on Dance And Glance who won a nice prize at Haydock this month; 5lb out of the handicap today and pulled up in the William Hill Hurdle at Newbury in February, but very few ran to form in that attritional contest; retains potential; chance.

stable_tour.quote: This is a really lovely sort from the David Maxwell dispersal sale. He came a head second in a competitive Ascot handicap hurdle over 2m, which he would have won had he jumped the last better. He then ran at Sandown on Saturday and put in a great performance to win by a length and a half, having travelled beautifully throughout. I took a risk running him so quickly after Ascot but I needed him to get into the William Hill Hurdle at Newbury. I was worried about the heavy ground, which rode like glue, but he handled it well and actually quickened on it. I've got five weeks to get him ready for Newbury. He has plenty of gears and likes a fast pace. I'd also like to run him at Royal Ascot in the summer. 07-01-26

runners.comment: Won in small field at Kelso recently; profile suggests he's vulnerable back up in grade
runners.spotlight: Following wind surgery he returned to form to win in a small field at Kelso (2m5f, good) recently, and he's fine on slow ground and at this trip; however, from out of the handicap he's 10lb higher today and his profile suggests he'll be vulnerable back up in grade.

quotes.race: Sky Bet Supreme Trial Rossington Main Novices' Hurdle (Grade 2) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We know Dedicated Hero is a nice horse but today was about finding out how nice he is, and he was very good. I was niggling at the end of the straight because he found the track a bit sharp but he stayed on all the way to the line. I just hope Ruby Walsh wasn't watching because I dropped my whip. The original plan was the Premier Hurdle at Kelso as he's won twice there and then maybe Aintree - we haven't really talked about Cheltenham - Ryan Mania, rider.

quotes.race: Racing Post Go North Jodami Series Final Open National Hunt Flat Race (Series Final) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Dedicated Hero is a proper horse. When I rode him last time it was like I did everything I could to get him beat and he still pulled it out of the fire and won nicely. It's great to come and do that under penalty on ground he probably didn't love - Ryan Mania, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

stable_tour.quote: We were delighted with his victory in the Rossington Main at Haydock on Saturday as he probably needs a bit further than 2m. He outstayed them, having got into a little bit of trouble, and it was a gutsy performance. He's quite difficult to fathom as he doesn't really show you anything at home. I thought 2m was going to be far too sharp for him, but he's won over that trip really well on his last two starts. We'll definitely go to the Listed Premier Hurdle at Kelso over 2m2f. He's unbeaten in three runs there and it has been the plan. Cheltenham won't be in the equation and I'm not a great lover of the handicaps at Aintree as they're very competitive and run at a hell of a pace. It'll be one race at a time and he's slightly ground dependent as soft is important to him. 22-01-25

runners.comment: 2l fifth in this last year off similar mark but hasn't been at his best this season
runners.spotlight: Beaten only 2l when fifth in this last year and runs off just 1lb higher today (from 8lb out of the handicap); however, he hasn't been at his best this season and would be a surprise winner.

stable_tour.quote: It was unfortunate what happened at Musselburgh last time when he whipped round at the start and unseated Ciaran [Gethings] as that was meant to be his prep run for the County Hurdle. It was annoying as it meant the plan was thrown out of the window. He's declared to run on Thursday at Taunton for a 0-140 handicap hurdle over 2m. He should run there and then we'll go to Cheltenham. 12-02-26

racecards.verdict: Progressive novice CAPTAIN HUGO won the competitive Morebattle Hurdle at Kelso in February and is taken to make it 2-2 in handicaps.
racecards.betting_forecast: 9/4 Tutti Quanti, 7/2 Captain Hugo, 11/2 Gibbs Island, 7/1 Secret Squirrel, 15/2 All In You, 11/1 Ooh Betty,  Dedicated Hero, 16/1 Queenie St Clair, 33/1 Welsh Charger

racecards.race_name: Jordan Electrics Ltd Seafield Trophy Mares' Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Posted her third Listed win in convincing fashion at Kelso last month; solid credentials
runners.spotlight: Posted her third Listed win in convincing fashion at Kelso (3m, good to soft) four weeks ago; went close in soft-ground Grade 3 the time before; solid credentials back in a handicap.

quotes.race: BetWright Beeswing Mares' Hurdle (Listed Race) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: The race suited as three miles is her trip, it's a Listed race and the pot was quite good. And if you look at her form, the only times she doesn't collect is when we've overfaced her in grade. World of Fortunes is deadly, she's some mare - Michael Broderick, owner.

quotes.race: Livescore Bet Mares' Novices' Hurdle (Listed Race) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It was all down to Jordan Gainford as he told me how to ride World Of Fortunes and that she'd stay. He has her to look forward to in the better races in the spring - Brian Hughes, jockey.

quotes.race: Cheesestrings Irish EBF Mares Hurdle
quotes.quote: World Of Fortunes is a lovely mare with loads of ability and is a nice one going forward. She can sharpen up a bit more - Jordan Gainford, rider.

runners.comment: Disappointing at Chepstow in February but in very good heart previously and not ruled out
runners.spotlight: Front-runner who went close twice in a row at Kempton (3m, good) towards the end of last year following an absence; tailed off at Chepstow since on soft ground she should have handled; needs to bounce back, but not ruled out with first-time blinkers replacing cheekpieces.

stable_tour.quote: She won at Chepstow in October 2024 and has finished second or third in her four runs since then. She's likely to go to Chepstow on Friday. She has run very well at Kempton in her two races this season, beaten only a length in November on her first run for nearly a year and then being unlucky to get beaten a head at Christmas. She's been knocking on the door but hopefully isn't far away from knocking the door down. 12-02-26

runners.comment: Could bounce back with bold showing back against fellow mares; trip may be within range
runners.spotlight: Untested at this trip under rules but there have been hints that she'll stay this far; in good form against fellow mares this winter prior to tailing off in the Imperial Cup at Sandown last month; takes on her own sex today and it will be no surprise to see a bold showing.

stable_tour.quote: She's been a really good mare and has always shown plenty of speed at home. She fractured her leg in the spring and had to take a bit of time off because of that. She's progressed this season, going close a couple of times before winning a novice hurdle at Lingfield last time. We want to run her at Kelso in a £100,000 mares' final in a couple of weeks. If it's good to soft ground she'll act on it as she's got plenty of speed. She's pretty well handicapped off her current mark of 116 and we're looking forward to it. 12-03-25

runners.comment: She's below her last winning mark but Hexham seems to bring out the best in her
runners.spotlight: Bang there when falling seven out in the Hexham Marathon over fences last month (4m, soft); she's 1lb below her last winning hurdle mark but Hexham seems to bring out the best in her and this inconsistent mare was pulled up in this race 12 months ago; it might be best to look elsewhere.

runners.comment: She's run some good races this season, including Chepstow win, and might not be far away
runners.spotlight: Unseated rider at the start at Chepstow two starts ago but she's run some good races this season, winning at Chepstow (2m7f, good to soft) in December and fourth of 15 at Windsor (3m, soft) in January; wears first-time cheekpieces and might not be far away.

runners.comment: Third in this last year and won here last month; it was a small field but form franked
runners.spotlight: 6l third of nine in this last year (good to soft) and she won here (2m5f, soft) last month; had just three rivals to beat last time but did it nicely from a next-time-out winner; could be in the shake-up.

runners.owner: Mrs Paul Shanahan & Mrs John Magnier
runners.comment: 2-2 in handicaps; this is tougher but she's clearly highly progressive for her top yard
runners.spotlight: Won on handicap debut at Newcastle (2m4f, heavy) in January and improved again to follow up at Bangor (2m7f, soft); this is a tougher test of her credentials but she's clearly highly progressive for her top yard.

stable_tour.quote: A lovely filly, she was never really a bumper horse and is much stronger this season. She ran really well in a mares' maiden hurdle at Uttoxeter and will step forward massively for that, but I'm most excited about her being a chaser. 10-11-25

runners.comment: Respectable efforts in her first two handicap hurdles but those were over 2m1f/2m
runners.spotlight: She's run reasonably well, albeit without seriously threatening, in her first two handicap hurdles (2m1f/2m, soft/good to soft); won five times on the Flat (at up to 1m4f) and she could have more to offer in this code, but it remains to be seen whether she'll stay this far.

quotes.race: Download The Vickers.Bet App Fillies' Handicap
quotes.quote: We were disappointed when Azahara Palace got beat at Catterick, but I think the course caught her out. She's quite difficult to train, and was still learning here, but hopefully she'll keep progressing - Hughie Morrison, trainer, talking to Sky Sports Racing.

stable_tour.quote: I don't think she's a miler and I think she'll get 1m4f now. She ran last time at Newbury behind Burrito but the ground was too firm. The winner is a Group horse and I thought beforehand he was the one we all had to beat. She's got races in her and, although she'll run on fast going, she basically needs the speed to be taken out of the ground for her to be at her most effective. She could even run up to a mark of 90 on the right surface. 29-05-25

runners.comment: Major improver this season but has to prove her current mark isn't beyond her
runners.spotlight: 6yo who has been a major improver back over hurdles this season, winning three times (2m-2m5f, good-soft); having shot up the weights she again ran well when second of four at Chepstow (2m7f, soft) in February, but she needs to prove her current mark isn't beyond her; 1lb wrong today.

runners.comment: Needs handicap career-best but outran 200-1 odds when Listed fourth at Kelso last month
runners.spotlight: Five-time hurdle winner (2m4f/2m5f, good/good to soft), the latest last March; below best for most of this season and from out of the handicap today she has a career-high mark to defy but she outran her 200-1 odds when staying on strongly for fourth behind World Of Fortunes in a Listed race at Kelso (3m, good to soft) four weeks ago, and perhaps isn't a forlorn hope.

quotes.race: Ladbrokes Go North Cab On Target Handicap Hurdle (Series Final) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I love racing because of the horses and Starlyte is the sort of horse I love. She's only tiny but she's so brave. You have to drop her in and let her pass horses and I'm delighted for the owners Allan and Anne Grant who've just got married - Lucinda Russell, trainer.

quotes.race: Follow Thehawkponteland On Instagram Mares' Handicap Hurdle (Go North Lady Buttons Series Qualifier)
quotes.quote: Starlyte needs a fast-run two-and-a-half miles and she's the most game horse. It's her attitude that wins her races - Lucinda Russell, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: She came to us from the Flat and made a flying start by winning a 2m4½f Newcastle handicap hurdle. We'll keep her to that trip with a view to going up to 3m later. She desperately needs good ground and is ready to go as soon as things dry out. 25-01-23

racecards.verdict: Topweight WORLD OF FORTUNES was a commanding winner of a Listed race at Kelso last month and can follow up back in a handicap.
racecards.betting_forecast: 5/2 Twistthenightaway, 11/4 World Of Fortunes, 5/1 Love Of Neymore, 8/1 Game Colours,  Fox's Fancy, 10/1 Holly Hartingo, 16/1 Princess Keri, 20/1 Pinot Rouge,  Azahara Palace

racecards.race_name: Coral Scottish Grand National Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)

runners.owner: Molly Willis & Paul Willis & Brian Groarke & Tom Groarke

prev_owners.owner: Molly Willis & Paul Willis & Brian Groarke & Tom Groarke
Brian Groarke & Tom Groarke & Ms Margaret Mullins

runners.comment: Won in good style at Cheltenham (extended 3m2f, good to soft) in December; first headgear
runners.spotlight: Off the mark over fences in good style at Cheltenham (extended 3m2f, good to soft) in December and that's the furthest he's been; worked his way into contention at the Festival there (3m1f Ultima) on latest outing until some bumping on the home turn and running out of steam; not disgraced there but 4m has to be something of a guess; cheekpieces are added.

quotes.race: Turners Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Blaze The Way is very reliable, he always turns up every day and always runs his races. The step up in trip was needed. We'll get through today and we'll see after this. Today was the plan and it all worked out - Mags Mullins, trainer.

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: I'm delighted with Blaze The Way. He won his bumper and was placed over hurdles. I think he's a stayer and the last day we kind of rode him the wrong way in a better race. I've liked him for a while and I wasn't surprised to see that. We won't go again quickly with him, there might be something at the Thyestes meeting for him. We'll see how he improves from here - Mags Mullins, trainer.

quotes.race: Ballagh INH Flat Race
quotes.quote: Blaze The Way will be a grand horse over a hurdle and has plenty size to jump a fence. He battled well and is a saleable horse - Mags Mullins, trainer.

runners.comment: Close third of 22 in the 3m1f Ultima at Cheltenham where he kept on stoutly; raised 5lb
runners.spotlight: 0-5 in this first chase campaign but pipped at Cheltenham (2m4f, soft) in January and a close third of 22 in the Ultima at the Festival there (3m1f, good to soft) on latest outing; raised 5lb for this first attempt at a marathon trip but he's relatively unexposed and kept on stoutly in that bold show last time.

quotes.race: Trustmarque Ultima Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I'm thrilled with Quebecois and we'll have to see now whether we keep him a novice for next season or try and win a nice race this spring. I was going to put him in the Scottish National as novices have a good record in it. I probably still will, but there's a novice chase there too. The thing is that if you win now, you are still a novice until December. I was always thinking he'd be the sort of horse for the Coral Cup, as he goes well left-handed on decent ground, and he's shown today that after the summer he'll be up there with those horses. His jumping is great and that was a fantastic run -  Paul Nicholls, trainer.

quotes.race: OLBG 'Chasing Excellence' Novices' Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Fair play to Ben's [Pauling] horse, he knew what he was doing and took us out [of our comfort zone] on ground like that over two miles. It's qualified Quebecois now for the Ultimate and all roads lead there now - Max McNeill, owner, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

quotes.race: Colourfence Newport Long Life Garden Railings Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race) (Div II)
quotes.quote: We've always liked Quebecois and we thought he'd win, but we didn't quite know what to expect past that. He jumps nicely and is a half-brother to Brindisi Breeze, so he's from a good family and he's got the right attitude. The Challow would have to be in our sights. When Stage Star won this we sent him to Newbury before the Challow, so I suspect we'll up Quebecois in grade and go somewhere similar in a month's time. He'll improve a fair bit yet with more experience. We'd like to think he's in that sort of Stage Star, Hermes Allen bracket - Paul Nicholls, trainer.

quotes.race: Clapham Open National Hunt Flat Race (Category 1 Elimination) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Quebecois was very impressive. It's always a job to try and gauge a horse in these bumpers, but it was a half-decent race and he quickened clear. You have to be very pleased with that performance - Harry Cobden, jockey

stable_tour.quote: It would be nice to have a runner for Max McNeill in the race he sponsors, and I've always thought the Ultima trip would suit him. The race he all but won on Trials day always turns out to be good, and he caught me a bit by surprise there. I've always thought he's handy and for some reason he's better going left-handed. He needs one more run over fences to qualify and we intend to go to Newbury on Tuesday. He'll have entries in the Plate, and in the novice race in case we don't get qualified for any reason. 15-02-26

runners.comment: NH Chase 2nd at Cheltenham; jumping can be a bit sticky but he's a prime candidate for 4m
runners.spotlight: Won two small-field handicaps at Kelso (soft/heavy) over the extended 2m7f, easily on penultimate start (made most) despite the odd jumping indiscretion; wore cheekpieces that day and again when an excellent second of 17, coming from out the back, in the NH Chase at Cheltenham (3m6f, good to soft); his jumping can be a bit sticky but he's a prime candidate for 4m.

runners.owner: G Mason, Sir A Ferguson, C & G Barber

prev_owners.owner: G Mason,Sir A Ferguson,Mr & Mrs P K Barber

runners.comment: Asserted by 8l on run-in for 4m2f Midlands National at Uttoxeter (soft) last time; up 7lb
runners.spotlight: Made a bad mistake on penultimate outing but he won starts either side and latest was the 4m2f Midlands National at Uttoxeter (soft) in which he was always prominent and asserted by 8l on run-in, with Git Maker in third; up 7lb but his only attempt at a marathon trip brought a clear career best.

quotes.race: JenningsBet Midlands Grand National (Handicap Chase) (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Isaac Des Obeaux has always wanted a trip. Harry [Cobden] always said to me that would be the ideal race for him. He just needed time to mature and Sam [Twiston-Davies] gave him a great ride. It's great for the Barber boys, that's fantastic, and for Ged as well - Paul Nicholls, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's not the most robust of individuals. It was frustrating he drew a blank last season but he was one of ours who simply wasn't right for much of the campaign. I'm sure he's better than that and I hope he'll return to form in staying handicap chases on soft ground. Flo Willis, who rides him in the mornings, keeps telling me he's a different horse this season, so I hope she's right. 04-11-25

prev_owners.owner: Walters Plant Hire & James & Jean Potter

runners.comment: 11l third in this last year; 6lb lower today, as he's not fired on all cylinders this term
runners.spotlight: 11l third in this race (good to soft) last year; 6lb lower this time, as he's not fired on all cylinders this term but this 11yo may be dangerous to dismiss, including as first-time blinkers replace his usual cheekpieces.

quotes.race: Coral Trophy Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I've got no real faith in the runners at the moment just with how the form of the yard is. However, this lad stays forever. I was a bit worried down the back straight but when I saw Our Power turning in, I was quietly confident. He would have run in the Ladbrokes Trophy at Newbury but he had a little setback and we had no other option but to train him for this, which is a fantastic race itself. I'd say he would be doubtful to get in at Aintree so it will be Cheltenham for the Ultima then he will either go for the Scottish National or the bet365 Gold Cup - Sam Thomas, trainer.

quotes.race: Bateaux London Gold Cup Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Our Power will never win by too far. He's your typical horse off the Flat - he's streetwise and is not ever going to over-exert himself. But he's genuine and we'll aim him at the Coral Gold Cup. We wouldn't have got in off a mark of 137 so he had to win. Fingers crossed that will sneak us in. You'd think a flat track like Newbury will suit him. Sam Thomas, trainer, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

quotes.race: Racing TV Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: There was a lot of pace on (at Doncaster) and Our Power reached for the first but didn't quite get there. Sam (Thomas) had said he had been fantastic since and thankfully he was right. It was very tacky holding ground and I'd say he would get a bit further. He has a good way of racing as he doesn't use energy up and his jumping is getting better - Sam Twiston-Davies, jockey.

quotes.race: St. James's Place Juvenile Hurdle
quotes.quote: I was slightly disappointed with Our Power at Exeter, but I think he's a better horse this way round; he went badly left at the first at Exeter, but we've done a lot of schooling since. That was much better and he probably outstayed the second. I'll speak to the owners but we might look at Cheltenham at the end of January. The Finale comes too soon and Wayne said he wouldn't want it any softer than today; he's handled it only just - Alan King, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He had a nice prep run and then ran in the Coral Gold Cup. He was in a good rhythm and Adam Wedge was very happy with him before he fell - it was too far out to know how he would have fared. He came back sore from that and we're trying to get him back to 100 per cent before deciding on where to go next. I wouldn't have thought we'll be aiming him at the Grand National at the end of the season as he didn't quite get the trip last year. 05-01-24

runners.comment: Went close in the Kim Muir at Cheltenham (3m2f); up 6lb and more to prove on soft ground
runners.spotlight: Willie Mullins had six runners in both the last two renewals, including the winners (both young horses unproven beyond 3m); this time, with the trainers' championship out of reach, he relies on just this 7yo who was delivered with what seemed a winning challenge under Patrick Mullins in the Kim Muir at Cheltenham (3m2f, good) last time only to find that Ask Brewster battled back; up 6lb and more to prove on soft ground, but he has to be in serious calculations.

quotes.race: Happy Birthday Margaret Watling Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Road To Home's jumping at speed needs work as at the second-last and the last he was a bit careful. I don't mind that too much, but I wanted to win as easy as I could because we might go to Fairyhouse and Punchestown with him. I think he's a nice horse - Patrick Mullins, rider, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

runners.comment: After wind surgery, faded badly from three out when 10-1 for the Kim Muir last month
runners.spotlight: Second-season chaser who took his form to new levels over about 3m1f-3m2f at Cheltenham initially this season but, after wind surgery, faded badly from three out when 10-1 for the Kim Muir there last month; needs to bounce back with another career best and he has more to prove on this third attempt at a marathon trip.

quotes.race: Betfair Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: The horses have been brilliant all season and Herakles Westwood deserved that. He loves Cheltenham. I might give him a break and come back in March. There's the Ultima and the Kim Muir - Warren Greatrex, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's a smashing horse who is going the right way. He ran a bit fresh on his comeback at Cheltenham, but he finished the race strongly after having a bit of a blow. He'll have an entry in the Welsh National but he wouldn't want the ground to be really deep. There's also a £100,000 handicap chase at Cheltenham's December meeting, and the fact he handles the track is a plus. He should leap markedly forward for his run the other day and I'm confident he's going to win a big one. 23-11-25

All three of his starts this season have been at Cheltenham and it's a track that suits him. He needed his first run but still finished second and then ran a good fourth to Blaze The Way in a premier handicap chase. He then got his head in front back there on New Year's Day, when he stayed on really well all the way to the line. I was really pleased with his win. He did it nicely and jumped well. Looking ahead, he could go for one of the festival handicaps such as the Ultima or the Kim Muir. And looking even further ahead, the Welsh Grand National would be a target. He handles just about any ground. 07-01-26

runners.comment: 3m4f winner who took the Kim Muir on latest start; all chase wins on good or good to firm
runners.spotlight: 3m4f resulted in an 8l win at Cheltenham last April and, over shorter, he's won two of his three starts this season; latest was the 3m2f Kim Muir at Cheltenham last month in which he was always front rank under Shane Cotter and responded so well when Road To Home joined him on run-in; up 7lb but 4m is unlikely to be a problem; what could be is that all five of his chase wins have been on good ground or good to firm.

quotes.race: Rosconn Group Fulke Walwyn Kim Muir Challenge Cup Amateur Jockeys' Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Yesterday we needed soft ground for Libberty Hunter and today we needed good ground for Ask Brewster, so when it rained this morning we thought 'oh no'. But we knew they were both in great shape and we've come away with a first and a second. Ask Brewster stays, and we had a very good boy on board. I don't know him, but I think Evan [Williams] and Conor Ring spoke to a couple of the Irish lads and that's who we got - Cath Williams, trainer.I watched a few replays, and any time Ask Brewster was in front he seemed to love it and winged his fences. I jumped him out nice and handy and he ran away nearly to the first, and I knew it was his day then. He was very game when Patrick [Mullins] came to us - Shane Cotter, jockey.

quotes.race: Brooklands Watches Golden Miller Racing Holman Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I thought Ask Brewster won well on spring ground at Chepstow and he travelled, jumped and stayed well. My concern was if he'd stay but he was strong at the line. He's a young horse and there's no doubt he's improved. We can train him for next spring and he could be a horse for the Scottish National next season. Evan Williams - trainer.

stable_tour.quote: A progressive sort who ran well at Sandown last time despite the ground being far too soft for him. Before that he won over 2m7½f at Chepstow, a good effort considering he'd gone up 9lb since his previous run at Cheltenham in April when he won a 3m4f chase. He must have a fast surface and, when he gets it, he's a really good staying handicap chaser. 14-01-26

runners.comment: Unraced beyond 3m2f; should stay further than that but others are a bit more persuasive
runners.spotlight: Unraced beyond 3m2f but should stay further than that; 15l winner of a major 3m handicap at Kempton last February but he's found his revised mark a bit too tough since (close second to Herakles Westwood at Cheltenham on New Year's Day) and is still 10lb higher today; others are a bit more persuasive.

quotes.race: Ladbrokes Trophy Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It was a brilliant ride from Charlie [Deutsch] and I do feel for Dylan [Johnston] as he has been fantastic for us all season as first jockey. He had the choice and it wasn't an easy decision so I do feel for him as he does all the work and schooling on him at home. A lot of credit goes to him for prepping the horse back at base. We've got a few entries at Cheltenham for Katate Dori, so we'll see what the handicapper does and go from there - Sam Thomas, trainer.

quotes.race: Happy New Year From Greendale Farm Conditional Jockeys' Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: Katate Dori loved every minute of it. He's obviously improved a lot for a fence and he's a very neat jumper. When he needed to fiddle he fiddled and when I needed him he came up for me - Shane Quinlan, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: We've always thought a lot of him and pitched him in at the deep end last season. I'm still learning about the stallion. We thought we'd handle softer ground but he probably wants a sounder surface. He won on his final start last season and we gave him a tough assignment on his first start at Cheltenham. He was a bit outpaced but stayed on nicely and will have learned plenty. He then got stuck in the mud at Chepstow last time. We'll bide our time, wait for the ground to dry up and try to find the right race over hurdles. He's going to be a lovely novice chaser next season. 05-01-24

prev_owners.owner: Walters Plant Hire & James & Jean Potter

runners.comment: Seemingly nothing like the force of old; not proven beyond 3m either
runners.spotlight: Seemingly nothing like the force of old; not proven beyond 3m either, with heavy defeats on his only two attempts at 3m1f or 3m2f; the former was on latest start when beaten 46l at 150-1 in the Ultima at Cheltenham and all this season's form suggests he will be a big outsider again.

quotes.race: Matt Hampson Foundation Silver Trophy Handicap Chase (Grade 2) (A Limited Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We're pleased with that. Stolen Silver was fourth here at the festival and has come back and finished the season on a high note. He'll go out to grass now and we'll see what Sam [Thomas] and Dai [Walters] say but we could look at the October meeting, but certainly November - James Potter, part-owner.

quotes.race: Urbano By Symphony Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Stolen Silver didn't miss a beat with his jumping. He's very free-going and the ground helped him, he bounced off it - Charlie Deutch, jockey.

quotes.race: Sky Bet Supreme Trial Rossington Main Novices' Hurdle (Grade 2)
quotes.quote: I was worried about getting third place at the last with Stolen Silver but Sam got another gear out of him. He's a nice horse and the Betfair Hurdle might be his next race - Nigel Twiston-Davies, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's lost his way since the Coral Gold Cup last season but the ground has been quick both times he's run since, which he wouldn't have enjoyed. We're on a bit of a recovery mission with him at the moment, but he's sound and well and we may just have a spin over hurdles in the next two or three weeks on some softer ground. He's got lots of ability, we just need to recapture some form. 25-11-24

He's been a dude for the yard. We stepped him up in trip this season and he won the Native River Handicap Chase on his first start at Chepstow. He then ran well in the Coral Gold Cup and just found it all a bit too much pace wise. He needs to be in his comfort zone. He came back a little bit sore. He's a lovely horse to aim at some of the big handicaps this campaign. 05-01-24

prev_owners.owner: Exors Of The Late Trevor Hemmings

runners.comment: First home in Grand National Trial at Haydock (3m4f) last February; disappointing of late
runners.spotlight: The way he asserted in the Grand National Trial at Haydock (3m4f, good to soft) last February made this race look an appealing proposition, but he faded badly when it was put to the test and later lost the Haydock race due to a banned substance; this season has been very disappointing but at least he's 9lb lower than 12 months ago and his yard has been in great form.

quotes.race: Oddschecker Grand National Trial Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Famous Bridge was only ticking over when he unseated last year. He's always been a grand horse, a good stayer who'll stay all day. He'll miss the cut for the National this time, which is a shame as we'd love to go to Aintree. Hopefully it might be next year. He could be one for the Scottish National but he wouldn't want it too fast. He'll probably go to Cheltenham now. He ran a good race in the Ultima last year and is probably just coming to himself now - Nicky Richards, trainer.

quotes.race: Betfred Tommy Whittle Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Famous Bridge is hard to beat when he gets in a battle. Sean said he always thought he was going to win from the second-last. He's a grand horse. I don't know if we'd want to run him on that ground too many times, it's fairly gruelling and he's a youngish horse. He wouldn't be one for the Grand National this season. I want to keep seeing a bit of improvement. Something like the Grimthorpe might be for him - Nicky Richards, trainer.

quotes.race: bet365 Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Famous Bridge was about to get involved when he unseated Brian two out here last time. He's done a good bit of schooling since and was a lot more professional today. There are a couple of handicaps for him at Aintree - Nicky Richards, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He has done very well for us in the past but was a bit disappointing in the Tommy Whittle at Haydock. Everything's in the melting pot at the moment - we're just having a think. He has run a couple of below-par races this season, so we're just going to see how it pans out over the next three or four weeks.
