He's on a good mark now but Haydock was disappointing and that's about as much as you can say. 31-12-25

runners.comment: A rising force, likely to prove well handicapped if he gets this trip, which is feasible
runners.spotlight: Half-brother to top-class Protektorat; made three notable steps forward on varied ground over 3m at Ascot this season, including for a good prize on latest start when he led two out for a clearcut win; raised another 4lb but he's a rising force, likely to prove well handicapped if he gets this trip, which is also feasible; on the shortlist.

quotes.race: Full Circle Series At Punchestown Festival Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: I was really disappointed with Montregard at Newcastle but I think the cheekpieces have helped him here and he's toughed it out well - Tom Lacey, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's a nice horse of JP McManus's who won his maiden at the second attempt over hurdles when last seen at Warwick in April. I was really pleased with him that day; he was green but toughed it out and stayed on nicely. I'd say he's progressed through the summer and is set to return in a 0-105 handicap hurdle at Uttoxeter on Friday. He'll ultimately jump a fence too. A nice prospect. 20-12-23

runners.comment: Shaped as if he stayed when third of five over 3m4f at Haydock last time; wind op since
runners.spotlight: Missed 2024 and came up a bit short in his six races since, sent chasing for his five starts this term; shaped as if he stayed when third of five on the step up to 3m4f at Haydock last time but he needs much better than that; perhaps the subsequent wind surgery (his second) will help his cause.

quotes.race: Winners Wear Cavani Sefton Novices' Hurdle (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I wouldn't change anything. Maximilian has run a great race. That will be it for the season and we'll concentrate on next year now. He's a very exciting horse; second in a Grade One, and on another day? He's given the winner seven pounds, and it was a good try - Donald McCain, trainer.

quotes.race: Albert Bartlett River Don Novices' Hurdle (Grade 2) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I nearly walked away because Maximilian wasn't going but he just saves plenty for himself. We went down to Sandown, the ground was like glue and he hated it. He had a bit of blood in his nose but I think that was because he was hating the ground and not going. But he was still third in a Grade 2 and we've always had a lot of faith in him. But he's never going to do anything flash. I'm not a massive Cheltenham fan. Aintree is our muckheap and he's had a hard enough race today so I'd think that would be first choice. Donald McCain, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He came back later last season and although the plan was to go novice chasing, there were a lack of options so we went over hurdles. Having his first run for nearly two years at Chepstow carrying top weight in a big field was never going to work out great, but I still was very disappointed, although the vet said he choked on some kickback. He then had entries but the ground went everywhere. He's been in fast work for a little while and he's working well and we're ready to go novice chasing when we get slow ground. There are very few miles on the clock and he's a very talented horse. 30-10-25

I have always thought he was well above average and he has done nothing to dampen my enthusiasm in his six career starts, with five wins. I was disappointed with his third at Sandown in the Grade 2 Winter Novices' Hurdle in December but he had his excuses as the ground was horrible. We raised him in trip last time at Doncaster for the Grade 2 River Don Novices' Hurdle and he got back on the winning trail in a race that looked pretty smart. He cruised up, but as ever as soon as he got a length up he thought to himself “that's enough”. But that is his way - he will never win by far, but so long as he keeps winning that does not matter. Before Doncaster I spoke to his owners and the consensus was that we would give Cheltenham a miss and head to Aintree. I am looking long term and I think Cheltenham is not going to help in that department. Of course we could change our minds nearer the time, but I am minded to head to Aintree at this stage. 09-02-23

runners.comment: No win since 2022; while easier to envisage him as a stayer, this race is so much tougher
runners.spotlight: Ex-Irish 11yo (five races for current yard) who has not won since July 2022 but nearly put that right in first-time cheekpieces (kept since) over 3m2f at Newbury in February, losing out in the final strides; second of three at Ascot (3m) three weeks ago was creditable in the end, after he'd been detached at one point, and that helps to envisage him as a stayer, but this race is so much tougher.

quotes.race: Guinness Galway Blazers Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: I thought Gabby's Cross was fantastic there. He's a funny sort of a horse but he relaxed lovely today and he did it really well. He's quite quirky at home and he can be difficult to ride but the lads have done a brilliant job with him in Knockeen - Rachael Blackmore, jockey.

quotes.race: BetVictor Novice Handicap Chase (Grade B)
quotes.quote: Gabbys Cross really tanked with Rachael but she settled him. I was thinking of the novice handicap chase at the Punchestown festival for him - Henry de Bromhead, trainer.

quotes.race: Shop Local Online Rated Novice Hurdle
quotes.quote: Gabbys Cross got a great ride from Rachael. He was a bit weak last year but seems to be really improving this year. There is a novice handicap hurdle at Leopardstown which we will look at is he's eligible - Henry De Bromhead, trainer

stable_tour.quote: Hopefully he can win off his hurdles mark soon. He ran really well at Galway and the plan is to go for the Pertemps qualifier at Punchestown this coming weekend. 20-11-23

runners.owner: R A Bartlett/J Carthy/Mrs Paul Shanahan
runners.comment: Passed a lot of rivals to finish fourth of 23 in the 3m2f Kim Muir at Cheltenham
runners.spotlight: Ex-French 6yo who has shown promise in defeat in his four starts for this yard; latest was the Kim Muir at Cheltenham (3m2f, good; acts on soft) in which he was joint-second favourite, never posed the slightest threat to the front two but passed nearly all his other rivals to finish fourth of 23; whether he's battle-hardened enough for this is a question but there's very little doubt that he remains capable of better.

stable_tour.quote: He'll likely turn up in one of the Cheltenham Festival handicap chases. He ran a great race at the Dublin Racing Festival and was the only one who was up with the pace who hung on. He's run well at Cheltenham in the past. 19-02-26

runners.comment: Too often disappointing in major long-distance handicaps for him to be greatly fancied
runners.spotlight: Won the Somerset National over an extended 3m2f at Wincanton in January 2025 and second in the Welsh National Trial at Chepstow in December this term; he also showed last season that he stays 3m4f but there have been too many disappointing shows in major long-distance handicaps for him to be greatly fancied for this one.

quotes.race: Hinton Workspace Somerset National Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: We're delighted with Collectors Item. Maybe something like the Eider could suit him, but there are plenty of options. Kev gave him a lovely ride with plenty of positivity, which he responds quite well to. His jumping was better towards the end and he didn't put in any short ones - AJ O'Neill, joint-trainer.

quotes.race: Coral Get Closer To The Action Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Collectors Item is not the biggest but he looks like an athlete and he will gallop all day long for you. The ground has been too dry for him and Jonjo said how he won over two miles he will never know as this is his trip. The ground was too quick for him at Cheltenham last time but he stayed on all the way up the hill. He really pinged the last and he's run right to the line. We will look at the EBF Final at Sandown with him now but he needs to qualify for that so we will look at a little qualifier in February - John Goodman, spokesman for the winning owners.

quotes.race: Chepstow Plant International Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Collectors Item did it nicely, he jumped and travelled well. I'd say he's a nice horse to look forward to. He ran well in a nice bumper at Newbury and it's worked out quite well so you never know. He took to it well and he'll be a nice chaser - Jonjo O'Neill, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: We're aiming towards the London National at Sandown on December 6, a race he finished second to Mr Vango in last season. He's best with some cut in the ground and is well suited to a test of stamina. 18-11-25

runners.comment: The key to him is soft ground; third in this race in 2024 and in Midlands National latest
runners.spotlight: The key to him is soft ground, on which he was third in this race in 2024 and had for the first time since over fences when third of 16 off today's mark to Isaac Des Obeaux in the Midlands National at Uttoxeter (4m2f) on latest outing; blinkered on last two outings; each-way claims.

quotes.race: racingtv.com/freetrial Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Git Maker is certainly going the right way. He's learning with experience and it was another lovely ride from Gavin, so fingers crossed he progresses. These novice handicap chases seem to suit him well, and I might give him an entry into the Midlands National and have half an eye on that. It's taken a bit of time for him to take to his jumping, but he's improving and getting the hang of it - Jamie Snowden, trainer.

quotes.race: Join Racing TV Now Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Git Maker is a lovely young horse and we've been crying out to go three-mile chasing with him. It was great that he won three hurdle races last season but he's a proper staying chaser. Like Park This One, he's not flashy but the harder the race the better he'll be-Jamie Snowden, trainer

quotes.race: Play Coral Racing Super Series For Free Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race) (Div I)
quotes.quote: We've always really liked Git Maker and he finished second to Up For Parol, whom we like, in a point-to-point. Staying chasing is where he's going and on this testing ground as he's got a high-enough knee action. We'll tip away gently this season and go chasing in the autumn. He definitely wants to go up in trip, but the fact he can do that over two miles is a bonus. He's a nice horse and we'll probably keep him to two miles on galloping tracks - Jamie Snowden, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's been a star for us. He was second to the subsequent Gold Cup winner in the Kim Muir last year and then came third in the Scottish National, but it didn't happen for him this spring. He'll have one run over hurdles and then go for the Welsh National. He loves soft ground. 05-11-25

This lad is a proper staying chaser and I expect races such as the Midlands Grand National to be right up his street. He had a niggle in his back last season so his campaign was cut short and he didn't run after winning at Catterick in January, but he's 100 per cent now. He'll be ready for the depths of winter as he loves soft ground and he'll stay any trip you want. 28-09-23

runners.comment: 2-4 chasing; remains capable of better and could stay beyond 3m; ran respectably on soft
runners.spotlight: Chasing on last four starts, winning on good ground at Taunton (2m7f) on first and latest; overcame interference to oblige in eventually clearcut fashion in a small field on latest, so surely remains capable of better (up another 3lb since) and that suggested he could stay beyond 3m; this is his first attempt to do that and this 6yo ran respectably on soft ground on penultimate start.

stable_tour.quote: He didn't run badly at Cheltenham but it was a bit disappointing. I think we'll switch him to chasing now - we've schooled him over fences and he's gone quite well, so that looks a nice option. 20-11-25

runners.comment: Upped to 3m4f when he scooted clear at Leopardstown (3m4f, yielding to soft) last time
runners.spotlight: 9yo who is well related (half-brother to Kildisart and The Big Breakaway) but very lightly raced for his age; remote second of 17 at Navan (3m, heavy) in his first handicap chase, which he followed with much better form to win 13-runner Dublin National at Leopardstown (3m4f, yielding to soft) last time, scooting just over 6l clear on the run-in; has a much higher British mark today but also untapped potential and he's one to consider.

quotes.race: Dublin National Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: I was worried about the ground going to Navan but Promontory handled it better than we thought he would. The plan was always to come here for this race but I thought he wouldn't have the experience to go and win a handicap like this without having that run under his belt. He doesn't travel really well but he jumps well and I knew he'd stick at it. We'll have a look and see where we go next - Sarah Connell, trainer.

runners.owner: CW Racing Club & Ursa Major Racing

prev_owners.owner: Ursa Major Racing, Cw Racing & Partner

runners.comment: Winning 3m races this season and a lot suggests that a major test of stamina will suit him
runners.spotlight: Three wins (wore cheekpieces for last two) and a second from his last four starts, all over about 3m/3m1f; unraced beyond that but there's a great deal about him which suggests that he won't really come into his own until handed a major test of stamina; he receives one today and, despite the step up in class, consequently makes serious appeal.

quotes.race: Mark Nield Wealth Management Go North Red Rum Series Final Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Chasingouttheblues loves a horse to aim at. He wants far further and he's a Nationals horse. We might have a crack at the Scottish National if there's a bit of give, he wouldn't run on quick ground. He's improving. This track suited him better than last time, when he wasn't quite right - Tim Walford, trainer's father.

quotes.race: William Hill Racing Bet Builder Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: When the horse fell in front of me Chasingouttheblues did well to stand up and I thought we'll just get balanced again and jump the last three, there will be another day.  Then he started to pick up and I thought he was going to be a good third. He winged the last and I thought he was going to be a strong finisher.  But when he's won previously he's been off it turning in and kept going. I was outpaced turning in today but it all worked out in the end, with a bit of luck on our side - Jamie Hamilton, jockey.

quotes.race: William Hill Proper Prices Novices' Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Chasingouttheblues won his novice at Hexham and this was a big step today. He's a chaser for the future and we were thinking of going straight over fences but we may give him another spin over hurdles - Mark Walford, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: We paid £22,000 at the recent Doncaster Sales - he was our pick of the sale - for myself and Mark [Walford] and he's definitely one for the notebook for the winter when he comes out in novice hurdles. 14-06-24

runners.comment: Won Edinburgh National in 2023 and 2025; fifth in this race in 2023; needs a second look
runners.spotlight: Won the Edinburgh National over an extended 3m7f at Musselburgh in 2023 and 2025 (both good to soft); creditable fifth in this race in 2023 but pulled up in it last year and has not recaptured his form in his only two starts since; given a wind operation since latest and it helped when he had one in 2024; needs a second look.

quotes.race: bet365 Edinburgh National Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It's really nice to get Magna Sam back. He had some issues last season, we were just missing something. We did it [his wind] after his break and obviously it's showing dividends now. He had a little blow at the back of two out at Doncaster and it was a nice confidence-booster for him - Alastair Ralph, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's entered in the Eider on February 21 but he's ground dependent for that. He'd need the rain to stop and for it to dry up a bit, but that's his next logical target. Unfortunately, he missed the Edinburgh National, which he's won twice, but hopefully he'll go in the Eider. We'll probably need a few to come out but we'll see. 12-02-26

racecards.verdict: King Of Answers may be best of those who ran at Cheltenham, but Montregard and CHASINGOUTTHEBLUES (nap) are preferred.
racecards.betting_forecast: 4/1 Kim Roque, 11/2 King Of Answers, 6/1 Chasingouttheblues, 13/2 Montregard, 15/2 Promontory, 9/1 Isaac Des Obeaux, 11/1 Quebecois,  Git Maker, 16/1 Kap Vert, 20/1 Herakles Westwood, 25/1 Our Power,  Katate Dori,  Famous Bridge,  Maximilian,  Blaze The Way, 33/1 Gabbys Cross, 50/1 Collectors Item, 100/1 Stolen Silver

racecards.race_name: Stagecoach Your Designated Driver Novices' Hurdle (Winners Of One) (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Easy hurdle debut win here for Noel Kelly; leading claims on first run for Gordon Elliott
runners.spotlight: Easily won a bumper at Listowel (2m4f, yielding) last September and same outcome on hurdle debut here (2m4f, soft) in February on final run for Noel Kelly; leading claims on first outing for Gordon Elliott.

quotes.race: Every Race Live On Racing TV Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: He's a lovely horse and we've always thought a lot of Apache Tribe. He won his bumper very nicely. This was the prep run and we'll be heading to Cheltenham for the Albert Bartlett. The further he goes the better. It's good to bring him over on the boat to Ayr and get him used to travelling, as he's quirky enough - Noel Kelly, trainer

runners.breeder: E A R L Haras D'Enki
runners.owner: M Buckley, C Noell And M Hankin
runners.comment: Pulled up in EBF Final but promising previously and could bounce back with big performance
runners.spotlight: Pulled up on handicap debut at Sandown (2m4f, soft) last month but that was the competitive EBF Final; promising previously, finishing first at Hereford (2m3f, good to soft) and second at Ascot (2m5f, soft); with a top trainer and could bounce back with a big performance.

quotes.race: Betwright Bangers N'Cash Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Laguna Beach's jumping was a bit untidy at Sandown, which was disappointing, but he improved plenty and was slick today - Nicky Henderson, trainer.

runners.breeder: E A R L Du Loisir
runners.comment: Easy win at Doncaster on second hurdle start and this likeable prospect is one to consider
runners.spotlight: Bought for £160,000 after going close in sole point and left last October's hurdle debut well behind to post easy win in a maiden at Doncaster (2m3f, soft) in February; this likeable prospect is one to consider.

runners.breeder: N J Henderson And Mrs S A Aston
runners.comment: Well held at Cheltenham in December but could be capable of considerably better
runners.spotlight: Runner-up on debut in Listed bumper (2m1f, soft) and won his next two, latterly his hurdle debut at Ffos Las (2m, soft) in November; finished well held in Cheltenham novice (2m1f, good to soft) in December but could be capable of considerably better, with the step up in trip a possible plus.

stable_tour.quote: He could be our best novice hurdler. He's certainly the speediest, and he did nothing wrong last season despite being a big, backward thing. He looks great this season. 07-11-25

runners.comment: Impressive when winning over 2m3f here in February and he's entitled to respect
runners.spotlight: Bumper winner (2m1f, good to soft) who got off the mark over hurdles at the third attempt over 2m3f here (soft) in February; he was impressive on that latest outing and is entitled to respect.

runners.owner: Times Are A Changing Racing Syndicate
runners.comment: Solid form, including a win at Navan, and this Irish challenger could be thereabouts
runners.spotlight: Point winner who scored on hurdle debut at Navan (2m6f, soft to heavy) in January; third of five in Grade 3 at Gowran Park (2m7f, heavy) next time before close second in Navan novice (2m6f, soft); this Irish challenger has some solid form and could again be thereabouts; races prominently.

quotes.race: NavanRacecourse.ie Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: He hasn't been in Andy's [Slattery] that long but what we've seen of Timesareachanging we liked. The bumper run was a good one, we were happy coming away from it as the ground was so dead. We were confident of a good run today. He idled away in front, he only gives you what he has to, it was a good performance - Philip Donovan, jockey, speaking to Racing TV

runners.comment: 2m runner-up here; further improvement needed today but the step up in trip could help
runners.spotlight: 3m point runner-up who was well beaten here on bumper debut in January but took a big step forward when runner-up in maiden hurdle here (2m, soft) next time; further improvement is necessary in this warm novice but the step up in trip looks a positive move and he's not discounted.

runners.comment: 12l third in Grade 2 novice at Kelso in February and he's firmly in the picture
runners.spotlight: 0-8 but placed in three maiden hurdles in a row (2m-2m5f, soft) prior to 12l third Grade 2 novice at Kelso (2m2f, good to soft) in February when 33-1; receives weight from his main rivals and is firmly in the picture.

stable_tour.quote: You'd have to be encouraged with him and I've been very pleased with all of his runs. He was second first time out in a bumper at Kempton last February, showing promise behind a nice horse of Keiran Burke's. We then pitched him in a bit high in his two subsequent bumpers - a Listed bumper at Ascot and then one at Newbury, but his hurdle runs so far this season - two at Newbury and one at 21-01-26

runners.owner: They Are Never At Home Partnership
runners.comment: Point winner & maiden hurdle runner-up; lots to find but very unexposed and in good hands
runners.spotlight: Won mares' maiden point last March (3m, soft) on her second start; following an absence she was a promising second on last month's hurdle debut at Hexham (2m4f, soft); she has lots to find in today's company but is in good hands and it's possible she'll take a sizeable step forward.

stable_tour.quote: She won a point-to-point for Aidan Fitzgerald in Ireland and came recommended. We picked her up at the sales. She wasn't expensive and should prove to be good value and a bit of fun. She'll ideally start in mares' novice hurdles or just in novice hurdles. 19-11-25

racecards.verdict: Having been seriously impressive on his final two runs for Noel Kelly, APACHE TRIBE is taken to make a winning start for Gordon Elliott.
racecards.betting_forecast: 13/8 Apache Tribe, 9/2 Stride On,  Timesareachanging, 11/2 Our Boy Stan,  West Hill Verde, 12/1 Laguna Beach, 16/1 Allfor, 33/1 Queens Secret

racecards.race_name: Golf Inn Prestwick Luxury Accommodation Open National Hunt Flat Race (Cat 1 Elimination) (GBB Race)

runners.comment: First and second over C&D; should go well again even though rider cannot claim this time
runners.spotlight: Both bumper runs have been over C&D; made winning rules debut in November (soft) and bumped into a useful type when second under penalty in January (heavy); should go well again even though rider cannot claim this time.

runners.comment: Big-money buy after Irish point win and followed up in bumper here; useful prospect
runners.spotlight: Changed hands for £220,000 after winning an Irish point, and he followed up over C&D (soft) on rules debut in February; only scrambled home that day but the first two pulled clear; looks a useful prospect.

runners.owner: Mrs Diana L Whateley, McNeill & Stone Families
runners.comment: Made winning rules debut at Southwell in December; in good hands and open to improvement
runners.spotlight: Well backed and made winning rules debut at Southwell (good to soft) in December, leading over 1f out; the third won a bumper next time out; in good hands and open to improvement.

quotes.race: attheraces.com/marketmover National Hunt Flat Race (Conditional/Amateurs') (Cat 1 Elimination) (GBB)
quotes.quote: That was good. Old Habits is a lovely big horse who's had little racing and we'll probably go softly, softly with him for a little while yet as he's not had much racing and needs to learn what he's doing. His jumping was very good and I'm delighted by that. He had a look at the last but he'd been surrounded by horses all the way around until then. But I wouldn't worry about that. He's a lovely backwards horse who doesn't need rushing at the moment - Olly Murphy, trainer.

runners.comment: Unbeaten in point and bumper in 2025; changed hands for £205,000 in between; promising
runners.spotlight: Unbeaten in point (soft/heavy) and bumper (good/yielding) in 2025, making all and pulling clear final 1f at Down Royal on second occasion; changed hands for £205,000 in between; clearly a promising type and his owner and trainer combined to win this race two years ago.

quotes.race: WTW Willis INH Flat Race
quotes.quote: Skerry Hill is a lovely horse. He's a baby and green, but we like him. We think he's a nice horse. You probably won't see much more of him this year, he's a big chaser - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: A very nice horse. You could do a lot worse than remembering this guy's name. He impressed me when he won his point for Cormac Abernethy and seems to do everything right. He's one we're looking forward to and he'll start off in a bumper soon. 26-10-25

runners.comment: 11,500euros 3yo; rare runner in Britain for stable that does well (18%) in Irish bumpers
runners.spotlight: 11,500euros 3yo; Wings Of Eagles half-brother to point winner Crocodile Lounge; dam 2m5f hurdle winner; rare runner in Britain for a stable that does well (18%) in Irish bumpers and had the runner-up in these colours 12 months ago.

runners.comment: Irish point winner; runner-up on C&D rules debut; bred to be suited by 2m4f+ in due course
runners.spotlight: Bought for £130,000 after winning Irish point on good ground; left behind last 2f when second on rules debut here (soft; 7-1) in January; bred to be well suited by 2m4f+ in due course.

runners.breeder: E A R L Les Bordes De Mornay & M Gerard Hanquiez
runners.comment: Second to the smart No Drama This End at Warwick; long absence since but retains potential
runners.spotlight: Cosy winner of Irish point and followed that with a most encouraging second to the smart No Drama This End in bumper at Warwick (soft); that was on New Year's Eve 2024, so clearly things have not gone to plan since, but he's in very good hands and retains potential.

stable_tour.quote: He's another nice novice hurdle prospect who finished second in his bumper last December. We thought he might win that day as he'd been doing everything well at home, but he came up against a nice horse [No Drama This End], so we weren't disappointed. He looks every inch a stayer who has a real long-term future as a chaser. I think I'll be very excited about him this time next year. 10-11-25

runners.comment: Shaped well behind Champion Bumper fourth at Down Royal; respected but this is quite warm
runners.spotlight: Runner-up to a subsequent rules winner in point last spring, and shaped quite well behind the subsequent Champion Bumper fourth at Down Royal on Boxing Day; should be up to winning a race but this is quite a warm one.

runners.breeder: Ecurie Cerdeval , Mme Valerie Aumont, Mr
runners.comment: Not beaten far on either start in bumpers and remains open to progress
runners.spotlight: Half-brother to high-class staying jumper Gaillard Du Mesnil; not beaten far on either start in bumpers, leading and keeping on well at Wincanton (good to soft) six weeks ago; remains open to progress.

stable_tour.quote: He's by a top French sire who is getting stacks of winners either side of the Channel. Judged on his work this autumn he's going to be one of our better bumper prospects. Ascot on Saturday due to the ground but we'll find another race shortly. 04-11-25

runners.comment: Close second at Punchestown and Limerick (Listed race); clear top of the pile on ratings
runners.spotlight: Beaten less than 1l at Punchestown (soft) in February and Limerick (soft/heavy; Listed race) in March, rallying after being unable to quicken on second occasion; yard has a well-above-average strike-rate in British bumpers; clear top of the pile on ratings and should go well.

runners.comment: First foal of an unraced mare; stable isn't known for bumper winners
runners.spotlight: First foal of an unraced mare; stable isn't known for bumper winners.

runners.comment: Promising third at Southwell; stable's few runners here do well; may be the answer
runners.spotlight: Related to several useful performers and he shaped very nicely when a close third at Southwell (soft; 6-1) two months ago, doing  his best work late on; the pair that beat him had experience from points; stable's few runners here do well; open to plenty of improvement and may be the answer in an open race.

racecards.verdict: The one that makes the most appeal is SEA TEMPEST, who shaped well behind two point winners at Southwell.
racecards.betting_forecast: 7/2 Brady Hartsfield,  Skerry Hill, 11/2 Keops Des Bordes, 13/2 Old Habits, 8/1 Sea Tempest, 10/1 Jardin De Tunis, 12/1 Coconut Man,  Close House,  Finisk Pride, 14/1 Le Cold Grey, 100/1 Busted Springs

racecards.race_name: Broxton Gates Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Very smart Flat horse; won at Musselburgh despite a slipping saddle
runners.spotlight: Very smart Flat horse for Andrew Balding; had wind surgery after his one blip over hurdles and then won at Musselburgh despite a slipping saddle (2m1f, good to soft); carries a penalty but looks a major player.

quotes.race: Racing Post+ Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Alsakib left his back end in the third-last and he was quite long at the last, where the saddle has gone round his side and I had to kick my other leg out or I was gone with it. I managed to keep the partnership and I managed to cling onto the weight cloth and the saddle. He had the wind done after fading at Catterick last time and went round there easily. I wasn't planning on making the running but he's taken me there and he's quickened up really nicely in the straight - Theo Gillard, jockey.

quotes.race: John Smith's Silver Cup Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.quote: When you get a chance to get on these horses you have to be so grateful and hopefully I can make hay now. Alsakib tested me a bit today, but we knew he'd enjoy the ground and would stay - PJ McDonald, jockey.

quotes.race: bet365 Old Rowley Cup Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
quotes.quote: Alsakib is a lovely horse who stays the trip well. I don't think he'll run again this season here. The owners wanted him to run in the Qatar Derby, which is over ten furlongs, and that's always been the plan in having him here with me. If he comes back after that then he has a lot of possibilities - Andrew Balding, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: A horse I bought this week at the sales - he ran in the Prix du Cadran for Andrew Balding. He's very useful on the Flat and has been bought to do to both jobs. He'll go jumping now and it's really exciting to get a horse of his calibre. 30-10-25

runners.comment: Has a chance on the figures back at novice level if he's back on song after last time
runners.spotlight: Advanced his form on his handicap debut when third of ten at Exeter (good to soft) but wasn't so good at Taunton (good); has a chance on the figures back at novice level if he's back on song.

runners.comment: Very opposable on his pointing exploits
runners.spotlight: Very opposable on his pointing exploits.

runners.breeder: V Adenot & P Adenot & F Vannereux
runners.comment: Latest RPR was nothing to shout about and he'll need more here
runners.spotlight: Respectable run at Sedgefield on the back of a wind operation but the RPR was nothing to shout about and he'll need more here.

runners.comment: Bumper winner but tailed off on hurdle debut after a mammoth absence
runners.spotlight: Won two bumpers, one in the pointing scene and the other under rules; however, finished tailed off in a 2m4f maiden hurdle at Sedgefield on the back of a mammoth absence.

stable_tour.quote: We put him in an online sale after his nine-length Newton Abbot bumper win in July but he didn't make the right money and stayed with us. He's well able to gallop and showed us what we'd been seeing at home. He's picked up a small issue but will be fine and is the other horse who might join Gozo in the US. He likes fast ground, being by Champs Elysees, and could pick up big money for winning a maiden hurdle out there. 30-11-23

runners.comment: Weak in the betting and tailed off on hurdle/stable debut at Huntingdon
runners.spotlight: Showed a nice of ability in bumpers for former Irish yard but was weak in the betting and tailed off on hurdle/stable debut at Huntingdon.

runners.comment: Shown enough in bumpers to believe he can win races but perhaps not this one
runners.spotlight: Shown enough in bumpers to believe he can win races but perhaps not this one.

runners.comment: Market Rasen winner who was a late withdrawal from an Ascot handicap last month
runners.spotlight: Placed in two French Flat races; sent off evens when narrowly accounting for a useful rival in a Market Rasen maiden two months ago (soft) and was withdrawn with a self certificate from a traditionally strong 4yo handicap at Ascot last month; can go well.

quotes.race: Join Racing TV Now Juvenile Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Senator was a bit cold early but warmed to his task and after turning for home I didn't think the result was in doubt. A step up up to two and a half miles would be right up his street - Gavin Sheehan, jockey, speaking on Racing TV.

runners.comment: Hooded for hurdle debut at Haydock (good) and was tailed off under Harry Cobden
runners.spotlight: Placed in her second point; hooded for hurdle debut at Haydock (good; 14-1) and was tailed off under Harry Cobden.

runners.comment: Running well when unseating four out in an Irish point last month
runners.spotlight: Running well when unseating four out in an Irish point last month and clearly has a level of ability; market useful.

runners.comment: No sign of good Flat ability over hurdles and probably one for handicaps
runners.spotlight: 2-4 on the Flat for Karl Burke and quite useful; no sign of that ability over hurdles and probably one for handicaps.

runners.comment: Modest Flat maiden who offered little on hurdle debut at Huntingdon two weeks ago
runners.spotlight: Modest Flat maiden who offered little on hurdle debut at Huntingdon two weeks ago.

runners.comment: French winner on heavy; faded on soft at Wetherby; drier ground may help
runners.spotlight: Won a French hurdle on heavy ground; only 5-2 for British/stable debut but faded on the soft ground at Wetherby; these conditions may be more to her liking, for all that she has won in the mud.

racecards.verdict: Jamie Snowden's Market Rasen winner SENATOR was a late withdrawal from a traditionally strong 4yo handicap at Ascot last month.
racecards.betting_forecast: 5/2 Alsakib,  Senator, 4/1 Knock Off Soxs, 8/1 Tunisya, 10/1 Static Charm, 14/1 Anxious Moments, 20/1 Laristote,  Phantom Gold, 25/1 Saxon Cross,  Cappa Lass,  Chico Magnifica, 66/1 Karthala, 100/1 L'Hybris Is Born

racecards.race_name: Gieves & Hawkes Novices' Handicap Chase

runners.comment: Runner-up to well backed and well handicapped winners in last two races; big shout
runners.spotlight: Jumping has been an issue but it's improved in his last two races when runner-up behind winners who were well backed and well handicapped; has course form; big shout.

stable_tour.quote: He bumped into a fancied horse at Bangor last week. He's had a few issues with his jumping, with form figures of UUF before that run, and it was nice to have a clear round. The confidence he got from that should be immense. 08-04-26

runners.comment: Has become disappointing but his third at Hereford was better (3m1f, good)
runners.spotlight: Has become bitterly disappointing but handicapped accordingly and his third at Hereford was better (3m1f, good); cheekpieces are back on but they'd done little for him previously.

runners.comment: It was good ground when close up behind Streamsforth Lad over C&D last month
runners.spotlight: Rules wins (including one chase) came on soft or heavy but it was good ground when close up behind Streamsforth Lad over C&D last month; good chance.

quotes.race: Spa Motors Hereford Novices' Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: I think Subtle Fortune would have won anyway, but that was my first win against professionals, so it's nice to beat them - Darren Andrews, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: We had her through the point-to-point ranks and she proved she was worth investing in for her new owners when impressively winning a maiden hurdle at Uttoxeter last month. She's one who'll just carry on improving as she jumps well, and as time goes on she'll go over further too. There's lots to like about her and, having won two point-to-points, she could be even better over fences. 16-01-25

runners.breeder: Hoguenet, C Guy, Nbb Racing, C German
runners.comment: Running well when falling at Sedgefield, though he wouldn't have won
runners.spotlight: Lightly raced hurdler; ran well in his first chase and was doing likewise when falling at Sedgefield, though wouldn't have won; others preferred.

runners.owner: Genghis Racing & Mike Harris Racing Club
runners.comment: Experienced chaser and 4-15; a winner last time out over 2m4f; some stamina worries
runners.spotlight: Has more chasing experience than many of these and with a strike-rate of 4-15 things are going well; those wins have been from 2m to 2m4f so the are stamina questions to answer, for all that he has won a 3m point.

quotes.race: Best Odds Guaranteed At Betano Novices' Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: If you saw El Rojo Grande in the paddock he would've looked as fat as a pudding and when you see what he eats it puts you off eating porridge, but he's a big horse and that's how he wins his races. Shane rode him a bit more aggressively, I thought, and it worked well. That put the horses making their first start in a chase under pressure whereas he's had plenty of experience - Katy Price, trainer.

runners.comment: On a workable mark on the best of his hurdle form; quiet on chase debut; in cheekpieces
runners.spotlight: This is a workable mark on the best of his hurdle form (maiden) and, although disappointing on his chase debut, he did go off favourite; respected in the new cheekpieces.

runners.comment: Placed in last three hurdle races and clearly a contender if taking to fences
runners.spotlight: Bumper winner; brings momentum into chase debut after three consecutive placed efforts over hurdles, in this headgear combination in his final two races (2m3f/3m); clearly a contender if taking to fences.

stable_tour.quote: A lovely horse who is going to make a hell of a chaser. He had his first start over hurdles at Ayr last week and scoped dirty afterwards, so we didn't really learn anything. We'll build him back up and step him up in trip throughout the season. 20-11-25

He hasn't quite lived up to expectations yet. He still looks quite green and babyish. He's a chaser for next season but he'll have a couple more runs. We thought he'd win at Doncaster last month but the winner looked well handicapped and got away from him. Once he gets his head in front, he could win two or three on the bounce. He should be very well handicapped. 13-03-26

runners.owner: P Conway, T Lewis & G Wilson
runners.comment: More appealing than a good many after finishing runner-up at Hereford last time
runners.spotlight: Placed effort over hurdles (3m1f) divides his two chase runs and was a 3l runner-up at Hereford last time (2m5f, good); more appealing than a good many.

runners.comment: 21 defeats under rules include 13 over fences but he's been running better than most
runners.spotlight: 21 defeats under rules include 13 over fences but he's been running well, latterly finishing third on yard debut at Hereford (2m5f, good); stays this far.

runners.comment: Jumped moderately when beaten 25l on chase debut two runs back; poor since over hurdles
runners.spotlight: Jumped moderately when beaten 25l on chase debut two runs back and again well held over hurdles here when tried in a hood.

runners.comment: Only 1-8 in points; no worthwhile form under rules and now makes chase debut
runners.spotlight: Only 1-8 in points; no worthwhile form under rules and now makes chase debut.

runners.comment: In new cheekpieces when second to a thriving rival at Carlisle (3m, good)
runners.spotlight: In new cheekpieces when second to a thriving rival at Carlisle (3m, good) and won't be far away if as good again.

runners.comment: Showed a bit more last time when beaten 8l in a 2m6f handicap hurdle at Stratford
runners.spotlight: Eight-race maiden who showed a bit more last time when beaten 8l in a 2m6f handicap hurdle at Stratford; that was his first run in cheekpieces as well; chase debut.

runners.comment: Poor five-race maiden over hurdles; has won a point but unconvincing claims on chase debut
runners.spotlight: Poor five-race maiden over hurdles; has won a point but unconvincing claims on chase debut.

racecards.verdict: An open handicap. With his jumping improving STREAMSFORTH LAD has been running well behind winners who were well treated.
racecards.betting_forecast: 6/1 Streamsforth Lad,  El Rojo Grande, 7/1 Black Occ, 8/1 Subtle Fortune,  Sandscape,  Peckforton Hills,  Kapamazov, 10/1 Atlanta Brave,  Siege Of Acres,  Tory Hill, 14/1 Rockvale,  Harksman, 20/1 Huckleberry Sting, 33/1 Shuile Warrior

racecards.race_name: Bangor-On-Dee Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners.owner: Mrs G Van Geest & M George
runners.comment: Ran poorly in a Grade 2 over 3m last time but that couldn't have been his true running
runners.spotlight: Ran quite well at Ascot in November but the wide-margin Kempton win in February (2m5f, good to soft) is his standout piece of form; ran poorly in a Grade 2 over 3m last time but that couldn't have been his true running.

stable_tour.quote: He's every inch a chaser but will get started over hurdles this season. He was second in a point-to-point before coming here and then we gave him one run in a bumper at the back end of last season, when he finished third at Worcester. He'll probably start over two and a half miles. 21-10-25

runners.comment: 3-6 over hurdles and contender with sights lowered (pulled up in Albert Bartlett latest)
runners.spotlight: When a wide-margin Listed race winner at Doncaster it was against her own sex and very few in that eight-runner race appeared to handle the deteriorating conditions; went off 50-1 for the Albert Bartlett and performed accordingly; 3-6 over hurdles and she's a contender with her sights lowered.

stable_tour.quote: She's a nicely bred youngster whose dam is a half-sister to La Bague Au Roi. We really like her and have been delighted with her since buying her at the sales. She's another one in the Irish sales bumper. 12-10-23

runners.comment: Outclassed by the best of these judged on what he's shown in a bumper and two maidens
runners.spotlight: Looks outclassed by the best of these judged on what he's shown in a bumper and two maidens; the longer trip could help as he was second in an Irish point.

runners.comment: A remote third two weeks ago when returning from a long absence
runners.spotlight: Point winner but was tailed off on hurdle debut and then a remote third two weeks ago when returning from a long absence.

runners.comment: Impressed for the win but finished last in final two races, the latest a Grade 2
runners.spotlight: Won by a wide margin at Exeter (2m7f, good to soft) in November but has finished last in her subsequent races, latterly in a 3m Grade 2 (50-1); retains potential but has been off for nearly three months.

stable_tour.quote: She's a staying type, like so many of mine. She's won a bumper and over hurdles and next season will go novice chasing. She was trained in Ireland for her bumper win and then won a mares' novice hurdle at Exeter by 24 lengths for us. You can put a line through her run at Doncaster last month - she couldn't handle the horrible ground. She may have another run over hurdles when the ground dries out but it's all about staying chases next season and beyond for her. 25-02-26

racecards.verdict: None of these ran particularly well last time but RECKLESS SPENDING clearly failed to give his true running in a Grade 2.
racecards.betting_forecast: 6/4 Park Princess, 5/4 Reckless Spending, 6/1 Pottersville, 12/1 Johnny Moonshine, 20/1 Patrick's Wells

racecards.race_name: Keegans Independent Drinks Suppliers Handicap Hurdle (Div I)

runners.comment: His Newbury third gives him major claims but he's already looking hard to predict
runners.spotlight: Made mistakes when third in a Newbury handicap (2m, good to soft) but his Southwell run over 2m4f (good) was disappointing when tried in cheekpieces (persevered with); already looking hard to predict.

stable_tour.quote: He had one run in a four-year-old bumper at Punchestown for Jamie Sloan, when inexperience showed, and then he was put away for the summer and sent to us. He's benefited from that break and has come in as a really strong individual. He'll almost certainly go straight over hurdles and it'll be interesting to see how far he goes. 22-10-24

runners.comment: Maiden winner; up in trip for handicap debut and tries a tongue-tie after wind surgery
runners.spotlight: Hasn't kicked on from the maiden win at Kelso (2m, good to soft) but this is his handicap debut over a longer trip and he did beat the useful Swindon Village in an Irish point; tries a tongue-tie after wind surgery.

prev_owners.owner: Lord Daresbury & Ecurie Madame Jacques Cypres

runners.comment: He was on the retreat when falling in his second handicap at Newbury; lightly raced
runners.spotlight: Ex-French 5yo who remains lightly raced; he was on the retreat when falling in his second handicap at Newbury (2m, good to soft; Sutherland was third) but he ran well to a point and probably has a bigger effort in him.

runners.comment: In two runs for this yard he's been tailed off over hurdles and pulled up on chase debut
runners.spotlight: Has the form to feature off this mark but in two runs for this yard he's been tailed off over hurdles and pulled up on chase debut.

runners.comment: Improved second at Huntingdon and this mark might not be too bad for his handicap debut
runners.spotlight: The ground was heavy when showing improved form in a Huntingdon maiden (2m) two months ago but he might be improving anyway; this mark might not be too bad for his handicap debut.

runners.comment: Back to something like his winning form when second to an improver at Musselburgh
runners.spotlight: Has won a handicap, at Catterick on New Year's Day (1m7f, good); back to something like that form when second to an improver at Musselburgh (2m4f, good to soft); can go well.

stable_tour.quote: He won at Catterick and whatever he does over hurdles is a bonus. I think we'll see the best of him as a 2m chaser. He's such a fantastic and quick jumper, I can't wait to go chasing with him. He's an exciting one for next season. 28-01-26

runners.comment: Course winner; struggled in last three races and been all over the shop trip-wise
runners.spotlight: Course winner last February; bang there when falling two out on handicap debut at Kempton (3m, good) in November but she's struggled since and been all over the shop trip-wise.

quotes.race: Irish Thoroughbred Marketing Mares' Maiden Hurdle (Herring Queen Qualifier) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I should have won a bumper on I've Madeupmymind before this but she's a little terrier - Ben Jones, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: Between myself and Ben Jones we've messed it up a few times with this filly, but she's going to make into a lovely novice hurdler this season. She has the ability to win two novices and then we'll see where we are. 21-11-24

runners.comment: Hard to make a case after finishing tailed off when 40-1 for his handicap debut
runners.spotlight: Hard to make a case after finishing tailed off when 40-1 for his handicap debut (2m3f, soft; first-time tongue-tie); did show a smidgeon of promise on good ground last year but he's unconvincing.

runners.comment: Chased home an unexposed Henderson horse here last time; handicap debut
runners.spotlight: Useful bumper form on good ground, winning at Ludlow and sixth of 16 at Cheltenham (Listed); yet to replicate that over hurdles but chased home an unexposed Henderson horse here last time; handicap debut.

racecards.verdict: A chance is taken on THEY WANT ME who goes up in trip for his handicap debut on the back of a wind operation.
racecards.betting_forecast: 9/4 I've Madeupmymind, 11/4 Crack Ops, 9/2 Lejo Du Seuil, 5/1 They Want Me, 8/1 Sutherland, 14/1 Locquirec, 25/1 Vinnie O'Neil, 33/1 Shengai Enki

racecards.race_name: Keegans Independent Drinks Suppliers Handicap Hurdle (Div II)

prev_owners.owner: Lord Daresbury, Ecurie Mme Jacques Cypres & Nicolas Cypres

runners.comment: Unexposed but doesn't look obviously well treated for this handicap debut
runners.spotlight: French bumper winner; bled from the nose two runs ago and left that behind with a hood added (retained) when springing a 33-1 surprise in a Sedgefield maiden hurdle (2m1f, good) last month; unexposed but doesn't look obviously well treated for this handicap debut.

stable_tour.quote: He came over from France and was going to run for us at the end of last season, but the ground went against him. He'll be running soon and we'll try to win a couple of races and then go somewhere nicer. He's from the same stallion as Homme Public and is very much like him - tough not flashy. 20-11-25

We really like him. He's got loads of ability and has just had a few niggly problems. So it was really good to see him land a maiden hurdle on Tuesday at Sedgefield, where he exceeded expectations. His confidence should be back and he can go on to better things. 13-03-26

runners.comment: Recent maiden winner; not the biggest but well bred and obvious claims on handicap debut
runners.spotlight: It wasn't a strong maiden she won at Plumpton (2m4f, good) but she breezed home despite a late mistake; not the biggest of mares but well bred and should be able to cope with this opening mark.

stable_tour.quote: She's a half-sister to Doddiethegreat and won her bumper at Southwell in May very nicely. She's not terribly big, but she's tough, feisty and jumps very well. She wouldn't want the ground too quick. 21-10-25

runners.comment: No match for the winner on his handicap debut here but it was an encouraging effort
runners.spotlight: Second to recent Aintree winner Forthfactor on bumper debut; no match for the winner on his handicap debut over C&D (good) but it was a fair start to life in races of this nature; considered.

stable_tour.quote: He ran well in a bumper at Hexham in November when second behind Forthfactor. He was running well on his first start over hurdles at Uttoxeter but fell at the second-last. Stan Sheppard, who rode him, was absolutely convinced he was going to win but I'm less sure. He then ran poorly next time at Ffos Las, but I think he just got stuck in the mud. He's declared to run at Ludlow on Wednesday and we'll see how we go. He looks a nice sort and is my choice for a dark horse. 18-02-26

runners.horse: I C U In My Dreams
runners.comment: Made all in latest maiden; this mark no gift but open to further improvement
runners.spotlight: Another handicap debutante who looks progressive having had a Newcastle maiden (2m4f, good to soft) sewn up some way out; this mark isn't a gift but open to further improvement.

runners.comment: In good form in handicaps prior to chase debut latest; since had wind surgery
runners.spotlight: Had a wind operation since pulling up on chase debut last time (first-time cheekpieces now dispensed with); bumper/hurdle winner who had been in good form in handicaps prior to that.

quotes.race: Advertise Your Business At Huntingdon Racecourse Conditional Jockeys' Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: Tramuntana had been a bit keen in his races so we decided to drop him in. It wasn't much of a race but he'll make a lovely chaser one day - Olly Murphy, trainer.

quotes.race: Save Our Sport Sign The Petition "Newcomers" National Hunt Flat Race (Cat 1 Elimination) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Tramuntana had been going well at home and is well bred so that was no surprise. He enjoyed himself out there and it was the perfect introduction - Fergus Gregory, rider.

runners.comment: Juvenile hurdle winner; departed early on handicap debut did go off at only 9-4
runners.spotlight: Easy winner of a Haydock juvenile hurdle and then fourth in another when penalised; departed early on handicap debut at Sedgefield (2m1f, good; first-time cheekpieces) when strong in the betting at 9-4; has to be of interest.

stable_tour.quote: A tough little horse who has done well this season, including winning at Haydock in December. He'll jump a fence next season. 13-03-26

runners.comment: Hasn't looked devoid of ability and could take a step forward now into handicaps
runners.spotlight: Hasn't looked devoid of ability in bumpers or over hurdles and could take a step forward now into handicaps.

stable_tour.quote: He could be a very nice horse in time. He's really quite keen and he pulled too hard in bumpers, but the hurdles have helped him settle and he's starting to grow up. He'll go to Bangor at the end of next week and we're pleased with him. 08-04-26

runners.owner: Exors Of The Late Mr A Rutherford

prev_owners.owner: Exors Of The Late Mr A Rutherford

runners.comment: 66-1 when fifth in a C&D maiden here last month when about 10l behind Good Boy Griff
runners.spotlight: 66-1 when fifth in a C&D maiden here last month when about 10l behind Good Boy Griff; he wouldn't be the obvious answer.

runners.comment: Encouraging handicap debut 14 days ago after an absence; should be sharper now
runners.spotlight: Only had six races and the latest on handicap debut was after an absence of 837 days; shaped well at Carlisle (2m3f, good to soft), finishing 14l off the winner after getting outpaced; should be all the sharper now.

racecards.verdict: Easy Plumpton winner EREMENKO is a close relative to the smart Doddiethegreat and she can make a successful handicap debut.
racecards.betting_forecast: 3/1 Eremenko, 4/1 I C U In My Dreams, 5/1 Titanium Ring,  Diamond Jim, 7/1 Las Canals,  Tramuntana, 14/1 Good Boy Griff,  Hang On, 20/1 Gimarias

racecards.race_name: Broxton Gates Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners.comment: In good form last year but since turned 12 and lacking a run might not be ideal
runners.spotlight: Returned to winning ways at Uttoxeter (2m4f, good) last summer and remained competitive afterwards; however, he has since turned 12 and lacking a run might not be ideal.

quotes.race: Price Promise At bet365 Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It has taken Presentandcounting a while to get his confidence back after a fall at Ayr in the spring, but he was entitled to win like that with his rating. He will stay three miles so I was keen to make it a test - Brian Hughes, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: He's a fine-looking, talented horse with a good pedigree who's still very raw. He raced a bit back to front at Cheltenham and you can't do that round there. I think the only thing that will steady him is a fence. He's done a lot of schooling over them and I think that's what we'll do now. He wouldn't want bad ground. 09-11-20

Our biggest earner so far this season and most prolific with four wins. He did us proud last summer, when among his wins was the valuable Fixed Brush Hurdle Series Final at Worcester in September. Last time out he finished third in the Grade 3 Persian War Hurdle at Chepstow, after which we gave him a well-deserved break, but he is back now and will be ready for when we get the better ground. He will have a busy spring and if I can get him there I know his owners, The Turner Family, would love him to run at Cheltenham. That will be the plan and we would be looking at something like the Coral Cup or Martin Pipe Hurdle, but after that I think he could go chasing again. 09-02-23

runners.breeder: Exors Of The Late Michael Lysaght
runners.comment: One of his better runs when beaten 14l here last time but not the percentage call
runners.spotlight: Ex-Dan Skelton; went close on yard debut in December (2m4f, heavy) but then twice pulled up and was beaten 14l here 18 days ago (good); wouldn't be the percentage call.

stable_tour.quote: He ran very acceptably at Newton Abbot first time up last month over a trip that was plenty far enough. It was the first chance I'd had to get a run into him, given the ground, and I think he could be winning again soon over a slightly shorter distance. 12-11-24

He was second on his first run for us at Uttoxeter in December but he's been quite disappointing since. He's bled a couple of times and we're just trying to work him out. He ran well at Bangor last week and hopefully that's a step forward. 08-04-26

runners.comment: Winner three starts back; back down in grade and with blinkers given a go, he's feared
runners.spotlight: Won at Uttoxeter (2m4f, soft) in January when wearing first-time cheekpieces (retained) and subsequent defeats have come in better races than this; didn't run at all badly in the latest at Kelso (2m5f); back down in grade and with blinkers given a go, he's feared.

quotes.race: Champion Equestrian Juvenile Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: My Noble Lord is a nice horse and he jumped really well. He'll be better suited by a more end-to-end gallop. He has a good attitude and should come forward from this - Jonjo O'Neill Jr, jockey.

quotes.race: Masons "Who Dares, Gins" Handicap
quotes.quote: My Noble Lord will just keep getting better and better. He's 540kg so he's a big unit that'll improve as he fills his frame hopefully.  We'll try him over further again. He was beaten over a longer distance at Wetherby, but he'll stay well. The ground is key, he wouldn't want summer fast ground. We don't have anything specific in mind, but there's that race at Haydock. Realistically he's not a July or August horse, though, so we could have a break - Michael Bell, trainer.

quotes.race: Download The Racecourse App Raceday Ready Handicap
quotes.quote: My Noble Lord has done well from two to three. He has a massive frame, he's taken a while to fill out and he's relished every inch of the mile and a half. I'd think he'll really start to flourish when we get him on some soft turf at a galloping track - Hector Crouch, jockey, speaking on Sky Sports Racing.

stable_tour.quote: He's going chasing and we'll try to benefit from his four-year-old allowance. He's jumping very well and looks really sharp. We've always thought a lot more of him than what he's shown. We're hoping he wasn't quite firing last season because he was a bit weak. 20-11-25

He ran as flat as a pancake last time at Newcastle in a better race and he'll come down in grade a bit now. He won the time before at Uttoxeter and has had a pretty good novice chase season overall. He's probably still got a bit in hand. 13-03-26

runners.comment: Close 4th after a wind op last time; burning question is whether he'll be as good again
runners.spotlight: Some lengthy breaks in his lightly raced profile but it was a positive first run back from wind surgery when beaten 3.5l at Uttoxter three weeks ago (2m4f, good to soft); the burning question is whether he'll be as good again.

stable_tour.quote: He won on his hurdling debut at Ffos Las and was second under a penalty at Ayr, trying to give 7lb to Jet To Vegas, who won a Grade 2 at Kelso and was fourth in a Grade 1. He's off a mark of 122 and there should be an awful lot more to come from him over a fence. We'll start off over two miles on soft ground. 05-11-25

runners.comment: This mark isn't beyond him and returning to a left-handed track looks a good thing
runners.spotlight: Dual Fontwell winner and his other victories have come on left-handed tracks; hung in that direction on last month's visits to Kempton and he duly underperformed; should run better around here and this mark isn't beyond him.

quotes.race: Chailey Classic & Vintage Tractor Club Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: They went far too fast in front and the race just fell apart, so I doubt the form will stand up. Freddie did ride a really nice race, though. Jorebel has been a fantastic horse and owes us nothing. He's great to train and very straightforward - Chris Gordon, trainer.

quotes.race: Bet Clever BetGoodwin Conditional Jockeys' Novices' Limited Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: I'm so sorry about that. I looked behind me and all I could see was a loose horse [Graham], and the one behind me [Hill Station] was covered by that loose horse. I looked at the screen and realised there was another one next to me. Coming to the line it was sickening because there was a big delay and I didn't know if I'd won or not. For a horse, it's good for them to have a nice time rather than being slapped down the shoulder and given a push. For Jorebel's sake, I was trying to give him a nice time because I thought I was so far ahead, but I wasn't - Freddie Gordon, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

stable_tour.quote: We've had a great time with him, winning four races since September. I think because our horses weren't in great form last season, they're all quite well handicapped. He has been very tough a few times - once when Freddie thought he'd won quite cosily and eased down and another horse came to get him. Jorebel did very well to pick up and just win it. He had a real good scrap at Worcester when he came out on top and another at Lingfield last time on his first run over fences. It wasn't the strongest race and hopefully the handicapper won't be too silly about it. He pulled clear with another horse who had very little form. It's down to the handicapper really whether he can win another one. He looked at the end of his tether the other day, but naturally you'd like to see him find more improvement with more experience of jumping. 01-12-25

runners.breeder: Earl De Cordelles & Earl La Dariole
runners.comment: First three handicap runs all positive and latest run was after a break; chase debut
runners.spotlight: Combination of handicaps, a wind operation and this headgear has made a different, delivering form figures of 132 in 2m5f-3m handicap hurdles before faring less well after 97 days off at Wetherby; hard to be confident on the back of that but no surprise should he run well now his attention is turned to fences.

runners.comment: This looks stronger than the race in which he ran second at Hexham
runners.spotlight: On a good mark but hard to predict and this looks stronger than the race in which he ran second at Hexham.

quotes.race: Colin Hawkins (Jockey) Memorial Handicap Chase (Go North Monet's Garden Series Qualifier)
quotes.quote: We had a couple of entries in this race and were keen to run something. Carrigeen Castle looks a progressive horse. He'll probably have one more run then we'll look forward to next season with him - Micky Hammond, trainer.

runners.comment: Bought for £10,000 in July and hasn't recaptured her best form for new yard
runners.spotlight: Won three small-field chases at up to 3m1f for Dan Skelton; bought for £10,000 in July and hasn't recaptured her best form for new yard.

stable_tour.quote: She won her maiden very well and has been second since to two nice horses. She'll go into handicaps, where she'll continue to pay her way, and she'll jump a fence in time. 12-11-24

racecards.verdict: Another trappy handicap. MY NOBLE LORDs is downgraded this afternoon and a change of headgear worked wonders three starts ago.
racecards.betting_forecast: 9/4 Duel Au Soleil, 100/30 Admiral Stewart, 9/2 My Noble Lord, 11/2 Doyouknowwhatimean, 7/1 Jorebel, 12/1 Lady Jago, 14/1 Presentandcounting

racecards.race_name: Overton Handicap Hurdle

runners.comment: Had long spell on the sidelines before struggling in both runs this winter; lots to prove
runners.spotlight: C&D winner who is well treated on his old form but he had a long spell on the sidelines before struggling at big prices in both runs this winter; hard to know how much ability remains and he has plenty to prove.

quotes.race: bet365 Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Hillview picked up well and is a strong stayer - he likes to be ridden that way. He was 9lb out the handicap but just keeps improving - Sean Bowen, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: He tweaked a suspensory so we had to stop with him. He's on his way back now and wants fast ground. At his age I'm not sure whether he'll be able to come back to his level of form. 08-04-26

runners.comment: Second in both runs for current yard including a close call over hurdles latest; respected
runners.spotlight: Multiple winner for the Newland/Insole yard; good second over fences on stable debut at Hereford (3m1f, soft) in February and he backed that up with a close call over hurdles at Wetherby (3m, good to soft) last month; 2lb higher here but he remains feasibly treated and won't mind what the weather does; respected.

quotes.race: Sky Sports Racing HD Virgin 535 Open National Hunt Flat Race (Category 1 Elimination) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: That was very straightforward. Dr Newland was quite keen to keep it simple, there was no pace so Tiger Orchid could go forward and do it himself - thankfully he's kept his head in front - Sam Twiston-Davies, jockey.

runners.comment: Record of 1-9 over hurdles but he had a near-miss at Hereford (3m2f) latest; key player
runners.spotlight: Record of 1-9 over hurdles but he found more improvement with a near-miss in a Hereford handicap (3m2f, good) last month; nudged up 2lb but he's building up a solid profile in staying handicaps and is a key player.

quotes.race: Birchwood Kia - Chichester, Driven By You Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We'll keep Dwight K Schrute on the go for the next 6-8 weeks but he'll have a break over the summer before going over fences next season - Jamie Snowden, trainer, talking to Sky Sports.

stable_tour.quote: He's an English point-to-point winner and won nicely in a novice hurdle at Fontwell last season. He ran well under a penalty when third at Worcester last month over two miles seven furlongs and he stays well. I'm looking forward to seeing him over a fence, and he should be nicely handicapped to progress. 05-11-25
Another who has joined us from the point-to-point sphere, where he won his sole start. He was ridden by Freddie Mitchell, who used to be my assistant and he recommended him to us. 28-09-23

prev_owners.owner: Mrs R Treacy & Mrs T J Kidd

runners.comment: Has won three of his last five and was as good as ever when scoring over 3m last time
runners.spotlight: Veteran who has won three of his last five starts and was as good as ever when scoring on the step up to 3m at Wincanton (good) last month; up 4lb but he should have more to offer over staying trips and he's an interesting contender.

prev_owners.owner: A J Wall, Briton International & Partner

runners.comment: Lightly raced 7yo but he's been well held in last three handicaps; blinkers are now tried
runners.spotlight: Won a novice hurdle at Chepstow (2m, heavy) last January but he's not really gone on from that and has been well held in his last three handicaps; still has low mileage but he needs improvement back up in trip; first-time blinkers replace cheekpieces.

stable_tour.quote: He ran well to finish second on his debut in a bumper in March and will start off in a maiden hurdle. He should develop into a lovely staying chaser. 24-10-24

runners.breeder: C Quellier, A Quellier & S Quellier
runners.comment: Ended last year with a win at Musselburgh (2m4f); respected upped in trip on his return
runners.spotlight: Has a patchy record but he made it 2-10 over hurdles when justifying support at Musselburgh (2m4f, good to soft) in November; 6lb higher on his return but that was a comfortable success and he looks worth a try at this new trip; not ruled out.

quotes.race: Blantyre Canter - Sponsored By Cleartech Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Speed Davis won a point-to-point, he won his bumper and he was second last time at Catterick. He was a bit novicey at times but he jumped well - Brian Hughes, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: His form has worked out well. We were a bit disappointed he didn't win over the summer and we've had his wind done. He'll make into a nice middle-distance novice hurdler/novice chaser. 12-11-24

runners.comment: Ties in with Dwight K Schrute on Hereford form and has claims if he can back that up
runners.spotlight: Ex-Nicky Henderson; just 1-10 over hurdles and has struggled with consistency but he ran well to finish third at Hereford (3m2f; first-time blinkers) last month; ties in with Dwight K Schrute on that form and has claims if he can back that up.

quotes.race: Trustatrader Apply Today Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race) (Div II)
quotes.quote: Nico (de Boinville) has just said Kintail is a work in progress and we are getting there with him. He is a lovely big baby. Like all those Blue Bresil's he has a laid back attitude to life. He would have learned a lot from. He is still looking around at everything that was going on, bar what was important. He will want to go do that again. All the two mile three-furlong race does is jump one hurdle in the back straight and then you are on the two-mile start. That was barely a two-mile race to me? They were going slowly over the first and to me it was like a two-mile race, but they didn't go a two-mile pace. I think the ground is quite hard work.?I wouldn't take away anything from Kintail. He just needs to learn a bit. The form of his bumper has worked out well and I think quite a lot of him as well - Nicky Henderson, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He won twice early last season, but we had to be patient with him later in the campaign. He wasn't 100 per cent in March, like many of our horses, and we had him all ready for weeks after that but the ground was too quick. We didn't take the chance and I'm sure that will pay off as he's going well now and has a big future. 22-10-24

runners.comment: Back from long absence with two tailed-off efforts and she's untried at this trip
runners.spotlight: Sole win was in a Haydock maiden (2m3f, good to soft) in April 2023 and she's finished tailed off in both runs since returning from a long absence in December; has plenty to prove and she's untried at this trip.

quotes.race: Happy Birthday Caroline Dingwall Mares' Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Golden Glance is an improving mare. She has form behind Greyval of Fergal O'Brien's - she was still a bit green that day and she's improved again today. She might go to Cheltenham for a mares' race - Henry Brooke, jockey.

runners.comment: Hexham specialist who has been well held in his last two runs and others are preferred
runners.spotlight: All three hurdle wins have been on slow ground at Hexham (2m7f) and latest was in October; only 2lb higher than for that success but he's been well held in his last two starts; may have needed the run at Carlisle last month but this is competitive and others are preferred.

racecards.verdict: Top of the list is DWIGHT K SCHRUTE (nap) who has been progressive in handicaps and was only just caught over 3m2f last time.
racecards.betting_forecast: 5/2 Dwight K Schrute, 100/30 Speed Davis, 9/2 Tiger Orchid,  Kintail, 6/1 Our Dylan, 10/1 Carismatic Soldier, 20/1 Robert d'Ores, 25/1 Golden Glance, 40/1 Hillview

racecards.race_name: Family Funday On 16th May "Junior" National Hunt Flat Race (Category 1 Elimination) (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Ran better than the bare facts on Warwick debut and he should know more this time
runners.spotlight: Out of a half-sister to three useful winners notably Stellar Notion (bumper and 2m-2m7f jumps); well-held fifth at Warwick (good; 13-2) last month but he ran green when it came to the crunch and should know much more this time; looks a likely improver on his second start and he's not ruled out.

runners.owner: Berkshire Parts & Panels Ltd No1 Fanclub
runners.comment: Promising third on Aintree debut but he's not gone on from that; bit to prove
runners.spotlight: Made a good start at a biggish price when third at Aintree (2m1f, good to soft) in November; had tough assignment in Listed bumper at Cheltenham in January but he was well below form again at Hereford (2m, soft) the following month; still early days but he has some questions to answer.

runners.comment: 38,000euros 3yo; yard 0-20 in bumpers in recent years and he could be one for later on
runners.spotlight: 38,000euros 3yo; fourth foal; half-brother to bumper/2m3f hurdle winner Just Golden; dam unraced half-sister to bumper and smart jumps winner O O Seven; stable 0-20 in bumpers in last five seasons and he could be one for later on.

runners.comment: Yard 21% in bumpers in recent years and he needs watching in market on debut
runners.spotlight: Seventh foal; dam bumper and 2m4f-2m5f hurdle/chase winner, half-sister to winners Rattlin (bumper and 2m4f-3m1f hurdle/chase) and Spud (bumper/2m hurdle); yard 21% in bumpers in recent years and he needs watching in market on debut.

runners.owner: Julie And David R Martin And Dan Hall
runners.comment: Turned over at odds-on on Doncaster debut but he travelled well for a long way; in the mix
runners.spotlight: 115,000euros 3yo; held in third of six when odds-on at Doncaster (2m, good to soft) last month but he travelled smoothly for a long way before his effort flattened out; that was an encouraging start and he's a player if he can build on that.

runners.comment: Promising third on Hereford debut and he should benefit from that experience
runners.spotlight: Market springer into 9-2 at Hereford (2m, soft) in February and he came from off the pace to finish a 2l third of ten; that was a promising debut and he should benefit from that experience; in the mix.

runners.owner: Mr And Mrs J D Cotton
runners.comment: 110,000euros 3yo; yard 25% in bumpers this season and he's an interesting newcomer
runners.spotlight: 36,000euros foal, 110,000euros 3yo; fourth foal; brother to point/2m4f hurdle winner Freshers Week; dam twice-raced sister to smart 2m2f-3m chase winner Gold Present, out of unraced half-sister to high-class 2m1f-2m5f hurdle/chase winner Rajdhani Express; yard 25% in bumpers this season and he's an interesting newcomer.

runners.comment: Brother to a useful hurdle winner and he needs checking in market on debut
runners.spotlight: Fifth foal; brother to useful 2m hurdle winner Llandinabo Lad, half-brother to winners King Of Tara (2m hurdle/chase) and Legendary Rhythm (2m hurdle/2m4f chase); dam placed in bumper, half-sister to useful 1m2f/1m4f winner Pentatonic; yard has had a debut bumper winner this season and he needs checking in market.

runners.comment: 80-1 and he finished a remote eighth on his debut at Southwell (2m, soft) in February
runners.spotlight: 80-1 and he finished a remote eighth on his debut at Southwell (2m, soft) in February.

stable_tour.quote: He's showing us plenty and we think he's a nice horse. He's had a bit of a break since his debut in a bumper at Southwell in February. He scoped dirty afterwards but he's back working really well. We were thinking of going to Aintree but we'll probably keep him in shallower waters until he gets his head in front. There's a bumper at Bangor at the end of next week. 08-04-26

runners.comment: Promising third on Kempton debut in February and he sets the standard on that form
runners.spotlight: Frontiersman gelding who made a promising start when a clear third at Kempton (2m, good; 17-2) in February; that was behind a useful prospect who was well backed and he sets the standard on that form; respected.

runners.comment: 36,000euros 3yo; has fair standard to aim at on debut and market should guide
runners.spotlight: 9,000euros foal, 36,000euros 3yo; tenth foal; half-brother to winners Last Garrison (1m2f-1m4f; RPR 68), Hyden (1m4f; 66), The Nutcracker (1m2f Flat; useful 2m hurdle) and Big Dispute (bumper); dam 5f 2yo winner (67), half-sister to 5f-6f winner Rigid Rock; has fair standard to aim at on debut and market should guide.

runners.owner: Sheep As A Lamb Syndicate Gary Gillies
runners.comment: Has shown clear promise in all three runs including two bumpers this spring; possibilities
runners.spotlight: Runner-up over hurdles at Warwick (2m, good to soft) in November and she's returned after wind surgery with two frame efforts in bumpers this spring; was only beaten around 5l when fourth at Newton Abbot (2m1f, good) last time and she has improved with each of her three runs; possibilities.

racecards.verdict: Several have possibilities but the vote goes to Nicky Henderson's striking newcomer LONGLANDS. Enya is feared most.
