quotes.quote: Von Krolock wants good ground and he loved it out there tonight. He's an ideal horse for here over the winter and there is plenty of improvement in him - Tim Doyle, trainer.

runners.owner: Peter Crate And Gallagher Bloodstock Ltd

quotes.race: It's Time To Turn To talkSPORT Handicap
quotes.quote: Harry Brown is a 5f horse really but gets 6f around here. He did that well as he had a lot of weight and will be an interesting horse on the grass - Hayley Turner, jockey.

runners.owner: J May, R L Field, W Trenchard, J Pook

runners.breeder: Whitsbury Manor Stud And Mrs M E Slade
Scea Marmion Vauville, Ecurie Skymarc Fa

prev_owners.owner: Aj Racing G Kelleway N Sowerby D Beedle

quotes.race: Mira Showers Rain Supreme Handicap
quotes.quote: We certainly weren't expecting that. We thought Top Biller would run well as it was a weak race but Dylan gave him a fantastic ride in grabbing the rail. I really think the return to grass has helped as he was probably getting a bit bored of the all-weather - Shelley Birkett, joint-trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He ran really well last week at Brighton when he was unlucky not to win. The first-time blinkers helped him in the first part of the race more than anything as he wasn't getting into gear in enough time. He's well handicapped off his mark of 54 as he's a 65-rated horse on his day. He's been second on three of his last four starts and is unlucky not to have won by now, but he'll have his day. Five furlongs is too short for him and going up to 6f on a galloping track will suit him better. He may head to Carlisle on Friday and he'll be winning pretty soon. 30-05-24

prev_owners.owner: Exors Of The Late Earl Cadogan

runners.owner: T Beeches, C Stone, J Gallagher

quotes.race: Trustatrader Apply Today EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I took a bit of a gamble and ran World Of Darcy at Newmarket over seven furlongs because I felt that now's the time to decide what we're going to do with him. Luke [Morris, jockey] said drop him back to six and get him a bit of confidence because he's obviously had a few hard days at work and we picked this one. There's nothing wrong with him, but he's not very big. There's always going to be a doubt whether this horse trains on, but at the moment he eats well and works well. There's a winter campaign and I think that's what I'm aiming for. We've got a big entry at the weekend, but we'll look at that and decide what the ground does. We'll see how he recovers and then we'll make decisions - John Ryan, trainer.

quotes.race: Racehorse Lotto National Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: World Of Darcy is a good solid horse, he'll be winning plenty of races. He'll probably go for the Windsor Castle - Karl Burke, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: She's a cool mare. She won nicely under Jim Crowley at Lingfield in July. She likes a bit of cut and the rain-softened ground at Glorious Goodwood worked for her when she was second to the Cheveley Park horse Protest in a fillies' handicap on her next run. I remember the Racing Post did a feature on the unluckiest losers at Glorious Goodwood and she was put up in it. Then she was unfortunate the next time at Goodwood as she banged her head leaving the stalls when she went off favourite. The other day at Epsom it was a bit of a messy race where they couldn't work out if they were going far side or stands' side and she ended up in a sort of muddle in the middle. She was fourth At Kempton on Friday and I was very happy with that, she's going to fall into one before the end of the season. I was keen to run her on rain-softened turf but bizarrely we haven't had that for a while, but I think that hopefully before the end of the season she'll find a chance or two when the rain gets into the ground. The owners are keen to keep her in training because when you run like that in a Glorious Goodwood handicap you know that she's a well- handicapped mare even though she's getting on in age. She's paid her way this year and if we can get her back to the same race next year and get a little bit of luck along the way she'll be winning again. 15-10-25

quotes.race: 1xBet.ie Supports Irish Racing Gladness Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: I think Albert Einstein is a sprinter and that was a little bit of the reason he was here. It was a very tough call to run him in that ground against older, hardier horses. Obviously we just have to do the right thing by the horse. He's always found it very hard to go slow. Some horses find it very hard to go quick but he finds it very hard to go slow. Usually that kind of horse needs a very strong tempo early. The lads will decide but my initial thought is that he'll be coming back and he'll go sprinting. It's a very difficult thing to run against those horses in that bad ground. If you have an older, strong horse, they can maul a three-year-old. He was travelling very strong and in that ground you'd have preferred that he would be travelling a gear or two lower. He's naturally just not able to do that. His tempo is so quick; he is a very high-tempo horse. It was in the back of my mind that this is a big sprinter. Obviously, we'll go and talk to the lads and see what they want to do, but there is a very good chance that's [Commonwealth Cup] the route he's going to go. He will definitely have another run before the Commonwealth Cup. The sprinters are coming here [for a racecourse gallop] tomorrow - Charles Darwin, Brussels and a few others - they are all three-year-old sprinters as well and this fella will add into the mix there. This fella was always a bit different, but we'll see - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.

quotes.race: GAIN Marble Hill Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.quote: Ryan waited and got Albert Einstein to relax as best he could. When he pulled him out he said it took a minute for him to engage but he's a very, very fast horse. We were hoping it was going to be a fast-run race, which I thought it was, but Ryan said he would have liked them to go even faster. The plan was to come here and go to the Coventry. I was worried today because it was so windy and he's so sharp mentally but he had to run. If everything goes well I think he will go to the Coventry, but all those things are decided the week before Royal Ascot. I think his name was changed three times actually. Every time we named him I think Sue [Magnier] maybe thought the name wasn't good enough for him. I wasn't even sure what his name was because it was changed so many times. I'm delighted for the lads and he's very exciting - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He was a bit disappointing on Saturday, but he started off sort of three or four lengths off the leaders and nobody changed position. But Ryan said he was by no means unmanageable. Ryan felt they were going very slow, and he has a lot of pace on that bad ground. In the full light of day, you'd have to be happy enough. We'll see how he is over the next couple of weeks, and the lads will decide if they give him a chance at a mile or go back sprinting. We know if he goes back sprinting he'll find that very easy, if that's what they decide to do. 31-03-26

We don't know how good he is, but hopefully he's a colt we can be bold and ambitious with. He'll get a mile no problem and I think he's quite smart. 01-04-26

runners.comment: Money-spinner during a busy 2yo campaign but isn't sure to progress any further
runners.spotlight: Bargain buy at £33,000 as a yearling, and picked up almost £300k in prize-money during a busy 2025 campaign, including when landing the Two Year Old Trophy at Redcar (6f); ran respectably, amid trouble, upped to 1m at the Breeders' Cup; not certain to progress any further, however.

quotes.race: William Hill Two Year Old Trophy (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: Ardisia is such a trojan! He goes for it and I couldn't be happier. That's his tenth run and fifth win, with two thirds as well. Hugo [Palmer, trainer] said this morning he was in great fettle and goes on any ground - Jane Mairs, part-owner.We were drawn wide and I used up plenty of horse to get across but Ardisia travelled well and was only doing enough in the last 50 yards - Oisin Orr, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: He's been an absolute star, I can't remember having a two-year-old who won five races. He's tough and consistent and just a very likeable horse. He showed all those traits again in the Two Year Old Trophy at Redcar and we're going to roll on to the new conditions race on Champions Day. We're probably going to end up meeting the Mill Reef winner without a penalty. He'll go on any ground and he'll try his heart out. The stiffer 6f shouldn't be a problem as he only just got there over the sharp six at Redcar. 08-10-25

runners.comment: Quite a tidy success over 1m at Newbury in sole 2yo start; brings potential
runners.spotlight: Scored quite tidily at Newbury (1m, soft) in sole 2yo start; perhaps not crying out for this drop in trip, especially if the ground isn't so slow, and it should be noted that all of his future major entries are over middle distances; otherwise brings potential to Group level.

runners.comment: Won narrowly at Newbury on the same day that Gonna Fly scored in better style
runners.spotlight: Edged ahead inside the final half-furlong and did just enough at Newbury (6.5f, soft) on the same day that Gonna Fly won in better style over 1m; holds a 2,000 Guineas entry, unlike that rival, and is open to progress; bottom of this pack on bare figures as things stand, however.

runners.owner: Derrick Smith & Mrs John Magnier & Michael Tabor

prev_owners.owner: Derrick Smith & Mrs John Magnier & Michael Tabor
Mrs John Magnier & Michael Tabor & Derrick Smith

runners.comment: Success in the Jumeirah 2,000 Guineas took his record to 3-5; improving colt
runners.spotlight: Has shown further improvement at Meydan this year and landed the Jumeirah 2,000 Guineas (1m, good; Listed) by 1l most recently, taking overall record to 3-5; the form received a boost of sorts at Newmarket this week; sole Newbury effort, namely close second in strong maiden (6f) last May, has worked out very well; solid claims.

quotes.race: Jumeirah 2000 Guineas Sponsored By Emirates Holidays (Listed Race) (Turf)
quotes.quote: The pacemaker stepped on it a long way out and I was just trying to fill him up. I had to come a little bit wide into the straight but Title Role showed a really good attitude when I asked him, he really dug in. Simon and Ed's [Crisford] horses are in great shape and he's beaten two fairly good horses there - Ryan Moore, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

quotes.race: Jumeirah Guineas Trial Sponsored By DP World (Conditions) (Turf)
quotes.quote: A little worry was going up in trip but the way Title Role hit the line and galloped out, the trip was perfect for him. The [slowly run] race did suit him as he's a quick horse and the wide draw was on the only worry - James Doyle, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

runners.comment: Landed three major 2yo races prior to respectable effort in the Dewhurst; the form pick
runners.spotlight: Cracking purchase at 35,000gns as a yearling, and developed into a smart colt during a 2025 season that featured wins in three major 2yo races, notably the National Stakes at the Curragh (7f, yielding) where his gameness was confirmed; handled the July course at Newmarket in the summer but proved all at sea on the Rowley Mile in the Dewhurst, losing his unbeaten record (still ran respectably in fourth place); he's the pick on form and launches 3yo campaign in a race that his trainer's father Fulke won twice.

quotes.race: Goffs Vincent O'Brien National Stakes (Group 1) (No Geldings)
quotes.quote: Zavateri is a superstar ? he really is. He's come from a long way back and they've not been coming back from off the pace. Hats off to Charlie Bishop as there was no plan or pressure, and he sorted it out. I sent him to the July Stakes after his maiden and everyone thought I was mad, but he's just kept on improving. He definitely wants further as well, especially as he matures - Eve Johnson Houghton, trainer.

quotes.race: Coral Vintage Stakes (Group 2)
quotes.quote: Zavateri is just so tough, he had to win his race twice. He went to win it and then William [Buick] came at him so he had to win it again. He just amazes me, he's such a dude and a lovely horse. He cut through the pack like a knife through butter - Eve Johnson Houghton, trainer.

quotes.race: Kingdom Of Bahrain July Stakes (Group 2) (Colts & Geldings)
quotes.quote: Zavateri and Havana Hurricane [winner of the Windsor Castle Stakes at Royal Ascot] are different horses and never work together - this one probably wants seven now, maybe a mile, and Havana Hurricane wants five or six furlongs. They don't win nothing at home so we don't do very much but they are both really, really nice horses. I think Zavateri could stretch out to a mile next season, he's got the pedigree for it. I love this horse, I always have done. Everyone said why don't you go for a novice but I said why do you want to go for a novice and get beaten with a penalty by a Group horse? Come to a Group race. I am Eve Johnson Houghton with 80 horses - not John Gosden with 150 or whoever but he [Zavateri] is one of the nicest I've had and he's done nothing wrong so far - Eve Johnson Houghton, trainer.

quotes.race: Clive Cox Racing British EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands B/C/D) (Qual') (GBB/IRE Inc) (Div II)
quotes.quote: Zavateri did it really nicely. He is still a big, green baby, but I'm very happy with the way he did it. Ascot is coming up a bit quick, so that's unlikely, but maybe we'll find something at the July meeting for him - Eve Johnson Houghton, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's a really nice horse who won impressively on his debut at Salisbury this month by two and a half lengths. We'll probably go to the July Stakes next at Newmarket. It's hard to win a novice with a penalty and he was so impressive at Salisbury that we might as well go to Newmarket. 02-07-25

racecards.verdict: The thoroughly likeable ZAVATERI sets the standard. Title Role and Albert Einstein are likely to be the biggest dangers.
racecards.betting_forecast: 2/1 Albert Einstein,  Zavateri, 6/1 Title Role, 10/1 Alparslan,  Needle Match, 11/1 Gonna Fly, 16/1 Ardisia, 33/1 Aqpan

racecards.race_name: Dubai Duty Free Finest Surprise Stakes (Registered As The John Porter Stakes) (Group 3)

runners.comment: Flopped on soft ground on final start; could be on the premises if resuming on song
runners.spotlight: Pipped in the Deutsches Derby (1m4f) last July before landing a 1m4f Group 3 at Leopardstown and 1m3f Group 2 at Longchamp; flopped on soft ground on final start but he should not face that here and, despite giving weight all round, could be on the premises if resuming on song.

quotes.race: Boodles Chester Vase Stakes (Group 3) (Colts & Geldings)
quotes.quote: Convergent has run a lovely race and is very much a work in progress. He's a horse for next season as well as this one. He's been running over shorter trips and was keen over the first couple of furlongs, then he got into a rhythm. Turning in I thought we'd win, before I thought we'd get run out of it, and then he's stayed on again. We know he stays a mile and a half well now and we're very happy for the future. I couldn't be happier without winning - Karl Burke, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's really exciting as his homework is telling us he's improved again. He finished off the season in good form, bar his last start in Germany when it was one race too many. He wants just good ground and not fast, and he'll probably start off in the John Porter at Newbury or the Alleged at the Curragh. The Coronation Cup would definitely be a target. 31-03-26

runners.comment: Four Listed wins before he added a Group 3 success in Bahrain 15 days ago; needs extra
runners.spotlight: Four Listed wins before he added a 1m4f Group 3 success in Bahrain 15 days ago; stacks of smart form in his lengthy career and none of it better than that latest start, but a bit extra will be needed to win this.

quotes.race: Get Best Odds Guaranteed At BetVictor Steventon Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: We bought Phantom Flight for the Bahrain International and just wondered whether he'd end up being rated high enough but he certainly will be now. He looks a really exciting recruit and the boss, Shaikh Nasser, gets all the credit. He lets me try and find horses wherever I can and he's so supportive and willing. He came to me in great condition and James Horton did a great job with him last year. We'll work back from Bahrain and I was thinking about the Ebor before then but the handicapper will have his say now. I'm going to have to slightly reevaluate now but he's a serious horse - George Scott, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: His first preference is the Golden Gates over a mile and a quarter. He's hit the line well in all his races and the longer trip may eke out a bit of improvement, which we'll need. He's done little wrong and if he gets a nice draw he could be competitive. He's only had three runs but he's sensible and relaxed and he's straightforward in his races. 08-06-22

runners.comment: Eight Group 3 wins, almost as good as ever with his two last term; sets the standard
runners.spotlight: Held up; eight Group 3 wins are already in the bag, including this race in 2021 (his only appearance in it); has a slightly mixed reappearance record but he was almost as good as ever with his two wins last term, including first time out, and a return to that level would make this 9yo the one to beat.

quotes.race: Coral Glorious Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.quote: Al Aasy is terrific isn't he? He's pretty reliable in this grade when things set up like that. They didn't go very fast today - he usually likes a stronger pace - but they picked up well up the straight and he found a gear. He actually ran on strongly today - he usually wins by half a length or a neck. He's been called some names in the past but I wish people would respect him for what he is - he's a very talented horse but you just need to wait, and wait and wait. I think he enjoyed a bit of cut in the ground today as well - William Haggas, trainer, speaking to Racing TV.

quotes.race: bet365 Gordon Richards Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.quote: We knew Al Aasy was in good form and he has looked great all winter. He is paying us back for looking after him in his earlier years and is just a lovely horse to have about. I think Jim [Crowley, jockey] has really got the hang of him by just waiting and waiting and the mile and a quarter pace suited him better. I was worried he might be too fresh but Jim gave him a beautiful ride. I think a both a stiff mile and a quarter and a mile and a half suit him. We'll look around and find something for him - Maureen Haggas, trainer's assistant.

quotes.race: BetVictor Geoffrey Freer Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.quote: Al Aasy has always been talented and has probably been better since being gelded. It was great for him there, it was easy. He's a dude at home now. It's only four weeks since he had his first run here, with Goodwood in between, which is a big ask, especially having had some time off like he has but you couldn't have passed up an opportunity like this. He's seven-years-old and it's time to get to work really.  He enjoyed it today. It was a good pace, which he enjoys. He's run over all sorts of trips, from a mile and a quarter up to a mile and five furlongs. He likes a good pace. He used to be very keen at home. He's not as keen but can still be strong when he wants to - Maureen Haggas, wife of trainer William.

quotes.race: Coral Glorious Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.quote: It was a messy race. We went very steady. I got a bit closer at the top of the hill and then I was quite happy when he was in a pocket. William [Haggas, trainer] said to ride him for luck and, if it opens up, it opens up. We just needed that gap and I was very fortunate to have got up the rail. There wasn't a lot of room up the rail but Al Aasy was very brave. Once he was in there, it was game over really. He's just as good over this trip as he is over a mile and a half. He's been a bit unlucky because that's his run style. He's been called a few names in the past for not being a battler. He's just one of those horses who has to be produced at the last minute - Jim Crowley, jockey.

quotes.race: Betfred Rose Of Lancaster Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.quote: Al Aasy has always been a talented horse and bringing him back to a mile and a quarter has been a good thing, he gets the trip well and he travels really well. He looked as though he was enjoying himself today. The horse has been unfairly criticised, since he's been gelded we've never really classed him as ungenuine, he's been unfortunate once or twice. Although he's old he's a bit like Hamish, there aren't many miles on the clock - Maureen Haggas, trainer's wife.

quotes.race: bet365 Stakes (Registered As The Steventon Stakes) (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: That's very satisfying for everyone involved with Al Aasy. They badgered me to run him over a mile and a quarter. I wouldn't do it but I finally succumbed and clearly, now aged six, that's his trip. They go a bit faster and that helps him to relax. He did it comfortably today. Physically, he's been a battle, and mentally he's not straightforward either. He's had a couple of injuries but he's coming. He still doesn't look right in his skin but he's coming. He'll go for the Rose of Lancaster at Haydock, a Group 3 over a mile and a quarter on August 12, next - William Haggas, trainer.

quotes.race: Carey Group Buckhounds Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: You could say that Al Aasy should have won the way he won because he's only just been beaten in a Group 1, but I thought Dane [O'Neill, jockey] gave him a brilliant ride and he did it nicely. He had a nice, easy run around and it'll have done his confidence the world of good because that's what he needs. That's half the battle with him really because he's got stacks of talent. In terms of where we go next, that'll be a discussion we have but he's got options - Maureen Haggas, trainer's wife.

quotes.race: Qipco Champion Stakes (British Champions Middle Distance) (Group 1)
quotes.quote: I'm sorry that Al Aasy never ran at all - William Haggas, trainer.

quotes.race: Al Rayyan Stakes (Registered As The Aston Park Stakes) (Group 3)
quotes.quote: Al Aasy won very well and liked the ground. He settled well and I can't really say anything else because he looks like that at home. He's a talented horse. He's done well this year and we'll find out in the Coronation Cup, which is where he'll run next. He's in everything and we've put him in the Arc, but that's a long way to go. I fancy a mile-two, but I'm not sure, and there are some fantastic races at a mile and a half. If he's going to run in the Arc he'll need a break and I wasn't planning to run him after the John Porter until Epsom, but he was too well - William Haggas, trainer.

quotes.race: Bahrain Trophy Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.quote: William has always liked Al Aasy - he's a beautiful horse, and he's bred to be a good horse. He ran really well first time last year and we were really disappointed when he ran like he did at Newmarket and we don't know why, perhaps it was rustiness. He did what he needed to do last time and he's improving and learning. When he won last time this was the race William wanted to go for, but I don't know what's next. I'd think a well-run mile and a half would suit him best, he's not slow, and ideally faster ground than today. I think the Great Voltigeur would be the likely next step - Maureen Haggas, wife of William Haggas, trainer.

runners.comment: Ran well only once last term; gelded since; ring-rusty on 2025 reappearance in this race
runners.spotlight: Won Group 2 at Newmarket (1m4f, good) last May in first-time cheekpieces, which were kept for two modest efforts in June but not today; first run since a gelding operation in September; ring-rusty on his 2025 reappearance in this race and the market may reveal whether the same is expected this time.

quotes.race: Betfred Jockey Club Stakes (Group 2)
quotes.quote: Bellum Justum is a high-class horse and had got some good form from last year. Obviously, the second is a very good horse as well. I am delighted because he was a big disappointment in the John Porter and it's just nice to see him back on track. I think the cheekpieces helped and it was an excellent performance. He has had a hard enough race today and I think we will probably wait for the Hardwicke now. It will nice to have runners with a chance for King Power at the Royal meeting - Andrew Balding, trainer.

quotes.race: DK Horse Nashville Derby Invitational Stakes (Grade 3) (3yo) (Turf)
quotes.quote: Bellum Justum absolutely flubbed the start. I was way too far back, but lucky Jamie [Spencer, on pacesetting Navy Seal] was so fast. On the back straight, I was able to make good improvement to get a slot, because I knew he would stay very well. I knew he'd gallop out to the line because he stays a mile and a half - Frankie Dettori, rider.

quotes.race: Betfred Blue Riband Trial (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: Bellum Justum showed some promise last year but had a little setback about a month ago. I think he is bound to come on for the run and we thought that whatever happened today, we would go to the Dante Stakes next and see where we are with him. Obviously, I need to talk it over with the owners but if all goes well there then the Derby would be the plan - Andrew Balding, trainer.

quotes.race: British Stallion Studs EBF Maiden Stakes (Colts And Geldings)
quotes.quote: Bellum Justum was very professional and it's great to have a winner for King Power. He'll probably have another run this year in something like the Autumn Stakes here next month - Sam Geake, trainer's assistant.

runners.comment: In the mix judged on peak efforts but there are plenty of lesser shows to be considered
runners.spotlight: Not discredited in Qatar in February on latest outing and in the mix judged on peak efforts, including a Newmarket Listed win (1m4f) last September; however, there are also plenty of lesser shows to be considered.

quotes.race: BOYLE Sports Smart Race Card Godolphin Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: I didn't expect Lion's Pride to win quite like that but he's always been a talented horse and I'm delighted for his owner breeder Anthony Oppenheimer. We could have a look at the Listed races on the all-weather this winter and maybe Saudi Arabia if we get invited - John Gosden, joint-trainer.

quotes.race: Racing TV Floodlit Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: We didn't go overly quick, but I was happy with the way Lion's Pride jumped up two gears really quickly at the bottom of the straight. He won the race there and was still strong at the line. We've always thought a lot of him and he's had excuses for when he's been beaten. He had good horses like Middle Earth behind him when he won here before, so he's a nice horse - Rab Havlin, jockey.

runners.comment: A strikingly mixed bag last term but it included two Group 2 wins, one after he was gelded
runners.spotlight: Started last season with a big win in the Group 2 Dante at York; tailing off in the Derby and Irish Derby showed another side to him but he was gelded afterwards, posted a career-best effort to win the Group 2 Great Voltigeur at York (1m4f, good to firm) next time and was not discredited in Bahrain on final outing; big player if he resumes in good heart.

quotes.race: Sky Bet Great Voltigeur Stakes (Group 2) (Colts & Geldings)
quotes.quote: Pride Of Arras is back to his best, in fact it was probably better than his best. I actually brought him here slightly underdone, as we only gelded him in July the week after the Irish Derby and it's only seven weeks on. I've only really done maintenance stuff with him and haven't turned the screw because that seemed to suit him the last time we brought him here and because I wanted him to run well more than anything else. Really, we came with no expectations. We'll probably have to end up travelling, but I won't be averse to that. I'd be tempted to think about California and Hong Kong. The nature of those races will suit him really well. The flat tracks suit him great. I wasn't at all happy with how he moved during the first half a mile at the Curragh, which isn't exactly undulating anyway. He just wasn't enjoying himself any more that day than he was at Epsom. This place suits him and gives us a steer for the future - Ralph Beckett, trainer.

quotes.race: Betfred Derby (In Honour Of His Highness Aga Khan IV) (Group 1) (No Geldings)
quotes.quote: It looks as if Pride of Arras didn't come down the hill. He came on the bridle at the top of the hill but then he was on the wrong leg and it was the wrong way round so it was all over - Ralph Beckett, trainer. Pride Of Arras was very inexperienced for this track. He wasn't comfortable coming down the hill - Rossa Ryan, jockey.

quotes.race: Al Basti Equiworld Dubai Dante Stakes (Group 2)
quotes.quote: Pride Of Arras is not Westover, he's not Bluestocking. He does have a very good back pedigree but he doesn't have perhaps the profile of those when it comes to pedigree. But he has more speed than Westover did and he's a better workhorse. It's all in front of us, I hope. If he handles Epsom, which I think he will, and he handles the jamboree, which based on today I think he will, we've every right to think he's going there to be competitive. What happens after that, who knows? - Ralph Beckett, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He was pretty impressive on his debut in August and then he had an issue. He's in good form now and I think he's going to go for the Dante. His owner is from Yorkshire and his work would suggest that's a good place to start. 28-04-25

runners.comment: Did well last term; his form is not what's required to win this but he brings potential
runners.spotlight: Won a novice and three Ascot 1m4f handicaps on varied ground last June-September; creditable second of five in Ascot Group 3 on final outing; none of that form is near what should be required to win this race but he brings potential starting this second season.

quotes.race: Silent Pool Gin Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
quotes.quote: Tenability is going through the ranks. He did very well to win here the last day and he's improved a ton from then. He's done it really well and I really like this horse, it feels like he's doing everything the right way - Cieren Fallon, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

racecards.verdict: 2025 for PRIDE OF ARRAS had two peaks and a huge trough but his Group 2 wins at York suggest he's a likely winner of this race.
racecards.betting_forecast: 7/4 Convergent, 5/2 Al Aasy, 3/1 Lion's Pride, 9/1 Phantom Flight, 12/1 Bellum Justum, 14/1 Tenability

racecards.race_name: Win Unique Experiences At OLBG Prizes Spring Cup Handicap

runners.comment: Usually runs in Listed/Group races; not quite at best in 2025; others preferred
runners.spotlight: Pretty consistent in Listed/Group races in 2025 without performing to his very best; losing sequence now stands at 18 and he reappears after seven months off in his first handicap since July 2022; cheekpieces left off and others preferred.

quotes.race: Mutasaabeq At The National Stud James Seymour Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: Checkandchallenge has run in some hot races this year and I don't think he has actually run a bad race in any of them. Dropping back into a Listed race today it was just nice to get his head back in front. I know the distance between them was a long way at Ascot the other day, but he was fourth in a Group One and he picked up a good bit of prize money and he had some nice horses behind him. I think a mile and a quarter is right for him. We went back for the stiff mile at Ascot as we felt on that track it was going to suit him and he got his just rewards. He can cope with those extremes out there today where a lot of other horses can't. He is in the Hong Kong Mile, but I think he deserves a nice break. There will be plenty of options for him next year. Horses like him can turn up in those Group One races that cut up a bit and pick up a bit of money. We might also look at those Group Three and Group Two races in France again next year - William Knight, trainer.

quotes.race: Coral Burradon Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: I was absolutely delighted and excited with the manner in which Checkandchallenge has done it in what looked a competitive field. He had to go and win today to warrant a run in the Guineas and that's still on the agenda. It looked like there was a bit left there, which there needs to be to be competitive in the Guineas. There's improvement still to come from him, it wasn't all about today. The big challenge is he's got to convert his all-weather form across to turf, but there's no reason why he can't. He did a nice bit of work on the grass gallops last week which pleased us and made us feel he was definitely above average - William Knight, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's a lovely horse who won his first two races and earned a place in the 2,000 Guineas. His second start when bolting up in Listed company at Newcastle had plenty of people talking about him and I must be honest I thought he'd win but not in the manner he did. We decided he had to take his place in the 2,000 Guineas but he never got a chance to show his true colours. He got wiped out at the start, which caused him to lose his action, and from there on things never went right. Unfortunately he came back sore, having knocked a joint. It has been hard work getting him back but he's there now and ready to go again. I looked at Royal Ascot but he had a slightly dirty scope before and you must be 100 per cent for that meeting. He heads to Newmarket for the July meeting, where we'll aim for the Listed Sir Henry Cecil Stakes over a mile and then we'll look to the Thoroughbred Stakes at Glorious Goodwood. He'll run at Newmarket as long as they get nice ground and hopefully we can get him back to where he was before the Guineas. He'll have to carry a penalty there for his Listed win but it's a lesser race and hopefully it'll help him get his confidence back. We're all very excited about getting him out again. Further down the line we could look to step him up to 1m2f. 30-06-22

prev_owners.owner: Exors Of The Late Alan Mason

runners.comment: Progressive; easily made all at Newmarket last November; may have more in the tank
runners.spotlight: Has a progressive profile and made it three wins from eight attempts when easily making all at Newmarket (1m, good to soft) last November; subsequently gelded; a 10lb rise means he'll need another personal best but he's a low-mileage 4yo who may have more in the tank.

quotes.race: Juddmonte EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands C And D) (EBF Qualifier) (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.quote: This is renowned as an undulating track, I wanted to go forward but I'd have had to fight for it so I took the realistic option to follow. Linwood had to learn today and he did. I always felt like he was going to win. There was that tricky moment where he had to get himself in order and go through that gap. He hit a ridge at the same time I asked him and he didn't know where to put his legs but he pulled himself together and he ran to the line nicely. You'd like to think he's learned plenty. He gave me a great feel, he has a great mentality so fingers crossed he can build on today- Sean Levey, Jockey.

stable_tour.quote: A horse I really like, who could well be one for the Britannia. He's ready to run and will probably start off in a nice handicap at Haydock and then on to Ascot. 22-04-25

runners.comment: Tough and consistent; won this race 12 months ago; 13lb higher but impossible to rule out
runners.spotlight: Tough and consistent sort who won this race (good ground) on his reappearance 12 months ago and finished second in the Balmoral Handicap at Ascot in the autumn; starts the new season on a career-high mark but he's impossible to rule out.

quotes.race: OLBG Spring Cup Handicap
quotes.quote: It's great to be back and it's our first runner on grass [this year]. I didn't know how fit they all were but Ebt's Guard has been working extremely well. - William Muir, joint-trainer.

quotes.race: Vickers.Bet Restricted Maiden Stakes (For horses In Bands C And D) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Ebt's Guard has been slightly unlucky in his runs. First time out he got beat half a length and then last time we had to go the long way round - William Muir, joint-trainer.

runners.comment: Previously trained in France where he won four times; makes British debut in a warm race
runners.spotlight: Previously trained in France where he won four times, the last two coming over 8.5f (AW) and 1m1f (good ground) at Chantilly; changed hands for 75,000euros last autumn; makes his British debut in a warm race.

runners.comment: Beaten a neck last year; won the Lincoln at Doncaster three weeks ago; in the mix again
runners.spotlight: Goes well in a big field over a straight 1m; beaten a neck in this race last year (good ground) and made a winning return in the Lincoln at Doncaster (good to soft; beat Rogue Diplomat a nose) three weeks ago; should be in the thick of things again off a 4lb higher mark.

quotes.race: William Hill Lincoln (Heritage Handicap)
quotes.quote: Urban Lion will go for big handicaps, he's not going to go up massively for that. We'll try and get some black type, the owners still have a bit of the family. Straight miles are what he wants - Jack Channon, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He won on the all-weather at Chelmsford last time and he could follow in the footsteps of Metal Merchant. We might look at the Spring Cup with him as well, but he'll certainly be campaigning in all those big mile handicaps this year. The Royal Hunt Cup and Golden Mile are just some of those and you'd hope he can pick one up. He's a big horse who could even progress into stakes company if all things fell right. He's one I really like. 02-04-25

runners.comment: Smart at best in Britain; form tailed off in Australia in 2025; has had wind surgery
runners.spotlight: Smart at his best for William Haggas, winning a Listed race at Sandown (1m2f, good) in July 2024; campaigned solely in Australia in 2025 and well beaten on his last two starts; potentially well handicapped back in Britain for a new yard after wind surgery, but he carries obvious risks.

quotes.race: Ranvet Stakes (Group 1) (3yo+) (Turf)
quotes.quote: Al Mubhir just did too much on the way around. He just never let go - Tom Marquand, jockey.

quotes.race: Visit racingtv.com Handicap
quotes.quote: Everything went really smoothly and the soft ground was always going to help coming back to a mile. Al Mubhir\ relaxed well and surprised me how well he did it in the end. He's clearly a talented horse and if we keep getting things right, he's got a big future - Tom Marquand, jockey.

quotes.race: MansionBet Beaten By A Head Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Al Mubhir did that nicely. The jockey liked him but said he knew nothing so we might have to run him again but he was a bit spicy after the race so we'll have to see - William Haggas, trainer.

runners.comment: Won at Newmarket and York last summer; big player if ready to roll after six months off
runners.spotlight: Below par on his last two 3yo starts but he'd previously won competitive 1m events at Newmarket and York (both good to firm) in the summer, and he did well to prevail at York after having to wait for a run; only 3lb higher here and he'll be a major player if ready to roll after six months off.

quotes.race: bet365 Mile Handicap
quotes.quote: It was the plan to play Fifth Column late and Ryan got there just in time. He won his side of the race in the Britannia but not the whole thing. I'm told he could be a a Cambridgeshire type but we'll have to see - John Gosden, joint trainer.

quotes.race: bet365 Esher Cup Handicap
quotes.quote: Gelding has calmed Fifth Column down and made him a happier horse. Having had a run and won on the all-weather he was fully race fit, which he needed to be as the ground was slow, which is quite correct with there being jumpers here tomorrow. He had been working well at home and I thought if we had a winner today it would be in this race. We'll stay at a mile and aim for the Britannia at Royal Ascot and hope we get drawn on the right side. He could run before if we need to freshen him and can find the right spot; he will tell me - John Gosden, joint-trainer.

quotes.race: Try Unibet's New Improved Acca Boosts Maiden Stakes (GBB Race) (Div II)
quotes.quote: We didn't go overly quick and I was trapped a couple of rows further back than ideal. Fifth Column showed a good turn of foot stepping up to the mile for the first time and he hit the line well. A mile is probably his optimal trip and we'll see where he goes from here - Kieren Shoemark, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

prev_owners.owner: D Smith & Mrs J Magnier & M Tabor & Peter M Brant

runners.comment: Two 7f wins for Aidan O'Brien but not at best last three outings; another new trainer here
runners.spotlight: Has had several trainers in his short career to date; two 7f wins for Aidan O'Brien; not at his best on his last three outings, never dangerous at Kempton on latest (sole run for James Ferguson); probably best watched.

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Maiden
quotes.quote: Serengeti is a work in progress I'd say with loads more improvement to come and is an exciting horse. Hopefully he'll make into a stakes horse - Declan McDonogh, jockey, talking to Racing TV.

runners.comment: Smooth Ascot winner last autumn; too free in Lincoln on return; now looks ready to strike
runners.spotlight: Raced too freely in the Lincoln and ended up shaping nicely in a never-nearer ninth; had ended 2025 on a high with a smooth success at Ascot (1m, soft) and a fine fourth in the Balmoral Handicap (good) over the same C&D; gets on really well with Oisin Murphy and he's back in the saddle today; still unexposed and now looks ready to strike.

quotes.race: Ascot Iron Stand Membership Handicap
quotes.quote: He's a lovely genuine horse. Shout was unlucky here at the big meeting, he missed the break and then went to Goodwood and drawed the widest of all. He was quite frankly drawn out of the race. The horse really deserved this big win today. He's a nice progressive three-year-old and he'll make up into a lovely four-year-old. Hopefully we'll consider keeping him in training as he can run in so many races over a mile and nine furlongs - Gail Brown, head of Gail Brown Racing.

runners.comment: 3-9 in France; no easy task off this mark on British debut but could be unexposed
runners.spotlight: Like Ozat, he's an ex-French gelding who was acquired by Ian Williams (for 90,000euros) in the autumn; won three times (7.5f/1m) from just nine attempts in France; doesn't have an obvious chance off this mark on British debut but he could still be unexposed.

runners.comment: Beaten a nose by Urban Lion in the Lincoln and there should be little between them again
runners.spotlight: Progressive 4yo; 5-6 over 7f but showed he's just as effective at 1m when making Urban Lion pull out all the stops in the Lincoln at Doncaster (good to soft) three weeks ago; 1lb better off for a nose defeat and there should be little between the pair again.

quotes.race: William Hill Best Odds Guaranteed Handicap
quotes.quote: Rogue Diplomat is a bit of a legend. It's been a long year for him and I thought if he was going to get caught out it might have been today, especially on this ground. I got a really nice sit and we were going a nice gallop but all the horses in front of me stopped pretty fast and he wants to be hitting the front in the last furlong. I probably got there a bit soon and he was tying up late. He likes to come through horses and he's very honest but you've got to make his mind up for him when you do hit the front - Harry Davies, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

quotes.race: Best Ticket Deals Online At leicester-racecourse.co.uk Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We've always liked Rogue Diplomat and he's shown so much at home. We tried him over too far at Chelmsford last year and we're delighted to see him win. He's a different horse this year. James is such a good trainer and has done a great job with him - Tony Elliott, founder of the Rogues Gallery, owners.

runners.comment: 1m2f Royal Ascot winner in 2024; seen only three times last year but not ruled out
runners.spotlight: Won the Golden Gates Handicap at Royal Ascot (1m2f, good to firm) in June 2024; seen only three times last season and wasn't at his best, although each run came in a highly competitive race; may need a positive ride to get away with this shorter trip on his reappearance, but the handicapper has given him a chance and he's certainly not ruled out.

quotes.race: Duke Of Edinburgh Stakes (Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
quotes.quote: He said I was in front two down and thought I'll go and win this and he emptied the final two. Hand Of God looked pretty quick over 10 [furlongs] last year and it was when Ryan rode him at Newmarket, when the gelding was obviously a bit flat, he said 'I think he needs all of 12', but I think maybe he just didn't see the real Hand Of God that day. I suspect something like the John Smith's at York would be more suitable - Harry Charlton, trainer.

quotes.race: Golden Gates Stakes (Handicap)
quotes.quote: Hand Of God didn't have a great trip again, but he had a clear run at least this time and he picked up very quick from the three to the one, and William said he almost got there too soon. I think he's still a ten-furlong horse; he's got a great mind and is good physically. He's not done much wrong and I guess he's probably due a step up in class. He works with King's Gambit, so we were all quite confident, and Kikkuli (second in the Jersey) was another positive - Harry Charlton, trainer.

quotes.race: bet365 Esher Cup Handicap
quotes.quote: We thought Hand Of God was a mile and a quarter horse last year but he had the speed to win over a mile as he did here. We may have a look at the London Gold Cup at Newbury next month for him - Harry Charlton, trainer.

prev_owners.owner: M Tabor & D Smith & Mrs J Magnier & Westerberg

runners.comment: Mostly well held last year; falling in the weights but needs to turn over a new leaf
runners.spotlight: Mostly well held last year and unplaced on five of his six starts; falling in the weights and dangerous if revived by a winter break, but his losing run goes back to September 2023 and he needs to turn over a new leaf.

quotes.race: Mint Millions Stakes (Grade 3) (3yo+) (Turf)
quotes.quote: To be fair, Dr Hay picked this race out even before he purchased Ancient Rome. He's Kentucky-bred so it fitted in well. I think he went well on the [firm] ground today and he's pretty adaptable when it comes to surfaces. He ran in softer conditions a lot of the time in France and last time [at Goodwood] it was soft, but he's a War Front and they go on fast turf - Jamie Spencer, quoted by Bloodhorse.

quotes.race: Coral Chesterfield Cup Handicap
quotes.quote: They did go a good gallop, which was quite tiring in dead ground, and the race fell into his lap in the last furlong. I always thought I was going to be involved; maybe outside the three-furlong pole, he was moving up easily enough and I was following Tom Marquand [on Millebosc], who was kind of dying so we went round him. Ancient Rome is a very lazy horse - you ask him and he'll go for three or four strides, then he's lazy again. Even right at the line he pricked his ears and kind of jammed [the brakes] on, so he's a hard horse to assess. I just planned to drop out, stay on the outside, get cover and come down the outside. Dr Jim said, just ride like Richard Hughes! He's a smart horse and I thought he was a stakes horse, so I'm sure he will be capable of at least Listed company - Jamie Spencer, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: He had an injury at the backend of last season and has had some time off. He's a big horse who takes a bit of getting ready but he's undoubtedly talented. He's not a certain starter in the Wolferton but if he does take his chance, I think he's well up to that class. 13-06-24

runners.comment: Reappearance; best form is over further but he could be freshened up by a change of yard
runners.spotlight: In and out last season for Michael Bell, the high points coming when second in big fields at York (good to firm) in May and the Curragh (good to yielding) in September; all his best efforts have come over 1m2f so today's shorter distance is a concern but it's possible he'll be freshened up by a change of stable (same owner).

quotes.race: Precision Facades Handicap
quotes.quote: Tony Montana is a lovely horse with a lovely pedigree. He's probably won't be high enough for the Ascot handicaps, so we'll box clever and look at places like Goodwood - Michael Bell, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's been second on both starts this year and has nudged up the handicap as a result. He's in the Royal Hunt Cup and the stiff mile at Ascot is an interesting angle for him. I'm not totally convinced that it'll work but we're very keen to give it a go. If it doesn't work he'd be aimed at something like the John Smith's Cup at York, in which he was third last year. He's now on a career-high mark of 99 but the Hunt Cup could work for him and, if it did, he'd be a live player. 09-06-25

runners.comment: Third here last year; hasn't been seen for eight months but dangerous if cherry ripe
runners.spotlight: Chased home Ebt's Guard and Urban Lion in this race last year and he's better off at the weights with both; ran a cracker when dropped to 7f for valuable event at Ascot last summer; hasn't been seen for eight months but he'll be dangerous if cherry ripe.

quotes.race: Best Bet With Jenningsbet British EBF Novice Stakes (Colts & Geldings)
quotes.quote: Classic has travelled well every day but we let him roll today. He still has signs of immaturity there but he is a very talented horse. We just didn't want to have any excuses today. It wouldn't surprise me if we see him turn up at the top level, especially on soft ground. I'd say there is a fair chance we go to the Champagne at Doncaster next - Richard Hannon, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: It's been a mental thing with him - if he wants to win, he will - but we've had him gelded and he seems to have come back in great form. I was very pleased with his run at Newbury this month and he could well be a force in good handicaps like the Hunt Cup. 22-04-25

runners.comment: On 14-race losing run; below par in big field in Ireland on return; Ryan Moore booked
runners.spotlight: On a 14-race losing sequence but he was runner-up three times last term, including when beaten a head at Glorious Goodwood (1m1f, good); went off third favourite in a big field at the Curragh on reappearance but didn't give his running; on a retrieval mission with Ryan Moore booked.

stable_tour.quote: He ran a cracker at Sandown when second last time. He hasn't had a race in which they've gone really fast yet, but if there's a good pace in the Hunt Cup then he should go well. 10-06-25

He ran really well in the spring and went to Royal Ascot, where he ran really well off top weight, although he was jarred up on the quick ground. On nice ground, 1m2f will be right up his street. 18-09-24

runners.comment: Lightly raced 4yo; close second at Goodwood in the autumn; has been gelded; interesting
runners.spotlight: Lightly raced 4yo; consistent last season, winning in cosy fashion at this meeting (7f, good) and going down narrowly when stepped up in trip at Goodwood (1m, good) in the autumn; reappears having been gelded and with his stable in form; interesting contender.

prev_owners.owner: Exors Of The Late K Abdullah

runners.comment: Far from disgraced in valuable AW event last time but his turf form is at a lower level
runners.spotlight: Kept busy on AW during the winter, winning over 7f at Newcastle and far from disgraced in a valuable 1m event there on Good Friday; however, his turf form is at a lower level and he'll do well to regain the winning thread.

runners.comment: Four wins for Edward Bethell; reappears for new yard; doesn't have many miles on the clock
runners.spotlight: 4-10 for Edward Bethell, winning the Hambleton Handicap at York's Dante meeting (1m, good to firm) last spring; changed hands for 26,000gns last autumn; only 3lb higher than at York and doesn't have many miles on the clock.

quotes.race: Oakmere Homes Hambleton Handicap
quotes.quote: The trainer f***ed up by running Old Cock in the Lincoln. He got a rush of blood early in the year and ran him too soon. He wasn't quite there and I looked at him on the Sunday morning after the race and said I'm a f***ing idiot. This has been the aim since and I'm delighted we were able to come here and run a good race. He's very talented on his day and he looked a million going round the parade ring today, I was never confident because it's York but I had a strong hope. Who knows where the ceiling will be with him? He's a big horse with plenty of scope so we'll see. We'll aim towards the Hunt Cup but I'll speak to the owners before making a final decision - Ed Bethell, trainer.

quotes.race: Betfred 'The Classic Bookmaker' Handicap (London Mile Series Qualifier)
quotes.quote: Old Cock is a lovely horse and always has been. The first two home were the right two and he's a big, raw horse who could be even better next year. There's a 3yo 1m handicap at York in two weeks I had in the back of my mind, but he doesn't really take his racing that well. He's a big horse and he's not great when you rush him, so we'll see how he is - Ed Bethell, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's a legend, a really great horse for his owners and still pretty progressive. We decided the Hunt Cup probably wasn't his race, or Ascot his course. He's better on flat tracks and the Hunt Cup is a bit of a lottery. So he'll go back to York on July 12 for a 0-100 handicap over a mile then he'll be trained for the Sky Bet Mile at the Ebor meeting. That's his sort of track so we'll play to his strengths. I think he needs proper decent ground. 02-07-25

runners.comment: Had an excuse in Bahrain in January; well handicapped based on last year's Lincoln second
runners.spotlight: Showed his effectiveness over a straight 1m when beaten a nose in the 2025 Lincoln at Doncaster (good to soft) and he's now 3lb lower; several respectable efforts afterwards, and 6f on good ground was probably too sharp on his sole outing in Bahrain over the winter; certainly well handicapped on best form and well worth a market check after 106 days off.

quotes.race: William Hill Lincoln (Heritage Handicap)
quotes.quote: Oliver Show has run a massive race. Huge credit to Charles Eddery and Chas Robinson who brought him back from Bahrain. He's a progressive horse - I thought he was maxed out where he is but he looks like there may be a little bit left. He goes well fresh and I'd say we'll probably work back from the Royal Hunt Cup - George Boughey, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He was meant to come back for the Lincoln but got stuck in Bahrain, where he was completely outpaced over six furlongs in January. He could go to the Guineas meeting if he gets back in time, then maybe go for this month's Spring Cup at Newbury. 02-04-26

prev_owners.owner: Westerberg & Mrs Magnier & M Tabor & D Smith

runners.comment: Lightly raced 5yo; well held in 2025 but is thrown in on best form and has been gelded
runners.spotlight: Very lightly raced 5yo; Group-placed in 2024 for Aidan O'Brien; has failed to beat a rival in three runs for current stable, always behind after stumbling early on at Sandown (behind Urban Lion) last June; hard to recommend on recent form but he has been dropped a chunk in the weights and gelded, and he now reappears in a hood.

quotes.race: SP Or Better Guaranteed With Tote Irish EBF Maiden
quotes.quote: Samuel Colt is a lovely colt. He wasn't in love with the ground but his class got him through it. He could be an exciting colt for next year all being well - Chris Armstrong, assistant trainer.

runners.comment: Has run only five times; fine second over C&D last autumn; reappears with potential intact
runners.spotlight: Has run only five times and he signed off for last season with a personal best when second of 15 over C&D (good to soft) in September; has been gelded and makes his reappearance with his potential still intact; one of four runners for Richard Hannon.

quotes.race: Etcetera Construction 40th Anniversary EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race) (Div I)
quotes.quote: We were hoping to get Stem on the track quite quickly from the breeze up but Richard Hannon kept saying he needed more time and we've been as patient as we can. We went down there last week and he surprised everyone with how well he worked. After that we were hoping he'd run well today. Ryan said he'd get a mile plus eventually and that was great - Johnny de la Hey, owner.

stable_tour.quote: He won very well at Newbury on his only run at the end of last season. He's massive, very good-looking. He's in the German Derby and the Irish Derby and I'd like to think he's up to that sort of level. He's pleased us in his early work and we're quite excited about him. 22-04-25

runners.comment: In good form on AW; finished behind several of these when only seventh 12 months ago
runners.spotlight: Equally effective at 7f and 1m and arrives in good form from the AW; could be thereabouts again, although he finished behind several of these when only seventh in this race 12 months ago.

quotes.race: R & M Electrical EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race) (Div I) (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.quote: Cogitate is a beautiful looking horse, he has the size and scope and looks to have a big future ahead of him. He qualifies now for the Acomb and that could be a good step. We've won that a couple of times before with Dutch Connection and Phoenix Of Spain so that might be the route he takes.

stable_tour.quote: He wants fast ground and conditions will be key to his chance. I think a stiff mile will really suit him and he already has some decent form in the book. We were looking to get another run into him before the Britannia, but 93 is a good mark and we've decided to keep our powder dry. He bumped into a good horse in Night Raider on his comeback at Southwell but still ran well and wasn't 100 per cent wound up for that. He's done a couple of nice pieces of work recently and there should be good improvement in him. He's a horse who runs well fresh and I hope he's a Group horse. 13-06-24

He's a lovely, big colt we bought last year. He has a very good attitude and does everything we ask of him at home. He'll be a lovely horse next year but before then he should be okay as a juvenile as everything he has done on the bridle makes me think he's a useful colt. 21-06-23

runners.comment: Made most when beaten head here in spring 2025; will need career best from current mark
runners.spotlight: Reliable last season, going close under a positive Sam Hitchcott ride over C&D (good) in May; met some trouble at Newmarket on final start; not discounted, although he'll need a career best from his current mark.

runners.comment: Form tailed off in 2025 but back to same mark as when winning at Carlisle last summer
runners.spotlight: Best efforts when ridden up with the pace; form tailed off in 2025 but he's now back to the same mark as when winning at Carlisle (1m, soft; handles good) last summer; gelded since last seen; stablemate of Urban Lion.

stable_tour.quote: I'm delighted with him and we've taken a very speculative punt and stuck him in the Derby. He had only two runs last year, ­winning his maiden at Epsom and then finishing fourth in a Group 3 at Deauville in August. He went for another novice at ­Wolverhampton last week because he wasn't qualified for a handicap mark and was third. We might look at a Derby trial for him. If he cuts it at that level then brilliant, but if not we'll take stock and ­rebuild him, but we're very ­excited about him and he's been training really well. 02-04-25

runners.comment: Beat 15 opponents at Doncaster three weeks ago but up 4lb and in a much stronger race here
runners.spotlight: Well backed and defeated 15 opponents at Doncaster (7f, good to soft; just as effective over 1m) on reappearance three weeks ago; that was convincing enough but he's up 4lb and in a much stronger race here.

racecards.verdict: Fifth Column is respected but SHOUT (nap) did not get the rub of the green in the Lincoln and now looks ready to strike.
racecards.betting_forecast: 6/1 Back In Black, 7/1 Rogue Diplomat, 8/1 Shout, 9/1 Urban Lion, 10/1 Fifth Column, 12/1 Whip Cracker,  Stem,  Linwood,  Classic, 16/1 Ebt's Guard,  Boyfriend,  Hand Of God, 20/1 Jimmy Speaking,  Cogitate,  Oliver Show, 22/1 Tony Montana, 25/1 Checkandchallenge, 33/1 Old Cock,  Serengeti,  Al Mubhir,  Hot Cash, 40/1 Ancient Rome,  Nikovo,  Nizam, 50/1 Samuel Colt,  Ozat

racecards.race_name: Dubai Duty Free Tennis Championships "Confined" Maiden Stakes (No More Than 2 Runs) (GBB)

runners.comment: Absent and gelded since 50-1 seventh of 12 in Glorious Goodwood maiden
runners.spotlight: Absent and gelded since 50-1 seventh of 12 in Glorious Goodwood maiden (7f); looks the type to find peak stride when handicapping.

runners.comment: Has something to find on his October efforts over 7f
runners.spotlight: Has something to find on his October efforts over 7f, fifth of 11 at Newmarket latest; may be more interesting in handicaps shortly.

runners.comment: Combination of physical tweak (wind surgery) and first-time hood may prompt progress
runners.spotlight: Improvement required judged on his August efforts (7f) but combination of physical tweak (wind surgery) and first-time hood may prompt progress; yard also runs Lighting Thunder.

runners.comment: Study Of Man half-brother to 6f AW 2yo winner; market helpful
runners.spotlight: Study Of Man half-brother to 6f AW 2yo winner Jewel Of London (RPR 79); dam 5f-1m1f scorer (including Group 2; 111); market helpful.

runners.comment: Midfield in summer Deauville race that has worked out well; likely to improve
runners.spotlight: Midfield in summer Deauville race (7f, soft) that has worked out well; interesting on reappearance with improvement on the cards.

runners.comment: Fourth in two events won by colts who have since performed well at Group 1 level
runners.spotlight: Finished fourth in 7f events at Newbury and Goodwood won by colts who have since performed well at Group 1 level; gelded since; may take a step forward.

runners.comment: Modest fifth of 13 in 1m AW contest at Kempton
runners.spotlight: Modest fifth of 13 in 1m AW contest at Kempton; looks one for handicaps later on.

runners.comment: New scenario needs to spark improvement
runners.spotlight: Finished fifth in races at about 6f on soft/heavy ground, wearing hood both times; new scenario needs to spark improvement.

runners.comment: Handicaps should be more suitable shortly
runners.spotlight: Beaten about 12l at Haydock (1m) in both starts, modest fourth latest; handicaps more suitable shortly.

runners.comment: Second-place finishes at Newbury and Doncaster suggest he's a winner waiting to happen
runners.spotlight: Kingman half-brother to QEII winner King Of Change; entered in the 2,000 Guineas; has shown clear promise with second-place finishes at Newbury (1m, soft; behind Greenham contender Gonna Fly) and Doncaster (7f, good to soft; beaten only a neck); a winner waiting to happen.

runners.comment: Solid effort at Yarmouth, beating all bar the useful market leader; respected
runners.spotlight: Night Of Thunder colt who cost 650,000gns as a yearling; posted a solid effort at Yarmouth (1m, good to soft) where he was a neck second, clear of remainder, behind the market leader who subsequently ran well in Group 3; likely to show good progress this term; respected.

runners.comment: Time Test colt who may need longer trips
runners.spotlight: Time Test half-brother to five winners, notably Quietness (Group-placed 1m2f-1m4f; RPR 105); this newcomer may need longer trips.

runners.breeder: Nps, Jd Gunther & Ttr Bloodstock Limited
runners.comment: 15,000gns yearling; by Without Parole; likely best watched on debut
runners.spotlight: 11,000gns foal, 15,000gns yearling; by Without Parole out of French maiden; along with stablemate Long Reign, likely best watched on debut.

runners.comment: Needs to improve on his Newmarket effort
runners.spotlight: Needs to improve a good deal on his Newmarket effort (finished sixth of 11 over 7f).

runners.comment: Finished 4l second in Kempton maiden won by Greenham contender Title Role
runners.spotlight: Finished 4l second of eight, best of the newcomers, in Kempton maiden (7f, AW) won by Greenham contender Title Role; open to progress.

runners.comment: Good second at Kempton on reappearance; one of the main form contenders
runners.spotlight: Placed in both outings, gelded prior to good second at Kempton (7f, AW) on reappearance; one of the main form contenders upped further in distance and additional improvement is possible.

stable_tour.quote: He really impressed me with the way he finished off when third at Salisbury behind Italica on his debut this month. I think he'll win a maiden wherever we go now. He's my trainer's pick as he looks a really nice prospect. 02-07-25

runners.owner: Al Shaqab Racing, Miller And Day
runners.comment: 130,000euros yearling; by Mehmas; wears tongue-tie on debut; check the betting
runners.spotlight: 130,000euros yearling; Mehmas half-brother to two winners, notably Prince Lancealot (5f-6f including French Listed/US; RPR 112); wears tongue-tie on debut; check the betting.

runners.breeder: Razza Del Sole Societa Agricola Srl
runners.comment: Finished 28-1 fifth of 13 in Newbury event won by 125-1 stablemate
runners.spotlight: Finished 28-1 fifth of 13 in Newbury event (7f, good to soft) won by a 125-1 stablemate; recorded an ordinary RPR but shaped as if he may improve for this extra furlong.

runners.comment: Belied 100-1 odds with eye-catching Doncaster effort that ties him in with King Of Earth
runners.spotlight: Belied his 100-1 odds with eye-catching fourth of 12, best of the newcomers, in Doncaster contest (7f, good to soft); ties in with King Of Earth on that effort; possibilities, provided the promise is confirmed.

runners.comment: 65,000euros yearling; pedigree suggests he's not sure to stay 1m
runners.spotlight: 65,000euros yearling; Soldier's Call half-brother to three winners, notably Scarlet Bear (Group-placed 6f; RPR 98); not certain to stay 1m.

runners.comment: Sibling to eight winners; looks one of the better types among the newcomers
runners.spotlight: St Mark's Basilica colt; sibling to eight winners, notably Forest Of Dean (1m2f including AW Group 3; 116), English Oak (7f/1m; 114) and Crown Of Oaks (1m/1m2f; 107); stablemate of King Of Earth; looks one of the better types among the newcomers.

runners.comment: Dream Ahead colt; first foal of 1m6f winner; one of three newcomers for his yard
runners.spotlight: The product of extremes, being by Dream Ahead and first foal of 1m6f winner (RPR 78); one of three newcomers for his stable.

runners.comment: Has very weak claims on form
runners.spotlight: Twice-raced filly who has very weak claims on form.

runners.comment: Midfield in 1m AW event at Kempton
runners.spotlight: Midfield in 1m AW event at Kempton; again wears hood; looks one for handicaps in due course.

runners.breeder: Mickley Stud Ltd & Tim & Miranda Johnson
runners.comment: Poor claims on her AW efforts
runners.spotlight: Turf debutante who has poor claims on her 7f AW efforts.

runners.comment: Eye-catcher at Ascot in the first of her two outings for David Menuisier
runners.spotlight: Eye-catcher at Ascot (1m) in the first of her two outings for David Menuisier; still with same owner; heed the market signals.

racecards.verdict: Yarmouth runner-up LIGHTING THUNDER is taken to go one better. King Of Earth is feared most.
racecards.betting_forecast: 5/2 King Of Earth, 11/4 Lighting Thunder, 8/1 Exclusive Code, 10/1 Blue Aria,  Spirit Of Saxony, 12/1 Eagles Attire, 14/1 Siwa Oasis,  The Golden Snitch,  Tambora, 16/1 Sponsor, 25/1 Atlas Mountain,  Footstepinthewoods,  Battosai, 33/1 Thomas Picton,  Rossa Raheen,  Oceti,  Fizzy Bear, 40/1 Decade Of Time,  West Byfleet, 50/1 Long Reign,  Notable Charm, 66/1 Houndswood Willow,  Madame Passant, 100/1 Dijon Gone, 200/1 Nefyn Queen

racecards.race_name: Too Darn Hot Darley "Confined" EBF Maiden Stakes (No More Than 2 Runs) (GBB/GBBPlus Race)

runners.comment: Placed at Kempton on last appearance; holds major entries and may improve
runners.spotlight: Beaten just over 5l in both 2yo starts, placed at Kempton (1m, AW) latest; seemingly thought capable of much better, being entered in the Dante and the Derby; could go well.

runners.comment: 55,000gns yearling; by Ghaiyyath; likely best watched on debut
runners.spotlight: 48,000euros foal, 55,000gns yearling; Ghaiyyath half-brother to winners Herecomesthebear (6f 2yo; RPR 64) and Schwarz Blau (German 1m); dam German 8.5f scorer; likely best watched on debut.

runners.comment: Camelot colt; one of several debutants in the field; market instructive
runners.spotlight: Camelot colt; dam unplaced 6f 2yo (RPR 38), sister to 6f 2yo Group 2 winner Showcasing; one of several debutants in the field; market instructive.

runners.comment: Promising second at Newcastle in sole 2yo start; holds big entries; respected
runners.spotlight: Sea The Stars colt who cost 550,000gns as a yearling; entered in the Dante, Derby and Irish Derby; promising half-length second of ten, best of the newcomers, at Newcastle (1m, AW) in sole 2yo start; seems likely to progress well this term; respected.

stable_tour.quote: He did nothing wrong on his only start over a mile at Newcastle, but he's a horse who is going to stay well. There's a ten-furlong novice at Nottingham on April 8 and another one over a mile and three furlongs at Newbury the week after, so there are a couple of options for him. He's one to try to win with in April and then see if he could be one for a Derby trial. Whether he's a nice horse or a very nice horse remains to be seen, but he's got a lovely pedigree and he's one I like. 01-04-26

runners.owner: Mrs Valda Burke And Mrs Belinda Miles
runners.comment: Newcomer by Sea The Moon; the chances are he'll need the experience
runners.spotlight: Sea The Moon half-brother to winners Mindset (7.4f/1m1f including Italy; RPR 79) and In A Hurry (7f; 76); dam 7f/1m1f scorer (90); the chances are he'll need the experience.

runners.comment: 30,000gns yearling; by Sir Percy; probably best watched on debut
runners.spotlight: 30,000gns yearling; by Sir Percy; sibling to seven winners, notably Pondus (1m2f-1m4f including Australia/Listed; RPR 111); dam 6f 2yo scorer (76); probably best watched on debut.

runners.comment: Derby entry; placed in both starts; holds leading claims for last year's winning yard
runners.spotlight: Eye-catching second at Newmarket (1m, good) then clear third, beaten favourite but running well on the figures despite still seeming green, at Doncaster (1m2f, good to soft) on reappearance; this Derby entry holds leading claims for last year's winning yard.

runners.comment: Kingman colt who represents notable connections; looks the pick of the newcomers
runners.spotlight: Kingman half-brother to winners Naga (1m; RPR 83) and Inwi (French 1m1f); dam French 1m1f-1m4f scorer (including Group 2; 109), half-sister to HK 1m4f Group 1 winner Dominant; notable connections; looks the pick of the newcomers.

racecards.verdict: Having still seemed green on his reappearance, TURTY TREE may be more polished this time. Glory Of The Seas is respected.
racecards.betting_forecast: 15/8 Glory Of The Seas, 9/4 Turty Tree, 11/4 Water To Wine, 7/1 Alderman, 16/1 Eben Al Khawaneej, 25/1 Grilse, 40/1 Blue Hercules,  Last Trump

racecards.race_name: Dubai Duty Free Millennium Millionaire Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners.comment: Has had just four races over his previous two seasons, with two wins, latest a 7f win here
runners.spotlight: Has had just four races over his previous two seasons, with two wins; that includes at this track last June on latest start when he made all for a narrow win over 7f on handicap debut; raised just 1lb and this move up to 1m2f makes for fascinating reappearance.

quotes.race: Grosvenor Sport Win Rewards Everyday Handicap
quotes.quote: Twisting Physics ran very well and probably needs to be stepped up to a mile. He ground it out and we'll probably aim for the Golden Mile at Goodwood before going to the Cambridgeshire at Newmarket - Oliver Cole, joint-trainer.

runners.comment: Thereabouts if the returning cheekpieces (worn once in 2024) don't have an adverse effect
runners.spotlight: Ran creditably over 1m2f on good ground on first three starts last season and back-to-form fourth of 13 at Kempton (AW) three weeks ago; thereabouts if the returning cheekpieces (worn on final start in 2024, below form) don't have an adverse effect.

quotes.race: Weekly Rewards With tote Stayers Club Racing League Race 7 Handicap (Trainers Reg' To Racing League)
quotes.quote: It took us a while to really figure Rathgar out. I think his future lies over this kind of trip. He was relentless really, he jumped a lot better and he was able to keep the revs up from a long way out and responded well for pressure - David Probert, jockey, speaking on Sky Sports Racing.

runners.comment: Unexposed after three races, latest a win; promising for this seasonal and handicap debut
runners.spotlight: Close on good ground on both turf starts, latterly over 1m2f at the Newmarket Craven meeting last April; gelded that July and won a novice at Chelmsford (1m2f, AW; easily in the end at 1-3) in October, which makes him unexposed and promising for this seasonal and handicap debut for in-form yard.

runners.comment: Basically highly reliable and it would be no surprise if he's seriously involved
runners.spotlight: Both wins were on AW and his turf form is not quite as good, but he's basically highly reliable and it would be no surprise if he's seriously involved for yard which won this race last year.

stable_tour.quote: He's a very lovely horse. I was pleased with his run at Glorious Goodwood, where he stepped up in trip and was third behind Push The Limit. He's a slow-maturing type who has a bit of scope and is still only a baby. I think he's better over 1m2f and 1m4f with a bit of give in the ground. 20-08-25

runners.comment: Sold last July and has been comfortably held since on the Flat and over hurdles
runners.spotlight: Formerly useful on the Flat for Kevin Ryan but was sold last July and has been comfortably held since on the Flat and over hurdles; tongue-tie (tried once in 2023) returns, plus first-time hood.

quotes.race: Sky Bet Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
quotes.quote: Ryan [Moore] said he just jumped a little bit awkwardly and that they didn't go as quickly as they might have. Marhaba The Champ was running a little bit free with him but he relaxed and let him fill up. He's done it well and that was a class ride. He'll probably get further but needs to relax a bit more. That's an avenue for the future but we'll probably stick to this trip for now - Kevin Ryan, trainer.

quotes.race: Knights Solicitors Handicap
quotes.quote: We thought Marhaba The Champ would run a big race and William (Buick) gave him a fantastic ride. He's a horse we like a lot, we've just been waiting for the ground. He loves quick ground without any juice in it at all - it's so important to him. I could see him going a bit further in time - Kevin Ryan, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's a cracking horse and looks to have done well again over the winter. He loves York and fast ground so we'll aim him at the Dante meeting, but we could explore going up in trip at some stage this season. 04-04-24

runners.comment: Reliable last term; 1m6f probably didn't help when he tailed off on reappearance; hood now
runners.spotlight: His only two wins (31 races) were last spring on his first two starts for James Owen; a string of creditable efforts followed (1m2f-1m4f) and 1m6f probably didn't help when he tailed off on reappearance two weeks ago, but connections now reach for a hood; has a competitive mark but he's probably not the percentage call.

runners.comment: Well held (made most) in warm 1m3f AW race at Kempton latest; needs to resume improvement
runners.spotlight: Won three in a row to kick off his 3yo and handicap careers last term; back on the up when reappearing to score at Newcastle (AW) in February, before well held (made most) in a warm 1m3f AW race at Kempton; needs to resume improvement.

quotes.race: Cameron Smart Memorial Handicap
quotes.quote: Triple Double A is a son of Mohaather and was a bit immature last season. It was good placing by Hugo. He'll get a mile and a quarter, and a mile on a sharp, turning track like this was always going to expose his babyish antics, but he's getting it together - Oisin Murphy, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: We'll go to the all-weather with him. He picked up a fracture when running a big race in Ireland to finish fourth and it's been repaired. We really liked him as a two-year-old, even though he didn't manage to win, and he has improved a great deal for the time. 08-10-25

runners.comment: 343 days off before this belated fifth race and it's hard to know how much ability remains
runners.spotlight: Bright start as 2yo in 2024 but then trailed the field in a Group 3 that October and, following a 80,000gns sale, has raced only once since, when never dangerous in a 1m2f handicap last May; 343 days off before this belated fifth start and it's hard to know how much ability remains; market may guide.

runners.comment: Defeat when 4-7 in a novice event last time heightens concern over lingering maiden status
runners.spotlight: Runner-up over about 1m2f on four of eight starts last year, including in two handicaps; close third on reappearance at Southwell (1m3f, AW) in early March but that was when 4-7 in a novice event and that disappointment heightens the concern over his lingering maiden status.

runners.comment: 4th for new yard in a 1m2f handicap last July was a partial revival on only race last year
runners.spotlight: 1-10 over 2022 and 2023 for Ralph Beckett, with a soft-ground win over 1m2f, but modest over hurdles in 2024; fourth of eight for new yard in a 1m2f handicap last July was a partial revival but that was his only race last year and he needs to build markedly on it; tongue-tie (worn as a hurdler) returns.

runners.comment: The handicapper seems to have caught up on AW; this is only his third race on turf
runners.spotlight: All his three wins were over 1m2f on Newcastle AW last October-December, easily on last occasion; his three races this year suggest that the handicapper has caught up and this is only his third race on turf, having been twice towards rear last summer; he has a bit to prove.

runners.comment: Suited by good/firmer and won four 1m2f handicaps, the latest last May; back from wind op
runners.spotlight: Suited by good/firmer and has won four 1m2f handicaps, the latest last May; he seemed in need of the run when 28-1 in this race the time before, so that's a concern on today's first run since his second wind surgery.

runners.owner: Frost, Acloque, LB, FW, Clayton & Godsal
runners.comment: Just three starts for the Kublers (same owners); unexposed and worth a market check
