runners.spotlight: Won debut but well beaten in a soft-ground Listed contest on her only other start as 2yo, before wind surgery and a good second of five in 1m3f handicap at Southwell (AW) last April; that makes just three runs for the Kublers (same owners); tongue tied all starts, with a hood on final outing, and she now wears just the hood; unexposed and worth a market check.

runners.comment: Each-way claims and the return of headgear (tried by his previous stable) could be a help
runners.spotlight: While a Nottingham 1m handicap last April remains his only win, he's run well over about 1m2f in three of four starts for his current yard; that gives him each-way claims and the return of headgear (tried by his previous stable and he ran well, including for the win) could be a help.

quotes.race: Beer Festival 12th April Handicap (Div I)
quotes.quote: Arcturus Flame was 10-1, then 14s. I didn't care what price he was, I thought he'd win. He went for a gallop with Dutch Kingdom and he came out and won a 0-90  - Darryll Holland, trainer.

runners.comment: C&D winner who won his latest hurdle race; should be primed to run well again
runners.spotlight: 2-6 on Flat, with the second win registered over C&D (good) last August; two wins among his five hurdle races this season, including latest start, so he should be primed to run well again today.

quotes.race: Sodexo Live! Juvenile Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We thought King Al might be a Triumph horse before he ran over hurdles, but he's come on with each run and we've learned with each start. I'd imagine he could have some fun on the Flat as he's not going to be a juvenile for long. He's found his level and that's a nice pot to win - Tom Bellamy, jockey.

runners.comment: Clearly best form in three races over 1m2f on ground softer than good last July-September
runners.spotlight: Clearly best form has been in three of his starts over 1m2f on ground softer than good, last July-September; not so good on last two outings and perhaps the ground won't be soft enough for today's reappearance.

racecards.verdict: Gosden-trained VALEDICTORY looks the one to turn to, ahead of King Al and Twisting Physics.
racecards.betting_forecast: 11/4 Valedictory, 6/1 King Al, 7/1 Twisting Physics,  Jupiter Ammon, 10/1 Bulletin,  Triple Double A, 12/1 Rathgar,  Royale Goodnight,  Arcturus Flame, 16/1 Sportingsilvermine,  Morcar, 20/1 Baltic Voyage, 25/1 The Green Mile, 50/1 Marhaba The Champ

racecards.race_name: British Stallion Studs EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners.comment: 260,000euros yearling; picked up nicely for 7f AW win on debut; extra 1f can suit
runners.spotlight: 260,000euros yearling out of multiple winner, including in Group 3 and 2s at 1m1f; easy to back for Kempton AW debut (7f) in December but she picked up nicely to take the lead; the bare form wasn't anything dramatic but the extra furlong should suit; in the mix.

stable_tour.quote: She hadn't blown me away at home and caught me by surprise when she won at Kempton in December, but she's starting to work really well now. We've got her in the Prix de Diane and I might start her off in either the Nell Gwyn, the Fred Darling or the mile novice for fillies at Nottingham during the same week. Her first run will dictate where she goes from there, but I really like her. 01-04-26

runners.comment: Useful form when winning over 7f at Sandown (soft) in August; has 1,000 Guineas entry
runners.spotlight: Promising 7f debut and she more than backed that up when sticking her neck out for a Sandown win (7f, soft) in August, form that turned out to be useful; can improve for 1m; holds a 1,000 Guineas entry; good claims.

quotes.race: Tattersalls £40,000 EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We were delighted with Deedaydiva's first start. She's been straightforward. She works well and has a great mind. She came out of Newmarket relaxed and has done it well here. I don't think I've ever had a filly this good as a two-year-old. We'll enjoy this and then think about where to go - Alan King, trainer.

runners.comment: Showed plenty in 2 of first 3 runs, but disappointing on AW when last seen in October
runners.spotlight: Showed plenty in two of her first three starts, most significantly over 1m at Salisbury (good to firm) in August; disappointing favourite on AW in October but she should be in contention on the previous turf run.

stable_tour.quote: She runs at Goodwood in the 7f fillies' maiden on Thursday. She's a really nice filly and I'm taking my time with her as I feel she could be quite good. We've given her a big break since she was second on her debut at Kempton and I'd like to think she'll run a good race. 30-07-25

runners.comment: Well-connected newcomer from respected yard; solid standard to aim at; needs market check
runners.spotlight: 130,000gns yearling; seventh foal; by Night Of Thunder; winning siblings include King Of Conquest (including three Listed wins at 1m2f-1m4f; RPR 117) and Lady Boba (1m2f/1m4f including Group 3; 109); dam 1m2f and 10.5f (Listed) winner; has a solid standard to reach but market can guide.

runners.comment: 125-1 for Lingfield AW debut over 7f in September when never recovering from a slow start
runners.spotlight: 125-1 for Lingfield AW debut over 7f in September when never recovering from a slow start; one to watch for now.

runners.comment: Well held in two AW maidens (1m3f and about 1m1f) early in the year; handicaps soon
runners.spotlight: An outsider when well held in two AW maidens (1m3f and about 1m1f) at the start of the year; handicaps will be more her line.

runners.comment: Winless but had some tough tasks in sprints as 2yo; good return over 1m on AW; thereabouts
runners.spotlight: Winless in sprints as 2yo but had some tough tasks and was beaten only 3l in Group 2 Queen Mary at Royal Ascot; off after July and had stamina as well as fitness to prove on recent return on Kempton AW (1m) where she hung on well for third against strong-finishing rivals; thereabouts.

runners.comment: Italian Listed/Group winners close up in pedigree but likely to benefit from this debut
runners.spotlight: 75,000gns yearling; seventh foal; by Blue Point; winning siblings include Italian 7.5f/1m winner Love Words (including 2yo/Listed; RPR 108) and Irish Lullaby (10.6f-12.3f Flat, 98; hurdle/chase); dam 1m-1m1f winner (including Italian Group 3; 105); no surprise if this is needed.

runners.comment: Very modest form in first two starts; no form claims without a big turnaround for blinkers
runners.spotlight: Modest efforts in first two starts, at 7f (turf) and about 1m (AW; only 7-2), and has no form claims unless she sees the light in first-time blinkers.

runners.comment: Out of a Listed winner at 1m; from a top yard and the market can guide.
runners.spotlight: By Palace Pier; fifth foal; half-sister to winners Kaasirr (7f/1m including KSA; RPR 80) and Tarraff (1m4f; 80); dam 6f-1m 2yo winner (including Listed; 103); from a leading yard and the betting should be helpful.

runners.comment: Nothing doing on debut; better when 2nd over 7f in September; races freely so trip query
runners.spotlight: 28-1 and nothing doing on her Newmarket debut but she revealed more in a first-time eyeshield when runner-up to a next-time novice winner, at Yarmouth (also 7f; soft) in September; now hooded and has raced freely so the extra furlong raises a query; handicaps may offer more scope.

runners.comment: Has achieved very little in two 1m starts on AW; looks set for modest handicap mark
runners.spotlight: Has achieved very little in two 1m starts on AW this year; looks set for a modest handicap mark following this race.

runners.comment: 65,000gns yearling; probably faces a tough start to her career
runners.spotlight: 65,000gns yearling; fourth foal; by Invincible Spirit; winning siblings include 7f/1m winner Sindria (RPR 94) and Spanish 8.7f winner Chelsea Square; dam placed 1m4f (RPR 74); probably faces tough start to career.

racecards.verdict: The penalised runners Botagoz and DEEDAYDIVA have more to come, particularly the latter, who did so well when winning at Sandown.
racecards.betting_forecast: 11/4 Deedaydiva, 3/1 Eskimo Pie, 9/2 Botagoz, 7/1 Shadida, 8/1 Brighlee,  Concealed Passion, 12/1 Tashi Delek, 14/1 Withtearsinmyeyes, 20/1 Midnight Steppers,  Palace Artois, 150/1 Cortado Girl, 200/1 Echo Valley,  Tiny Tiger

racecards.race_name: Racing TV Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Nice enough pedigree but others likely to have the legs of her over 6f on belated debut
runners.spotlight: First foal; dam ran well on debut for yard, then won over 1m next time (RPR 82), winning siblings include useful 7f-1m winner Hay Dude (also Group 3-placed); others likely to have the legs of her on belated debut.

runners.comment: Bred to sprint so may fare better over 6f than on her recent 7f debut when a remote fourth
runners.spotlight: 77,000euros breeze-up buy; bred to sprint but her fourth of 11 on Newcastle AW debut (7f; tongue tied; 28-1) was a remote one; this trip may well suit better but she has some work to do.

runners.comment: Smart sprinting pedigree; 33-1 for Haydock debut in October but showed ability; contender
runners.spotlight: Smart sprinting pedigree, winning siblings include Group 3/Listed winner Diligent Harry and Harry Three; 33-1 for 6f debut at Haydock in October where she raced freely but hinted at ability against rivals with experience; open to improvement and a likely contender.

runners.comment: Shown plenty in two AW starts at 6f and 5f; return to 6f looks sure to suit on turf debut
runners.spotlight: Promising in two starts, doing well despite the bit slipping through her mouth on sole 2yo start, at Southwell (6f) in December and coming home strongly when runner-up to odds-on winner at Newcastle (5f) in January; return to 6f looks sure to suit on turf debut; major chance.

runners.comment: Dam's side of pedigree suggests longer trips will suit but sire could inject speed
runners.spotlight: 52,000euros yearling; third foal; by Blue Point; half-sister to winners Curran (1m2f-1m6f; RPR 86) and Professor Longhair (1m AW; 85); dam Group-placed 1m4f winner (99); dam's side of pedigree suggests longer trips will be in order but sire could inject speed.

runners.comment: Came home strongly when only just failed on 6f turf debut; not so good over 7f on AW after
runners.spotlight: Caught napping for pace on Leicester debut (6f, soft) in October but she rallied and only just failed to get up; failed to flourish over 7f on Tapeta in November but the return to these conditions could pay dividends.

runners.breeder: Mrs S M Rogers & Sir Thomas Pilkington
runners.comment: Four good runs over 6f; hasn't shifted much in form terms but return to turf could suit
runners.spotlight: Four good runs since dropped to 6f, on turf and AW; she hasn't shifted much in form terms in that time but it's possible the return to turf will suit; ought to be on the premises.

runners.comment: Beaten when odds-on for 5f AW debut; fair 3rd upped to 6f; capable of better on turf debut
runners.spotlight: Turned over when odds-on for 5f debut on Southwell AW and no serious inroads on the first two when upped to 6f at Kempton recently; looks capable of better on turf debut and not ruled out.

stable_tour.quote: A recent purchase from the breeze-ups. She looks pretty quick and should be one to follow. 09-07-25

runners.comment: 7-1 for AW debut (6f); finished way back but presumably had shown something at home
runners.spotlight: 7-1 for Lingfield AW debut (6f) in September but she finished way back after starting slowly; SP that day suggested she wasn't a no-hoper and interesting to see how she goes in the market this time.

runners.comment: Bred to be speedy but hood fitted on debut and may be one to watch this time
runners.spotlight: 15,000gns foal; third foal; by Zoustar; winning siblings include Kendall Roy, multiple 5f winner in Britain and elsewhere (99) and Hippocratic Oath (about 1m; 76), dam 5f/6f winner (92); hood fitted on debut so may be one to watch this time.

racecards.verdict: Bintaryana is bred to come on plenty as a 3yo but EGOTISTICAL can improve on a recent strong-finishing 5f run now back at 6f.
racecards.betting_forecast: 11/4 Egotistical, 7/2 Mehmas Engine, 100/30 Hen Party, 5/1 Frantic, 13/2 Bintaryana, 12/1 Elshie, 16/1 Always Perfect, 25/1 Nzuri, 33/1 Unique Procedure, 50/1 Sweet Desire

racecards.race_name: Burger King Flamin Champion Handicap

runners.comment: Third in a couple of 5f maidens at Thirsk last spring but ran moderately subsequently.
runners.spotlight: Third in a couple of 5f maidens at Thirsk last spring but showed little subsequently stepped up to 6f at York and on her nursery debut back at Thirsk last September; sold to join new yard for £1,800 in January and needs to rediscover her early form back in trip.

runners.comment: Disputed the lead until weakening into fourth on his handicap debut at Kempton last month.
runners.spotlight: Consistent in his four runs so far and may well progress for the step back in trip after disputing the lead until weakening into fourth on his handicap debut at Kempton (6f, AW) last month; 2lb lower and should not be far away.

runners.comment: Second in 5f Beverley novice in September but finished last at Newcastle in January.
runners.spotlight: Stayed on late when a good second of nine in 5f Beverley novice in September; dwelt at the start when last of six on her AW/handicap debut at Newcastle (5f) in January and needs to get back on track.

runners.comment: Has been busy on AW during the winter, winning at Lingfield (5f) in February.
runners.spotlight: Has been busy on AW during the winter, winning at Lingfield (5f) in February; needs to reproduce that form on turf and if she does so then is another player.

runners.comment: 0-11 but has been running with credit on AW this year; drops back in trip.
runners.spotlight: 0-11 but has been running with credit on AW this year, meeting trouble in running on several occasions; sports first-time cheekpieces and drops down in trip on this return to turf; should be thereabouts.

runners.comment: Just modest in three runs on AW this year but may show more on turf/handicap debut.
runners.spotlight: Just modest in three runs on AW this year but it would be no surprise if she shows more on her turf/handicap debut for top trainer.

runners.comment: Nine-race maiden whose form after being gelded is inferior to his efforts last spring.
runners.spotlight: Nine-race maiden whose form after being gelded is inferior to his efforts last spring; headgear worn on last two starts in September is removed and now has questions to answer.

prev_owners.owner: Mrs P A Johnson & C H Stephenson

runners.comment: Moderate form in three runs last August/September; handicap debut.
runners.spotlight: Moderate form in three runs last August/September; has been gelded since and makes handicap debut; yard yet to get off the mark this term.

runners.comment: Kept on well to finish fourth on her AW/handicap debut at Wolverhampton last month.
runners.spotlight: Showed little in three runs on turf last year but caught the eye when keeping on well to finish fourth of eight on her AW/handicap debut at Wolverhampton (6f) last month; should run her race if she can reproduce that effort down in trip and back on turf.

runners.comment: Well beaten on his three starts on AW last year; drops in trip on turf/handicap debut.
runners.spotlight: Well beaten on his three starts on AW last year; has been gelded since and drops in trip on turf/handicap debut; market can guide.

runners.comment: Always behind in three AW maidens at Dundalk over 6f/7f last autumn for Ross O'Sullivan.
runners.spotlight: Always behind in three AW maidens at Dundalk over 6f/7f last autumn for Ross O'Sullivan; sports a first-time tongue tie and drops in trip on her turf/stable/handicap debut.

runners.comment: Promising third at Wolverhampton last September but didn't replicate that subsequently.
runners.spotlight: Promising third on her handicap debut at Wolverhampton (5f, AW) last September but didn't replicate that in a similar race in November; still early days on this return to turf and may have more to give.

runners.comment: Has finished last in all bar one of his six starts.
runners.spotlight: Has finished last in all bar one of his six starts with first-time cheekpieces (retained) having seemingly little effect last time; drops back in trip on this return to turf and massive improvement is required.

runners.comment: Showed little at massive odds in her three starts last year; handicap debut.
runners.spotlight: Showed little at massive odds in her three starts last year; drops back in trip on handicap debut but yard still waiting for their first turf winner this term.

runners.comment: Won a Chelmsford nursery on AW last August but has failed to build on that since.
runners.spotlight: Got off the mark in a Chelmsford nursery on AW last August but has failed to build on that since; sports first-time cheekpieces on this return to turf; needs a revival.

stable_tour.quote: He got off the mark two starts ago at Chelmsford. He'll be kept to the all-weather in 5f nurseries and should give his owners some fun over the winter. 01-10-25

runners.comment: Inconsistent in seven AW starts for current trainer over 6f/7f.
runners.spotlight: Finished last on two turf starts for Richard Hannon last July; inconsistent in seven AW starts for current trainer over 6f/7f since; drops back in trip and needs to prove her effectiveness on turf.

runners.comment: Sent off at big prices and has run to a low level in seven starts; hard to recommend.
runners.spotlight: Sent off at big prices and has run to a low level in seven starts; hard to recommend.

racecards.verdict: Winning form is in short supply here but ROSIEISME DARLING did just that at Lingfield in February. She is preferred to Staniel Cay.
racecards.betting_forecast: 5/1 Rosieisme Darling, 11/2 Staniel Cay, 6/1 Maid In Devon,  Faithful Dream, 10/1 Seven Of Hearts,  No Claims Bonus, 12/1 Mereside Spark,  Takincareofbizness, 14/1 Magnificent Mel, 16/1 Our Hero Matty,  Doilookokay, 20/1 Muddy Nora,  Hellcat,  I'm Dan Dare, 25/1 Yesnia, 50/1 Amakhala,  Independent Angel

racecards.race_name: Burger King Winning Whopper Apprentice Handicap

runners.breeder: Exors Of The Late Mr A A Byrne

prev_owners.owner: W H & Mrs J A Tinning & Mrs C Wallis
D & R Chapman, W&j Tinning & C Wallis

runners.comment: Well handicapped if bouncing back to form after six-month break; betting to guide
runners.spotlight: Out of sorts when last seen in the autumn but has dipped to 1lb below the mark she defied at Thirsk (5f, good) last summer; well handicapped if reviving after six months off.

quotes.race: Stirrup Room Delicious Deli-Box Dining Fillies' Handicap
quotes.quote: We got Miss Brazen off Karl Burke and she's done very well for us. She's had problems with her bloods this year, but we've taken our time with her and it seems to have paid off. The horses are running well and it's very nice to see - David Easterby, joint-trainer.

runners.comment: Could still be on good mark if he can translate recent AW form back to turf
runners.spotlight: In good form on AW since blinkered; did well to overcome a wide stall and make all at Kempton (6f) ten days ago and could take a bit of pegging pack if as effective back on turf.

runners.comment: Went close back on turf latest and remains below last winning mark
runners.spotlight: Made a good return to turf when narrowly denied over 5f at Bath (good) 13 days ago; nudged back up 3lb but remains 1lb below the mark he defied on AW last autumn; needs considering.

runners.owner: SBK Racing & B & J Parr Racing Ltd
runners.comment: Creditable third on AW latest; respected for yard with recent winning form in this race
runners.spotlight: Well handicapped on his 2025 best and he hasn't always enjoyed much luck on AW this winter; creditable third of nine at Southwell (6f) back from a short break 23 days ago; Mick Appleby has won this twice in recent years.

runners.comment: Good C&D record and well treated if back to form after four months off
runners.spotlight: More miss than hit in 2025 but back on a good mark as a result and a record of two wins and two seconds from his five outings over this C&D means a revival can't be ruled out back from four months off.

quotes.race: Theakston's Beer Festival Saturday 28th September Handicap
quotes.quote: High Opinion was very straightforward and the penny is starting to drop. It was a step up in class but he's a fine, big stamp of a horse. He'll be a sprinter that keeps on improving - Paul Mulrennan, rider.

quotes.race: Racing TV Extra Handicap (Div II)
quotes.quote: High Opinion got there cruising but had to knuckle down and has a willing attitude. He's progressing with every run - Harrison Shaw, jockey.

prev_owners.owner: Kevin Frost Racing Club & David Orr

runners.comment: Four AW wins (latest in December) but he's 0-28 on turf
runners.spotlight: Led close home to score at Wolverhampton just before Christmas but the handicapper has been winning the argument since; a 0-28 turf record is enough reason to look elsewhere.

runners.comment: Well held on AW reappearance and first-time cheekpieces need to make a difference
runners.spotlight: Hard to draw any obvious positives from her Southwell reappearance 16 days ago, taking her record to 1-18; first-time cheekpieces need to make a difference.

runners.comment: 5f maiden win last summer; well held on AW handicap debut in autumn but still early days
runners.spotlight: Turned over a 1-12 shot in Chepstow maiden (5f, good) last August; never involved in an AW handicap in the autumn but retains unexposed potential on return having had only five starts.

quotes.race: Dragonbet Born From The Betting Ring Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Scent Of May had an awful spring. She had to have her spine operated on, with bits of bone removed, as well as chips in her knees which we had to get removed. She's been through hell. But she's had lots of training in the swimming pool, and she's at last got herself fit - most importantly, she has her confidence back. I'm hoping she'll go up a lot from that. It's not often you hear a trainer say that - Henry Candy, trainer.

racecards.verdict: The speedy INITIAL BLUE could still be on a good mark back on turf.
racecards.betting_forecast: 9/4 Initial Blue, 7/2 Level Up, 5/1 Winchurch, 13/2 High Opinion, 9/1 Scent Of May, 10/1 Miss Brazen,  Papa Don't Preach, 14/1 Jeany May

racecards.race_name: Trot To Burger King Lady Bay Handicap

runners.comment: Close second on recent 1m Pontefract return; prominent showing likely if in same form
runners.spotlight: Winner over 1m2f at Beverley (good) last spring and went agonisingly close to a second career success on Pontefract reappearance (1m, good to soft) 11 days ago; a 2lb nudge shouldn't prevent another prominent showing if in similar form.

stable_tour.quote: He's a huge horse by Kameko. I thought he was clueless around Beverley last time - apparently there were slits in the grass and he kept looking at them - but he still won despite doing everything wrong. I think he outstayed them and I hope he'll improve as the season goes on. He has big feet and big thighs, so he's not a horse for firm ground. He's a junior model of Superposition and he's my trainer's pick. 30-04-25

runners.comment: Consistent in defeat on AW this year and should be thereabouts back on turf
runners.spotlight: Consistent in defeat on AW this year, reaching the frame for the sixth outing in succession when fourth of 13 at Southwell (1m) 11 days ago; turf winner last year; likely to be thereabouts.

quotes.race: PPM Barnsley Handicap
quotes.quote: My plan was always to take my time as we knew there was going to be a good gallop. Commander Of Life is a horse who has got a lot of ability but he has to come with one run and you really cannot get there until the furlong pole. He did it really nicely in the end - Finley Marsh, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

runners.comment: Third in two AW novices this winter but disappointing start to handicap career latest
runners.spotlight: Returned from a long absence to finish third in two AW novices this winter but made a disappointing start to his handicap career when 12l fifth at Chelmsford (1m) 37 days ago.

runners.comment: Promise last year and makes obvious appeal as an unexposed sort from a leading stable
runners.spotlight: All three starts over 1m, showing promise on the first of two turf runs; no match for a smart prospect when second of three on Newcastle's Tapeta when last seen in October but showed enough to confirm he possesses a fairly useful level of ability; has obvious unexposed potential now handicapping on his return (has been gelded).

runners.comment: Below par on AW recently but not discounted back at scene of win last year; cheekpieces on
runners.spotlight: Came good at the fourth time of asking for current connections over C&D (good) last autumn; a little below that level on AW in recent weeks but may fare better back on turf; first-time cheekpieces are fitted after hanging left last time.

runners.comment: Promise in novice events and unexposed now handicapping
runners.spotlight: Second on good turf for James Tate last autumn and has bettered that form when reaching the frame in AW novices over 1m and 7f for new yard; unexposed handicap newcomer.

runners.comment: Fair form in three qualifying runs last autumn; one to note in betting on handicap debut
runners.spotlight: Showed a fair level of ability in three qualifying runs over 6f/7f last autumn; hasn't obviously shaped as if crying out for this step up in trip but still needs monitoring in the betting on this handicap debut and reappearance.

runners.comment: C&D win last May; led for long way when fifth on AW return and could be spot on now
runners.spotlight: C&D winner on good last spring and added to tally when easily making all at Musselburgh (7f, good) last August; unplaced in four runs since but led for a long way when fifth on 7f Wolverhampton reappearance 18 days ago and could be spot on now.

stable_tour.quote: I was worried about his high draw at Musselburgh last week but it probably helped him as he doesn't like being crowded and he could sit wide on his own. He put in a career-best to win by quite a distance. The handicapper is going to have a say, but he did run through the line hard and he's open to a little bit of progress. That win was over 7f and a mile will suit him better, so he'd have half a chance of defying a rise. 04-09-25

runners.comment: Remains on a good mark after Wolverhampton win but does most of winning on AW
runners.spotlight: Back to form a little out of the blue when awarded a handicap over the extended 1m at Wolverhampton four weeks ago; retains plenty of handicapping scope on peak form but has done the majority of his winning on AW.

racecards.verdict: Kokanee is respected on the back of his solid reappearance but Roger Varian's handicap newcomer INFLUENTIAL is preferred.
racecards.betting_forecast: 3/1 Influential, 4/1 Kokanee, 11/2 Commander Of Life, 6/1 Eagle Day, 15/2 Pulsar Star, 9/1 Pension Pot, 10/1 Moonjid, 11/1 Highland Olly, 16/1 Oceans Five

racecards.race_name: £9 Racedays At Nottingham Racecourse Handicap

runners.comment: Made it 4-7 since cheekpieces went on when seeing off ten rivals at Bath recently; player
runners.spotlight: Made it 4-7 since cheekpieces went on when seeing off ten rivals back on turf at Bath (1m, good) 13 days ago; a 3lb rise shouldn't prevent another prominent showing in his current mood.

quotes.race: Make The Move To Midnite Handicap
quotes.quote: Law Supreme was always doing enough. Since he stepped up to a mile and a quarter he seems to find it that bit easier and Ian's horses are in great nick - Billy Loughnane, jockey.

runners.breeder: His Highness The Aga Khan's Studs S C

prev_owners.owner: Exors Of The Late H H Aga Khan

runners.comment: A new recruit for Declan Carroll; the betting should help guide to expectations
runners.spotlight: 0-5 in maidens at up to 1m4f in Ireland for Dermot Weld; sold for 16,000euros in November; remains unexposed but the betting is perhaps the best guide to expectations on handicap and yard debut after seven months off; drawn widest.

runners.breeder: C R Withers & Mr & Mrs R Reed

prev_owners.owner: N Bromley, S Spampanato, R And E J Reed

runners.comment: AW win in January; this course scorer should figure if fully primed for first run since
runners.spotlight: Back to winning ways on Lingfield's AW (1m2f) in January; his four successes prior to that all came on turf (including 1m here) so he should remain competitive off only 2lb higher if fully primed after three months off.

quotes.race: Download The Vickers.Bet App Handicap (Div I)
quotes.quote: The weather could have been better and we were worried about the easy ground, but Dream Pirate handled it well - Nick Bromley, owner.

runners.comment: Best effort back from long absence when fifth on AW latest; needs to build on that now
runners.spotlight: Useful form when winning AW novice for Roger Varian in August 2022; unlikely he retains close to that level of ability but latest Kempton fifth (beaten under 3l) was his best effort since returning from an absence and being eased another 2lb can only help now back on the grass.

runners.comment: Claims if he can translate good recent AW form to turf (well held both previous attempts)
runners.spotlight: Overcame major early setback to break through at 16th time of asking in apprentice race at Lingfield (1m2f) in February; backed that up when second of seven over 1m3f at Kempton last month; down the field on both previous turf starts but bit too soon to suggest he won't prove as good on the grass.

quotes.race: Make The Move To Midnite Apprentice Handicap
quotes.quote: It was a bit of a mess at the start but Joseph got into a lovely rhythm and he quickened up nicely. I thought the eventual second was going to keep going but he hauled them back and kept on well. It was his first try over a mile and a quarter but he was well up for it there - Donagh Murphy, rider, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

runners.comment: Ended 2025 out of sorts but well treated if a break has revived
runners.spotlight: A bit below form on his final five starts last year but a revival can't be ruled out on return having dipped to 3lb below the mark he defied at Yarmouth (1m2f, good) last April.

runners.comment: Travelled well for a long way over 1m3f on AW latest; remains unexposed after six starts
runners.spotlight: Travelled with purpose close to the pace before fading late into fifth over 1m3f at Southwell 16 days ago; today's slightly shorter trip should help and retains potential after only six starts.

runners.comment: AW win in February; held twice since but was caught wide back on turf latest
runners.spotlight: Got his head back in front at Newcastle (1m2f) in February; down the field both starts since, although a wide trip didn't help back on turf at Doncaster three weeks ago; hasn't had much luck with the draw again.

quotes.race: Sky Sports Racing Sky 415 Handicap
quotes.quote: We're delighted with  Bearwith. He was down to a good mark and it was probably quite a winnable race, so we're just thrilled to get another win. I had every hope, especially as all the horses have been running so well recently - Harriet Bethell, trainer.

quotes.race: Tony Lythgoe Birthday Memorial Handicap
quotes.quote: Bearwith was very good today and had to be really brave. He was really gutsy, especially from the shabby draw that he had - Harriet Bethell, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's a great old horse. He's won for us every year since we've had him. This year he's been having a few wind issues and it's possibly made him a bit cute. But he's a great old stick and won again at Doncaster in June. He's probably better on the all-weather, as his mark reflects. 17-09-25

runners.comment: Capable off this mark but will need to break a lot better than he did at Thirsk last week
runners.spotlight: Dual 1m winner (good turf/AW); shaped quite well on AW first two starts this year but blotted his copybook when losing many lengths at the start back on turf at Thirsk last week; more than capable off this mark but not one for maximum faith after that.

runners.comment: This is easier than race he ran in last time and he won off this mark on AW last month
runners.spotlight: Got his head back in front off this mark on AW at Newcastle (1m2f) last month; not beaten far back there next time and this is a bit easier than the Class 4 he contested at Wolverhampton latest.

runners.comment: May strip fitter for return but weakened on previous attempt at 1m2f; cheekpieces go on
runners.spotlight: Weakened into sixth behind Law Supreme at Bath (1m, good) 13 days ago but he's entitled to come on for that first outing in six months; cheekpieces are added now; remains unexposed after five starts but stamina seemed stretched on previous attempt at 1m2f.

runners.owner: Dr M Voikhansky & Mrs S Voikhanskaya
runners.comment: Went close off 2lb higher here last summer; claims if ready to roll after 196 days off
runners.spotlight: Might have been a shade unlucky when close second over 1m here last August and he was a respectable third over 1m2f at Redcar (good to soft) when last seen in the autumn; should be competitive if ready to roll after 196 days off

runners.comment: Should be sharper for reappearance and feasibly treated if back close to his best
runners.spotlight: In good form with a pair of 1m2f fast-ground wins last summer; ought to be sharper for Doncaster reappearance 13 days ago and on a workable mark if back close to his best.

quotes.race: HEB Cleaning And Hygiene Amateur Jockeys' Handicap
quotes.quote: I'm really glad we got there, it would have been annoying after bumping off the rail. Star Start has got a tendency to go off quick and, being drawn wide, had I tried to make the running, I'd have done too much too soon. I had to sit and suffer, and it's paid off lovely - Charli Parker, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

stable_tour.quote: I bought him for the amateur of our yard, Charli Parker, and he's done well, winning twice last season and being placed twice. He seems to need a few races before he comes to his best, but I don't see any reason why he won't come good again this year. 15-04-26

runners.comment: Three 1m2f wins last August but never involved on Doncaster return three weeks ago
runners.spotlight: Reeled off a fast-ground hat-trick over this trip last August; also runner-up off 2lb higher at Redcar (1m2f, good to soft) in the autumn but never involved on Doncaster return three weeks ago.

quotes.race: William Hill Betting Done Properly Handicap
quotes.quote: We were unsure as Bay Dream Believer had a 5lb penalty and was only put up 2lb for her last win so it was a bit of a gamble but the prize money was good for the grade and she came out of the race really well. She's only a little pony but she tries hard - trainer Mark Walford.

stable_tour.quote: She's a very small mare but has one of the biggest hearts in training. We expect her to win again this summer - she's been fourth in her last two runs at Nottingham and Pontefract and is knocking on the door. She ran again at Pontefract on Monday, where the draw and a slow start made life very tricky for her. However, she finished powerfully to finish fourth behind Lord Warburton which was a great effort! 14-06-24

runners.comment: Did well to get up on AW reappearance, his first attempt at 1m2f; could be on good mark
runners.spotlight: Improved effort back from five months off when opening his account in a 1m2f Newcastle classified event 37 days ago, his first attempt at this trip; did quite well to get up late on having had to wait for a run and could be on a good mark back in a handicap.

racecards.verdict: Mark Walford's WICKLOW WAY (nap) is unexposed at 1m2f and could be on a good mark having overcome trouble to win on AW last month.
racecards.betting_forecast: 100/30 Law Supreme, 11/2 Wicklow Way, 13/2 Dream Pirate, 9/1 Joseph, 10/1 Wood Whisperer, 11/1 In The Post, 12/1 Boubyan, 14/1 Kasgani,  Bearwith,  Volto Di Medusa, 16/1 Caph Star,  Onslow Gardens, 20/1 Show Biz Kid, 22/1 Star Start, 25/1 Bay Dream Believer

racecards.race_name: Ladies Day 9th May Handicap (Div I)

runners.comment: Flopped in his bid for a Southwell hat-trick last month and he's just 1-17 on turf
runners.spotlight: Returned to form when winning two classified events at Southwell (1m) last month but he flopped in his hat-trick bid there (handicap) last time; has bit to prove again after that heavy defeat and he's 1-17 on turf.

runners.comment: Back on track with creditable efforts at Wolverhampton last month and he's in the mix
runners.spotlight: 6yo who turned things around with two creditable efforts at Wolverhampton (8.6f) last month; his last two wins have been at that track but he remains well treated on his old turf form; could be dangerous back in this sphere but he probably wouldn't want any rain.

runners.comment: Well below form on AW in last two starts and sole turf win was almost three years ago
runners.spotlight: Won two classified events on AW in January but he's been well below form in handicaps in his last two runs; this trip is no problem but his sole turf win was almost three years ago and others are preferred.

runners.comment: Unexposed 4yo but she needs a transformation at this new trip
runners.spotlight: Has worn a hood in all four starts; finished down the field at big prices in her qualifying runs and was a remote last of nine on handicap debut at Wolverhampton (7f, AW) last month; still early days but she needs a transformation at this new trip.

runners.comment: Nine-time winner who is well treated on his second in this race last year; interesting
runners.spotlight: Nine-time winner, with seven on Tapeta and two on turf; finished last of eight after a slow start on Southwell reappearance (1m) last month, but he's well handicapped on his best form last year including when runner-up in this race; needs a close look back in this sphere and he won't mind what the weather does.

quotes.race: Spreadex Sports Injury Time Loser Insurance Handicap (Div II)
quotes.quote: Back From Dubai broke well and I just let him use his stride and he's toughed it out to the line - Jordan Williams, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

runners.comment: Well treated on his old form but it was a struggle last season; lots to prove on return
runners.spotlight: Three wins (7f-1m2f) in 2024 but it was a struggle last year and he was beaten 13l at Redcar in his final run in October; has tumbled down the weights but he needs to turn things around after 173 days off.

runners.comment: In good form on AW but he still has something to prove on turf and 7f is his best trip
runners.spotlight: Just one win from 27 starts but that came at Lingfield (7f) in January and he's finished a close third there in last two starts; remains feasibly treated off same mark as last time but he still has something to prove on turf and his best form has been at 7f.

runners.breeder: Hellwood Stud Farm & G P Clarke
runners.comment: On dangerous mark but she's 0-24 and comes with risks attached on her return
runners.spotlight: Inconsistent 24-race maiden; went close at a big price in a Redcar handicap (1m, good) in November but she ended last year with a tame effort at Wolverhampton; on dangerous mark but she has a modest record when fresh and others are more convincing.

runners.comment: Only one win since 2022 and he's struggled in his last five starts; opposable
runners.spotlight: Only one win since June 2022 and has beaten just two rivals in his last five starts (either side of wind surgery); mark has bottomed out now and he has a lot to prove; cheekpieces back on.

runners.comment: 11-race maiden and she needs a major revival on return for new trainer
runners.spotlight: 11-race maiden who was beaten 10l or more in her final three runs for Stuart Kittow last season; had wind surgery but she needs a major revival on return for new trainer.

racecards.verdict: It's hard to find a solid option but it might be worth siding with last year's runner-up BACK FROM DUBAI.
racecards.betting_forecast: 5/2 Sceptic, 9/2 Fifty Sent, 5/1 Back From Dubai,  Tilsworth Max, 7/1 Al Baahy, 12/1 Molly Marine, 14/1 Evelyn's Phoenix,  Penny Ghent, 20/1 Bizarre Law,  Freedom Bay

racecards.race_name: Ladies Day 9th May Handicap (Div II)

runners.comment: Well treated on his old form and he needs watching in market after six months off
runners.spotlight: His last two wins were over 7f in 2024 but he's well treated on his old form and he ran well on a few occasions at up to 1m2f last season; seems to handle most ground and he needs watching in market after six months off; cheekpieces removed.

runners.comment: 0-7 but he ended last season with two placed efforts in handicaps; interesting on return
runners.spotlight: Seven-race maiden but he ended last season with placed efforts in 1m2f handicaps at Pontefract and Redcar (both on good to soft); tongue-tie is removed on this drop back in trip but he's on same mark as last time and that was a personal best; interesting contender on his return.

runners.comment: Nine-race maiden who finished down the field in final three runs last year; down the list
runners.spotlight: Creditable third in a Leicester handicap (7f, good to soft) in September but she's not gone on from that and was laboured at Chelmsford in her final run last year; record is now 0-9 and she needs a major revival after a break; hood reapplied.

runners.comment: Won a classified event at Wolverhampton (8.6f) last month; unexposed on turf
runners.spotlight: Not the easiest and plenty of short-priced defeats to his name but he won at Wolverhampton (8.6f) last month and was a creditable third in another classified event at Lingfield (1m2f) three weeks ago; remains unexposed on turf and he needs a close look back in this sphere.

quotes.race: Free Bets With BetUK Bet Club Classified Stakes (Div I)
quotes.quote: It's Desiderata's first run for us. We worked him up in Lambourn in the week and he went very well with a 60-rated horse so we expected him to run a nice race - Thomas Faulkner, trainer, talking to Sky Sports Racing.

runners.comment: Well held in last four runs but his last win was off this mark; needs checking in market
runners.spotlight: Well held in his last four starts but he may have needed the run at Bath two weeks ago and he's now back on the same mark as when completing a double at Brighton (1m, soft) in September; has claims if he can recapture that form and any rain would be a bonus.

quotes.race: Blackmore Building Contractors Apprentice Handicap
quotes.quote: James Park Woods is a big legend at Highview [Stables] and, after his win on Saturday, he's backed it up really well. It was definitely some of the windiest conditions I've raced in, but he handled it really well and toughed it out, so I'm very happy - Isobelle Chalmers, rider, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

runners.comment: On reduced mark and could be dangerous if this sets up for his closing style
runners.spotlight: Sole win was in Ireland in 2024 but he's on a reduced mark and has shown some encouraging signs at Wolverhampton (8.6f/9.4f) this spring; usually comes from off the pace and could be dangerous if he gets the breaks.

quotes.race: BoyleSports Lengthen The Odds Handicap (Div II)
quotes.quote: Mooretown Lad is a work in progress. He is a brother to I Am Superman but he is a slow learner and more like his half-brother Fastnet Crown. He has taken time and he will be a better horse next year - Michael O'Callaghan, trainer.

runners.comment: On long losing run and he needs a big turnaround back on the Flat
runners.spotlight: Two soft-ground wins (7.4f/1m) in 2024 but he's drawn a blank since and has been well held on the Flat and over hurdles in his last three starts; bit to prove and he needs a big turnaround back in this sphere; cheekpieces reapplied.

runners.owner: Dr M Voikhansky & Mrs S Voikhanskaya
runners.comment: Record of 1-21 and was down the field on her reappearance last spring; headgear on
runners.spotlight: Returned to form with a good fourth at Lingfield (1m, AW) in September but she was back in the doldrums in her final run last season; record is now 1-21 and she finished down the field on her reappearance last spring; cheekpieces added.

runners.comment: Overall record of 1-24 and he's been below form in his last seven runs; others preferred
runners.spotlight: Won at Brighton (1m, good to firm) for Alice Haynes last June but he's been below form in last seven runs including on stable debut at Southwell last month; overall record is now 1-24 and others are more convincing; cheekpieces reapplied.

runners.comment: Three wins in 2024 but he's been well held in last ten starts; needs to raise his game
runners.spotlight: Three wins (1m) in 2024 but he's been well held in last ten starts including when fourth behind Desiderata at Wolverhampton (8.6f, AW) last month; that wasn't bad but he needs to raise his game back in a handicap.

racecards.verdict: Preference is for RAYSHAM who ended last season with two placed efforts and still has potential after only seven starts.
racecards.betting_forecast: 3/1 Charencey, 100/30 Raysham, 4/1 Desiderata, 7/1 Clipsham Noble, 15/2 Mooretown Lad, 10/1 James Park Woods, 12/1 Love You More, 16/1 Law Degree, 20/1 Haaf A Diamond,  United Force

racecards.race_name: British EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)

runners.comment: 125,000gns yearling; out of multiple winner at 5f-7f on AW; yard won last 2 runnings
runners.spotlight: March foal; 125,000gns yearling by Blue Point; fourth foal; sister to 7f AW 2yo winner Blue Seeker (RPR 68), half-sister to 1m4f winner Dubai Venture (60); dam won six AW races at 5f-7f (including 2yo; 100); likely type for yard that has already had a winning juvenile in 2026 and has won the last two runnings of this.

runners.comment: Good sprinting connections; yard's first 2yo runner; has possibilities
runners.spotlight: February foal; £46,000 yearling; first foal; by Havana Grey; dam placed at 5f/7f on AW as 2yo (RPR 70), winning siblings include Good Vibes (5f 2yo Group 3; 104) and Easy Peeler (6f; 90) who ran well on debut for these connections; yard's first 2yo runner in 2026; possibilities.

runners.comment: No sign as yet that the yard's juveniles are forward; others look more likely this time
runners.spotlight: February foal; third foal; by Oasis Dream out of 1m/1m1f winner (RPR 69), half-sister to 5.7f/7f winner Bussento (Britain and Bahrain); no sign as yet that the yard's juveniles are forward.

runners.comment: 17,000gns yearling; dam bred winning sprinters; yard had winning newcomer here last week
runners.spotlight: January foal; 17,000gns yearling; by Dream Ahead; half-sister to winners Rocket Money (5f/6f including 2yo/KSA; RPR 78) and Doze (Italian 6f-8.5f including 2yo/AW); dam 7f AW 2yo winner (70); yard produced a useful winning newcomer over C&D last Friday (favourite); check the market.

runners.comment: April foal; dam 5f-winning half-sister to smart sprinter Liberty Beach; market can guide
runners.spotlight: April foal; £40,000 yearling; second foal; by Cotai Glory out of 5f winner (including 2yo; RPR 80), half-sister to 5f Group 2 winner Liberty Beach (also Group 3 winner as 2yo; 110); yard had first 2yo runner of the year finish third at Bath yesterday; market can guide.

runners.comment: £120,000 yearling; has possibilities on pedigree; yard also runs Moonlight Tango
runners.spotlight: February foal; £120,000 yearling; third foal; Zoustar half-sister to 5f 2yo winner Kamakameleon (RPR 87); dam Group-placed 7f 2yo winner (99), half-sister to French 7f 2yo Group 3 winner Moon Ray; of some interest on debut; yard also runs Moonlight Tango.

racecards.verdict: Karl Burke, already off the mark with 2yos, has won the last two runnings and he may be able to provide the answer with BAI TONG.
racecards.betting_forecast: Evs Bai Tong, 7/2 Silesia, 9/2 Niewiadoma, 13/2 Moonlight Tango, 9/1 Havana Gift, 33/1 Lake Muritz

racecards.race_name: Thomas Lord Dine & View Restaurant Great Value Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)

runners.comment: 2m4f hurdle winner; hard to fancy on Flat until tackling handicaps over longer trips
runners.spotlight: 2m4f hurdle winner; well held (7f/1m) on Flat and hard to fancy until tackling handicaps over longer distances.

quotes.race: Tynedale Function Suite Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race) (Div I)
quotes.quote: Pop The Question has not had her ground throughout the whole point-to-point season, so finally it's stopped raining and she's got it and she was able to show her true colours. No, it wasn't really [a surprise]. We always knew that if she got her ground she'd run well. I think this is her trip. She'll probably stay a little bit further, but I don't think she's a true out-and-out three-mile-plus horse - Jacqueline Coward, trainer.

runners.comment: Poor form in two runs last year for Kevin Ryan; needs this run for a handicap mark
runners.spotlight: Poor form in two runs last year for Kevin Ryan; changed hands for 11,000gns in the autumn and gelded; needs this run for a handicap mark and probably best watched unless strong in the market.

runners.comment: Consistent as 2yo; likely to be in the thick of things after his winter break
runners.spotlight: 0-7 last year but quite consistent, close fifth at York (7f, good) on final start; subsequently gelded; far more solid than most of these and likely to be in the thick of things after his winter break.

runners.comment: £80,000 breeze-up purchase last year; worth a market check on debut
runners.spotlight: £80,000 2yo (breeze-ups); by Space Blues; dam placed 7f AW (RPR 74), half-sister to Listed winners Hawke (10.6f) and Mireille (7f); worth a market check on debut.

runners.owner: Clova Farms And P D Niven
runners.comment: Newcomer by Territories; may not come into his own until getting more of a test of stamina
runners.spotlight: 3,000gns 2yo; by Territories; closely related to French winners Perfect Stranger (7.5f AW; RPR 87) and Palmares (1m5f); dam French 1m 2yo winner (94); may not come into his own until getting more of a test of stamina.

runners.comment: Signs of ability in three runs as 2yo but a couple of these have much stronger form
runners.spotlight: Signs of ability in three runs as 2yo, fading into fourth of ten at Catterick (7f, good) on final one; may have more still to offer but a couple of these have much stronger form.

runners.comment: Worth monitoring in the betting, although yard isn't known for first-time out winners
runners.spotlight: 13,000gns yearling; Dream Ahead half-brother to winners Ayr Harbour (7f/1m AW; RPR 105), Desert Lion (1m-1m2f; 104) and Navajo Scout (Italian 11.5f); dam 7f and 7.5f (Italian Listed) 2yo winner (103); worth monitoring in the betting, although yard isn't known for first-time out winners.

runners.comment: Some late headway when fifth at Catterick ten days ago; should improve but needs to
runners.spotlight: Gelded son of Lope De Vega; weak in the market and slowly away when over 10l fifth of 11 at Catterick (7f, good; 40-1) ten days ago; made some late headway and should improve, but he needs to.

runners.comment: Only seventh in two runs last year but has been gelded and still has potential
runners.spotlight: 82,000gns yearling; only seventh of nine on both outings last term, folding tamely after racing freely on second of them; lots of improvement required but he has since been gelded and still has potential.

runners.comment: Went backwards from debut at Newcastle last time; may be of more interest in handicaps
runners.spotlight: Made a low-key start at a big price on debut at Newcastle (1m, AW), and went backwards over the same C&D next time; may be of more interest in handicaps.

runners.owner: Exors Of The Late Sheikh Mohammed Obaid
runners.comment: Second at Redcar (to smart prospect) and Newcastle (behind wide-margin winner); big shout
runners.spotlight: 500,000gns yearling; runner-up to a smart prospect at Redcar (7f, good to soft) last autumn; faded after leading until over 1f out when second to a wide-margin winner at Newcastle (7f, AW) on reappearance; still has untapped potential; leading candidate.

runners.comment: Off 11 months between debut and reappearance; has plenty to find on the figures
runners.spotlight: Off 11 months between debut and reappearance; possibly failed to stay 1m on return and this shorter trip should help but he has plenty to find on the figures.

runners.comment: No threat on debut but he was an expensive yearling and he's in good hands
runners.spotlight: Slowly away and never the slightest threat at Newmarket (7f, good; 33-1) on sole outing last term; needs a big leap forward but he was an expensive (420,000gns) yearling and he's in good hands so it's possible.

runners.breeder: His Highness The Aga Khan's Studs S C

prev_owners.owner: Exors Of The Late H H Aga Khan

runners.comment: Improved when second in nursery on last of four starts in Ireland; still low mileage
runners.spotlight: Some promise on first three 2yo starts and he improved when second in nursery at Fairyhouse (6f, yielding; blinkered) in September; subsequently changed hands for 25,000euros and gelded; still low mileage and may progress further for new stable.

prev_owners.owner: The Vital Sparks & David D Smith

runners.comment: Comes from a family that has served Jim Goldie well, but minimal promise last term
runners.spotlight: Comes from a family that has served Jim Goldie very well, but minimal promise in two runs last term and probably best watched until handicapping; wears a hood for the first time.

runners.comment: Finished two places and 3l behind Forest Phoenix on debut at Catterick ten days ago
runners.spotlight: Finished two places and 3l behind Forest Phoenix on debut at Catterick (28-1) ten days ago; should improve but others still make more appeal.

racecards.verdict: Advance Twentyfive sets the standard but INISHBEG gives the impression there's still a fair bit of improvement to come.
racecards.betting_forecast: 13/8 Inishbeg, 5/2 Advance Twentyfive, 11/2 Weffaag, 10/1 Zarvali, 14/1 Forest Phoenix, 16/1 Deep Sleep,  Simba's Pride, 20/1 Blue Boy Junior,  Fozzie, 25/1 Talking In Kode, 33/1 Dream Odyssey,  Haltonwood, 40/1 Clova Royale, 50/1 Act Of Honor, 66/1 Saxon Gem, 100/1 Pop The Question

racecards.race_name: Nick Simpson Cannot Be 60 Handicap

runners.comment: Three wins as a 2yo but drawn a blank since; needs to step up on last month's stable debut
runners.spotlight: Won three times as a 2yo for Richard Fahey; ran well for a close third at Newcastle on his final run for that stable last October (6f; visored); low-key stable debut at Doncaster three weeks ago; visor absent once again.

runners.comment: Improving run by run, getting off mark in small-field novice (6f) in February; unexposed
runners.spotlight: He has improved with each of his four starts, getting off the mark in good style at Wolverhampton ten weeks ago (6f); while that isn't the most solid piece of form, he isn't being overfaced for his handicap debut and remains capable of further progress.

runners.comment: Prolific winner but she needs to leave her recent reappearance behind her; 0-7 at Thirsk
runners.spotlight: Prolific winner but her record at this track is 0-7; should be sharper with her recent C&D return behind her but she may need more weight off her back before she's adding to her 14 victories.

quotes.race: PricedUp Handicap (Jockey Club Grassroots Sprint Series Qualifier)
quotes.quote: I wish every horse I had was as game as Hurt You Never. When she hits form, she's very consistent. There aren't many horses who win one or two races, let alone 13. She's a credit to herself and I wouldn't mind a yard full like her - Adrian Nicholls, trainer.

quotes.race: BetUK. It's Where The UK Bets Handicap
quotes.quote: She's a really game mare. I thought Hurt You Never might need the run but she showed she's in great form. Early on I thought I'd gone a bit quick but she just kept powering through - Mia Nicholls, jockey, talking to Sky Sports Racing.

stable_tour.quote: She's been a superstar for us. She hasn't stopped winning and she's honest and tough. The soft ground wasn't ideal for her at Doncaster last week, but she was 4lb well in, so we gave it a go and she ran well to finish fourth behind Jojo Rabbit. She's easy to train and ride. She's won ten times and there'll come a point where the handicapper will have a say, but she'll be winning again. 26-07-24

runners.comment: 5f AW win in January; not so good six days later but can bounce back after a break
runners.spotlight: Ran on well to win a 5f handicap at Newcastle in January; not quite so good back there six days later but he is feasibly weighted and 6f on good ground no problem; stable operating at a fine strike-rate in 2026.

quotes.race: Lancashire DAF Handicap (Div II)
quotes.quote: Pal Joey is still a bit immature and inexperienced, but he really had to knuckle down at the end. He shouldn't be overly bothered by the handicapper and I thought out of the field he ought to improve the most. This track suited him, but he'll be a nice horse for the autumn as he likes to get his toe in a little bit. That's as quick as he'd want it - Ben Haslam, trainer.

runners.comment: Disappointing at Doncaster on his return to turf; should be well treated but not solid
runners.spotlight: Disappointing at Doncaster on his return to turf last month (5f, good to soft); in good form on AW beforehand and this mark should be well within his range; not sure what to expect.

runners.comment: Fine 2nd over C&D on last week's return to action; 1lb higher but still looks a key player
runners.spotlight: Both his wins have come on soft ground but he ran a cracker on good ground over C&D last week (cheekpieces first time), keeping on well behind an in-form sprinter; 1lb higher today but still a strong contender, especially with some rain in the forecast.

runners.comment: Solid 4th at Doncaster and then poorly drawn last time; claims enhanced if rain arrives
runners.spotlight: Solid effort back from a break when fourth of 17 at Doncaster last month (5f, good to soft); not well drawn at Musselburgh on Sunday and ran okay in the circumstances; chance would be enhanced by significant rain.

quotes.race: Sam Hall Memorial Handicap
quotes.quote: In the middle of the summer Impressor had a couple of near misses, he nudged up a couple of pounds and then had a couple of poor efforts. We thought maybe his chance was gone, but he does like the ground and still seems quite well in himself - Phillip Makin, trainer, speaking to Racing TV.

quotes.race: Jaimie Kerr Memorial Handicap
quotes.quote: Impressor is an in-form horse at the moment and Phil's horses are flying. This lad loves the ground. Before when he used to get caught on a wing like that he wouldn't really battle hard for you but he's turned a corner and he dug deep when needed - Shane Gray, jockey, speaking on Racing TV.

quotes.race: British EBF Molson Coors Novice Stakes (Plus 10 Race) (Div II)
quotes.quote: Impressor has got loads of speed and I wouldn't be rushing to go over seven furlongs with him. He's in the Mill Reef at Newbury and that's a likely type of race to run him in - Marcus Tregoning, trainer.

runners.comment: Two-time C&D winner; on a good mark and latest Newcastle fourth wasn't without hope
runners.spotlight: Two of his four wins have come over C&D; signs he was ready to exploit his reduced mark when fourth of nine at Newcastle three weeks ago; not discounted.

quotes.race: Rudding Park Handicap
quotes.quote: I thought Kings Merchant would have been an unlucky loser. He usually does just enough to win and I told Callum not to get to the front too soon, but he's given him a great ride, he was incredibly patient. He travelled all over them and is a really progressive horse. He's only been out of the first three once this year, which is brilliant. He's great fun - Ed Bethell, trainer.

quotes.race: Sky Bet Go-Racing-In-Yorkshire Summer Festival Handicap
quotes.quote: King's Merchant is a progressive sprinter. They were two in-form horses behind him and it was a good run. He loves top-of-the-ground, which is why he hadn't run for a month, and six furlongs is his bag - Ed Bethell, trainer.

prev_owners.owner: Capla Development, J Nordoff, L Westwood

runners.comment: This mark not beyond him and he has run well fresh after a break; betting useful
runners.spotlight: Getting on for two years since his last win; on a handy mark if ready to roll after 172 days off and he has run well fresh in the past.

quotes.race: tote.co.uk Saddle-Up For More Than Racing Handicap
quotes.quote: We didn't give Joanna any instructions, we just wanted to see what the drop back was going to do and it seems to have worked. It's Epsom next next, that's the plan - the three-year-old only Dash, because it's easier to win! - David Easterby, joint-trainer of Knicks.

runners.owner: Mrs K S Pratt & M Dods

prev_owners.owner: Mrs K S Pratt, P R Blackett, M Dods

runners.comment: Three-time C&D winner; good C&D run eight days ago but work to do with Stirrup Cup
runners.spotlight: His three turf wins have come over C&D and he made a pleasing seasonal return when fifth of 15 here (Stirrup Cup second) eight days ago; one for the shortlist.

runners.comment: 0-9 but he hasn't been with Jim Goldie for long; return to turf and 6f could both help
runners.spotlight: 0-9 but he hasn't been with Jim Goldie for long and getting back on turf should help; drop back to 6f another possible source of improvement.

runners.comment: Latest fifth wasn't without hope but he is back up in class today
runners.spotlight: Dropping down the weights and his latest Pontefract fifth was marginally more encouraging; more required back up in class though.

runners.comment: Prolific winner but not found his best so far in 2026; others appeal more for win purposes
runners.spotlight: The winner of 13 races, but just three of them have been on turf; yet to shine this year and he was behind a few of today's rivals over C&D last week.

stable_tour.quote: He's a decent all-weather horse and has won at Newcastle and Southwell this month and been second twice. He may switch back to turf but dry ground is quite important to him. When he's right he tries very hard and he's the sort who's important to the yard because he can win two or three a year and if every horse did that you'd have an awful lot of winners. He's entered at Newcastle on Friday. 20-03-24

runners.comment: On a good mark on last summer's best; returns from six months off; betting to guide
runners.spotlight: On a good mark on last summer's best; she is returning from six months off and she has been unplaced on her reappearance in the last two seasons.

quotes.race: Start Your Racing TV Free Trial Handicap (Div II)
quotes.quote: Taygar is tricky. She goes down early but she goes when she wants to go! She's not easy at all but she's got ability and she's just been waiting for some soft ground. Things didn't really go to plan but once Danny [Tudhope] got out she dropped her head a bit and settled well but, because of that, he had to send her on earlier than he would have liked. To be fair to her, she kept going and she's done it well - Michael Dods, trainer, speaking to Racing TV.

stable_tour.quote: I haven't done too much with my 2yos but this filly actually won first time out for us back in April. I don't usually have many youngsters out at that time of the year but she was showing a lot of speed and won well. Her next run at Pontefract was a different story as she was too keen and gave herself no chance, while at Redcar last time out she encountered good to firm ground for the first time and although she ran well, I felt she would appreciate a little more cut. We will look to upping her in trip to 6f next and find some slower ground. 26-07-23

runners.comment: Enjoyed ground-saving ride when 2nd at Pontefract on her return 11 days ago; respected
runners.spotlight: Best known for her Hamilton exploits but she is effective elsewhere and she ran well on her seasonal return 11 days ago (5f, good to soft; ground-saving ride against the rail), keeping on from well back to take second (apprentice jockey's first ride under rules); no surprise to see her in the shake up.

quotes.race: Usave Business Energy Specialist Fillies' Handicap
quotes.quote: Iris Dancer goes halfway through the race then jacks in a little then she warms back up and you always know you'll get a run out of her in the end. She really enjoys that stiff finish, she gets into top flight just at the line. It'd be nice to find another race before the end of the year and see what we can do - Andrew Mullen, jockey, speaking on Racing TV.

quotes.race: Usave Business Energy Specialist Fillies' Handicap
quotes.quote: I think the blinkers just made the difference for Iris Dancer. She's a game horse and always tries her best, and she'll be even better with softer ground - Tristran Davidson, trainer.

runners.owner: James Paul Services To Industry Ltd
runners.comment: Should be well handicapped but he has been disappointing so far this year
runners.spotlight: 8lb lower than for his Newcastle third in December (6f) but that hasn't been a springboard to better things; hopes rest on the return to turf perking him up.

quotes.race: Download The Vickers.Bet App EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Brave Empire improved a lot from his debut and was tough on his second start, he really battled hard,  but he showed a lot of quality today. To win with 9st 11lb on his back showed a lot of class. Not a lot of horses can carry a penalty and win with a performance like that. He quickened initially to get away from the pack and I felt he quickened again from the furlong pole- David Egan, jockey.

runners.comment: Infrequent winner but unexposed as a sprinter and holds each-way claims
runners.spotlight: Just one win from 22 starts but he is unexposed as a sprinter; apprentice takes off a handy 3lb and he holds each-way claims.

runners.comment: Two 5f wins for former trainer; cheekpieces return for stable debut
runners.spotlight: Raced exclusively at 5f, winning twice for Brian Ellison; starts out for his new stable off a dangerous mark and the return of cheekpieces can help; stable in the winners on Thursday; betting useful.

racecards.verdict: Perhaps not so competitive as the numbers suggest. STIRRUP CUP ran well over C&D eight days ago and could be the answer.
racecards.betting_forecast: 11/2 Stirrup Cup, 7/1 Kings Merchant, 8/1 Mr Dreamseller,  Iris Dancer, 10/1 Lord Abama,  Sherlock, 12/1 Pal Joey,  Ay Gee Ell,  Knicks, 14/1 Yes I'm Mali, 16/1 Taygar,  Impressor,  Hurt You Never,  Solar Biricz, 20/1 Ashen,  One More Dream,  Brave Empire, 33/1 Monotone

racecards.race_name: Join Racing TV Today Handicap (Div I)

runners.comment: Has gone well fresh & her C&D 3rd last September suggests she is still well handicapped
runners.spotlight: Ran well in the face of a stiff task in a Carlisle Listed event last summer; confirmed she hadn't been flattered there when finishing a fine third over C&D last September; two lesser efforts to round off 2025 but the form of that C&D run, where she travelled so powerfully, offers serious hope this mark is in range; has run well after a break in the past and her trainer is having a fine year; contender.

runners.comment: Talented but has a few ideas of his own; can go well fresh; each-way claims down in class
runners.spotlight: Regularly flattered to deceive for Andrew Balding; managed to put his head in front in a 7f Newmarket handicap last July (7f, good to firm) and today's 2lb higher mark not beyond him; he is the type that needs everything to fall right though and others appeal more for win purposes, for all this drop into Class 4 company will be of benefit.

stable_tour.quote: New to us from Andrew Balding's, we bought him as a maiden and haven't run him, but he's still won a race since. It was a disqualification, so he's no longer a maiden. He's got ability but might have a soft temperament. 14-04-25

runners.comment: Ended 2025 on the up; returns on a career-high mark so will need to be cherry ripe
runners.spotlight: Ended 2025 in a rich vein of form, winning a Catterick handicap (7f, good) before a narrow defeat at Musselburgh (7f, soft) when last seen 164 days ago; another 2lb higher on his reappearance so he will need to be cherry ripe for this return to action.

runners.comment: Six wins last season; returns from nine months off but still relatively unexposed at 7f
runners.spotlight: Six wins in the first half of 2025, notably when seeing off 21 rivals at York last May; absent for nine months but Paul Mulrennan has been booked for his return (two wins and two seconds from five rides on him) and this should be run to suit.

quotes.race: BetMGM: It's Showtime Handicap
quotes.quote: You'd like to think Frankies Dream is open to a bit of improvement. They went hard up front but that suited him. He's still learning to race, he's very forward going, but today he's switched off and finished strong. I think he'd stay 6f but he'd have to switch off again and a fast-run 5f is ideal - Joey Haynes, jockey, talking to Sky Sports Racing.

stable_tour.quote: He won six races last year and rose from a mark of 50 to 83. He's had a good holiday and is ready to start again. We're going to try to step him up in trip this year and he'll start off over a mile. He's going to be great fun in those mile handicaps over the summer. He goes on any ground and the faster they go the better he'll run. He just needs to settle - it's in his head sometimes. He's not the easiest of conveyances but he's capable of doing some good. 04-03-26

runners.comment: In good form last September; returns from 170 days off with a tough enough mark to defy
runners.spotlight: Prominent racer who enjoyed a purple patch last September, winning back-to-back Carlisle handicaps and coming up just shy in his hat-trick bid at Beverley; returns from 170 days off on a tough enough mark and others make more appeal.

stable_tour.quote: He had an issue in the stalls in the Spring Mile but passed his stalls test last Monday, so we're just waiting for a bit of cut in the ground for him now. He's a really nice horse and I think a lot of him. I wouldn't be surprised if there was a big handicap in him. 23-04-25

runners.comment: C&D winner; ended 2025 with a good 2nd of 15 at Leicester; likely best watched on return
runners.spotlight: C&D winner; two wins in the second half of 2025 and he ended that campaign with a good second of 15 at Leicester in October; runs off the same mark but he could only manage a midfield finish in this race on his reappearance 12 months ago.

quotes.race: Cubby Group Handicap (A Jockey Club Grassroots Mile Series Qualifier)
quotes.quote: Count Palatine is relatively inexperienced by all accounts. He's probably a tad better with some ease in the ground, so that combined with the prospects of maybe some headgear, or something like that, to keep his mind on the job could help him improve. There was a little bit of pace early on, although I didn't feel like we were going mad, he really likes this quick ground - Sean Kirrane, jockey.

quotes.race: Patrick Hibbert-Foy Memorial Handicap
quotes.quote: I said to Connor [Beasley, jockey] that the last time Count Palatine ran we sat him handy and I didn't feel he enjoyed that so I said to just drop him in and ride him to finish. He liked the ground and did it well - Michael Dods, trainer, speaking on Racing TV.

runners.owner: K Mills, J Brown, S Barley

prev_owners.owner: R A Pegum, P A Henry & X F Pegum
R A Pegum And Paul Anthony Henry

runners.comment: Unexposed 4yo; fine start for new yard with big-field win at Doncaster last month; chance
runners.spotlight: Lightly-raced 4yo; attracted support and made a perfect start for new connections when seeing off 14 rivals at Doncaster three weeks ago (7f, good to soft); 5lb higher in a better race but there was a lot to like about the way he responded to pressure last time; can do better.

quotes.race: William Hill Epic Boosts Handicap (Div II)
quotes.quote: Melvin Udall is still fairly babyish. He loves conditions and he'll get a mile in time. He's got to grow up mentally but when starts figuring it out there should be a nice bit of improvement there - Rossa Ryan, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

runners.comment: Shaped nicely on last month's reappearance; on a dangerous mark if that run brings him on
runners.spotlight: He finished down the field in this race 12 months ago but he has had the benefit of a run this time around and a promising effort it was too, shuffled back at a crucial stage but keeping on close home (7f, good to soft); his record at York suggests one eye may be on next month's Dante meeting but he's more than capable off this mark.

stable_tour.quote: He loves a bit of juice in the ground and seven furlongs or an easy mile. I think he could improve again this year, Lope De Vegas tend to do that. 23-04-24

runners.comment: Absent 560 days but his new yard are flying along and he looked promising in 2024
runners.spotlight: Only raced four times for Charles Hills but he won a 7f novice on his debut and finished second in both handicaps in 2024; the form of the Newbury second worked out extremely well and this mark ought to be in range; a 560-day absence, during which time he has changed hands (30,000gns last July) and been gelded, is the obvious concern but he returns for a stable in red-hot form; hooded first time; betting informative.

stable_tour.quote: He's been plagued with some niggly issues and had sore shins last year, but he was impressive when he won his only start at Haydock in July. He's had another little setback this spring, so he might be a month from racing, but he's talented, will get further than seven furlongs and should handle easy ground. 17-04-24

runners.comment: Four 6f wins last year; should build on last month's reappearance; rain would be a boost
runners.spotlight: The winner of four of his eight starts last year (6f, good or slower); perhaps needed the run on his return to action at Newcastle last month, running respectably in the smaller stands' side group; the more rain to fall the better for him.

quotes.race: pricedup.bet Handicap
quotes.quote: I was happy to get a nice lead and there was a good pace to aim at. City Captain has got a bit of knee action and really appreciated the bit of dig in the ground. He won cosy and I think he could improve in time  - Danny Tudhope, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

stable_tour.quote: He's won three times this season and is very exciting. It's not his downfall, but he needs soft ground as he's quite a big three-year-old and not a particularly good mover. I don't want to run him on anything quicker than soft or good or soft. He came back and was a bit sore after the interference he got at Doncaster last week and won't go for the Ayr Gold Cup now, but he'll be out again before the end of the season. He'll be even better next year when he's grown into himself. 17-09-25

runners.comment: Winless in 2025 but retained plenty of ability; market useful after 170 days off
runners.spotlight: Failed to win in 2025 but he ran some solid races in defeat and he makes his seasonal return off a dangerous mark; interesting to see how he fares in the betting.

stable_tour.quote: He's a likeable sort of horse and is very straightforward. Formerly with Jack Channon, he ran well first time out for us at Newcastle and then won over 7f at Wolverhampton two weeks ago. There might be more to come from him and he's quite exciting. His form has been on the all-weather but he hasn't had many opportunities on turf. While the weather stays wet we'll probably stick on the all-weather for a bit but then go on the grass when we get a bit of decent ground. 17-04-24

A 7f specialist who won twice at Newbury last year, in July and August. He came from Jack Channon's in March last year and quickly settled in at Mowbray because he won at Wolverhampton after only a month here. He might go back to Newbury on Saturday. 09-04-25

runners.comment: Two good runs for new yard this spring (1m); drop to 7f should be fine; contender
runners.spotlight: Smart 2yo for Wiliam Haggas; won a Killarney handicap in July 2024 when trained by Willie Mullins; two good runs for new yard this spring, third at Newcastle and Pontefract (both 1m), and likely to be in the shake up.

runners.comment: C&D winner last September; only had seven runs so could still rate higher
runners.spotlight: Lost his action and weakened at Catterick when last seen 199 days ago; prior to that he had comfortably seen off nine rivals in a C&D handicap (soft) in September; only had seven starts and there should be more to come.

racecards.verdict: Melvin Udall is solid but BEAUJOLAIS NOUVEAU ran a fine race over C&D last September, a run that offered hope of a fair bit better.
racecards.betting_forecast: 4/1 Melvin Udall, 5/1 Leadman, 6/1 Alpha Capture, 7/1 City Captain, 10/1 Frankies Dream,  Murashah, 12/1 U Sure Do,  Quest For Fun, 14/1 Beaujolais Nouveau, 16/1 One Night Thunder,  Count Palatine,  Woodstock,  Draupnir

racecards.race_name: Join Racing TV Today Handicap (Div II)

runners.comment: Doesn't look to have much in hand of the assessor now starting out for Tim Easterby
runners.spotlight: Promising 2yo; needed a drop into selling company, albeit a hot seller, to get off the mark in 2025 (7.6f, soft); sold out of Andrew Balding's stable for 20,000gns last October; could probably do with a few pounds off his back; has worn cheekpieces in the past but goes without today.

quotes.race: Irish Thoroughbred Marketing Nursery Handicap
quotes.quote: I don't think everyone would've won on Brighton Boy and he wasn't concentrating on what he should've been on. He's a big horse and we'll get our heads together as he's got a pretty bright future ahead of him - Anna Lisa Balding, wife of trainer.

runners.comment: Placed in 3 of his 5 runs in 2025, including seasonal debut; returns in a competitive race
runners.spotlight: Ran well on his seasonal/stable debut last March; placed in 7f handicaps at Sandown and Kempton on final two runs in 2025; returns in a competitive event.

stable_tour.quote: This lovely son of Mehmas finished a very good second on his debut at Goodwood before winning a 7f novice at Newbury last month. He has some nice entries and the first one he's likely to take up is the Weatherbys Scientific £300,000 2-Y-O Stakes at Doncaster on September 14. 25-08-23

runners.comment: Good 3rd on seasonal debut last month (best of stands' side group); same mark here; chance
runners.spotlight: Won a pair of 7f handicaps at Catterick last October; returned from a 142-day absence with a fine third at Newcastle three weeks ago, doing best of the smaller stands' side group; runs off the same mark today and should make another bold bid.

quotes.race: Jill Willows Handicap
quotes.quote: I thought Mudamer would have won before now - he's very talented. I think the cheekpieces have helped him a lot because he hit the front at York and then just shut down. It's just made him focus. He's made hard work of it on what he does at home. I have a horse, Scottish Summit, rated 91 and this fella will kick him into touch without even coming off the bridle - Geoff Harker, trainer.
